item.title: ReFi Deep Dive: Flowcarbon
item.dc:creator: Phaedrus
item.content:encoded: <p>In the latest episode of the ReFi Podcast, your hosts John and Simar sit down with Dana and and Phil from <a href="https://www.flowcarbon.com/">Flowcarbon</a>, a highly-discussed and anticipated entry to the ReFi ecosystem of on-chain carbon.</p><p>Listen to the episode on <a href="https://pod.fo/e/149fb4">Podfollow</a>, <a href="https://anchor.fm/refipodcast/episodes/Scaling-Carbon-Markets-with-Dana-and-Phil-from-Flowcarbon-e1pmt15…">Anchor FM</a> or directly on <a href="https://youtu.be/g1W2YFeckJQ">YouTube</a>, and read on for more!</p><h1 id="tldr"><strong>TL;DR</strong></h1><p>Flowcarbon is a web3 startup aiming to accelerate the restoration of our planet’s environment and ecosystems by tokenizing nature-based carbon credits. The project plans to launch as a two-way bridge, on the Celo blockchain, allowing credits to be readily passed on- and off-chain.</p><p>Flowcarbon’s proposed token Goddess Nature Token (GNT), will focus on nature-based credits broadly falling under the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (<a href="https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar5/wg3/agriculture-forestry-and-other-land-use-afolu/">AFOLU</a>) umbrella. While the project recently delayed their intended June, 2022 launch due to market conditions, they are actively seeking partners to bridge tokens from a rolling 5-year vintage, compliant with relevant standards from Verra, Gold Standard, Climate Action Reserve or American Carbon Standard registries.</p><p>Former WeWork CEO Adam Neumann was revealed as a co-founder in May, 2022, bringing the venture both significant early stage funding as well as an outsized dose of skepticism in mainstream media coverage.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-embed-card"><iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/g1W2YFeckJQ?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen title="ReFi Podcast S2E13: Scaling Carbon Markets with Dana and Phil from Flowcarbon"></iframe></figure><h2 id="the-challenge"><strong>The Challenge</strong></h2><p>Climate change poses an existential threat to humanity. Anthropogenic greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions have risen rapidly over the past 150 years, and are driving global warming, alongside a whole suite of cascading, inter-connected ecological disruptions including biodiversity loss, ocean acidification, soil erosion, glacier and sea ice loss etc.</p><p>At the root of these crises, our historic and prevalent economic systems have and continue to incentivize the destruction of natural systems, and pollution of our atmosphere via greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. </p><p>In the absence of a radical transformation of our economic systems and collective priorities, putting a price on carbon, and properly valuing the services provided by nature, can serve to introduce our environment to our economy - where there has otherwise been an historic disconnect.</p><h2 id="flowcarbon%E2%80%99s-solution"><strong>Flowcarbon’s Solution</strong></h2><p>Recognizing the role natural solutions can play in solving the climate crisis, Flowcarbon is focused on accelerating adoption of nature-based carbon credits. Carbon credits are a mechanism by which projects that provably reduce GHG emissions or actively withdraw carbon from the atmosphere can become financially incentivized.</p><p>Flowcarbon proposes a two-way bridge to bring nature-based carbon credits on-chain to back their Goddess Nature Token (GNT) token. Given recent concerns by <a href="https://verra.org/verra-addresses-crypto-instruments-and-tokens/">Verra</a>, tied to their freezing of bridging activity, this additional fluidity of GNT should allow universal price discovery via two-way arbitrage and position Flowcarbon well to be compliant with at least some of the conditions Verra seems likely to impose prior to resuming bridging activity. As of the time of publication of this blog post, <a href="https://verra.org/consultation-on-verras-approach-to-third-party-crypto-instruments-and-tokens-webinar-and-extension/">Verra has launched a public consultation that is expected to run through November 1st, 2022</a>.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/8lrozNmy4wHtH2UTqFx1OX2oSG4hl8ppCdZ_oaI55YEc8d5DXcASbrZXUyFKJEG5EiBUAOYyJ-2lV4np3XuKB9t5Z3BAAJF6sGNfwhk8n7-a13AXd89-69Xf9Mo31F9UOTwxZx9TvAtkswV2abC2oa8" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy"></figure><p>Similar to other carbon bridges <a href="https://toucan.earth/">Toucan</a>, <a href="https://moss.earth/">MOSS</a> or <a href="https://www.c3.app/">C3</a>, this approach positions Flowcarbon to capitalize on the macro <a href="https://www.mckinsey.com/business-functions/sustainability/our-insights/a-blueprint-for-scaling-voluntary-carbon-markets-to-meet-the-climate-challenge">trends expected for global carbon markets</a> by industry observers like McKinsey.</p><h2 id="gnt"><strong>GNT</strong></h2><p>Flowcarbon proposes a two-way bridge to bring nature-based carbon credits on-chain to back their Goddess Nature Token (GNT) token. Given recent concerns by Verra, tied to their freezing of bridging activity since May, 2022, this additional fluidity of GNT should allow universal price discovery via two-way arbitrage and position Flowcarbon well to be compliant with at least some of the conditions Verra seems likely to impose prior to resuming bridging activity. </p><p>Flowcarbon underscores this ‘live, unretired’ nature of the bridging process they intend to use for GNT, ensuring the underlying carbon credits remain relevant and accessible to both on- and off-chain markets. In principle, this transferability would allow two-way arbitrage between markets, and support efficient price discovery.</p><p>GNT will focus on recent a rolling 5-year window of carbon credit vintages, and all credits bridged to GNT will be nature-based. While various methodologies exist for nature-based carbon credit certification, these projects typically include reforestation, nature restoration and conservation where nature’s ability to draw carbon out of the atmosphere is leveraged, rather than renewable energy or other credits which rely on a reduction in anthropogenic GHGs tied to energy production or consultation, or drawing carbon out of the atmosphere with human technologies.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/k3fIumS4m3dGTzc_Jw73J--ZSsFos69-qezZGWRMe9g73WBm6VrlwXw7O8wA3pBIAR8DASEr1QuJpShHwkgjqzjicPPVhQrcv6DH_GyuQghrIIlf4faI2Ni1MTH-Tjpe1XrEKIQKGoKH2BOhCy-z7E0" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy"></figure><h2 id="direct-project-investment">Direct Project Investment</h2><p>Starting in September, 2022, Flowcarbon began to facilitate direct investment into carbon projects with a fundraising round for the <a href="https://registry.verra.org/app/projectDetail/VCS/2611">Corazón Verde Del Chaco Project (Verra VCS 2611)</a>, located in Paraguay within the Gran Chaco Fores. </p><p>This <a href="https://tinlake.centrifuge.io/pool/0xd8486C565098360A24f858088a6D29a380dDF7ec/flowcarbon-1">investment round</a> launched on the <a href="https://centrifuge.io/">Centrifuge platform</a>, was oversubscribed and raised over 865,000 DAI via the sale of senior and junior tier tokens (labelled DROP and TIN, respectively) that provide a range of expected yield-based returns to investors. Looking ahead, Flowcarbon hopes to continue to facilitate these types of investments to address critical funding shortages for impactful projects.</p><h2 id="flowcarbon-founders-funders-partners">Flowcarbon Founders, Funders &amp; Partners</h2><p>In May, 2022 Flowcarbon announced that they had secured <a href="https://impactalpha.com/a16z-leads-flowcarbons-70-million-round-to-improve-voluntary-carbon-market-transparency/">a total of $70 million USD in Series A funding</a> to date. This was comprised of $32 million in venture capital, led by silicon valley venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, in addition to $38 million raised via their GNT token pre-sale earlier in the year.</p><p>It was during the media attention that the Andreessen Horowitz funding garnered that it first become public that former <a href="https://www.vice.com/en/article/88gwax/adam-neumanns-web3-startup-raises-dollar70-million-from-vcs-goddess-nature-token?utm_source=motherboard_twitter">WeWork founder and CEO Adam Neumann and his wife Rebekah were co-founders of Flowcarbon</a>. The organization does not list the Neumanns in as part of their <a href="https://www.flowcarbon.com/about">core team</a>, and it remains unclear what role the Neumanns might play in the day-to-day or strategic operations of Flowcarbon, or what level of investment the couple have made in the startup.</p><p>As part of the token pre-sale, Celo blockchain agreed to purchase $10M of the GNT token once it is available, in a move to offset their own residual emissions. In addition to a similar partnership that saw Celo commit to holding 0.5% of their treasury in MOSS’ MCO2 token, this move comes as Celo looks to position itself as a leading home for the burgeoning regenerative finance (ReFi) movement.</p><h2 id="key-people">Key people</h2><ul><li><a href="https://twitter.com/danagibber">Dana Gibber, CEO</a></li><li><a href="https://twitter.com/philfog">Phil Fogel, Chief Blockchain Officer</a></li><li><a href="https://www.linkedin.com/in/caroline-klatt-5b404323/">Caroline Klatt,</a> Co-Founder</li><li><a href="https://www.vice.com/en/article/88gwax/adam-neumanns-web3-startup-raises-dollar70-million-from-vcs-goddess-nature-token?utm_source=motherboard_twitter">Adam Neumann</a></li></ul><h2 id="key-resources"><strong>Key resources</strong></h2><ul><li><a href="https://assets.website-files.com/625db0bad5cfd681bd654bd8/62910403eab3711ae8e0b6b2_Flowcarbon%20Lite%20Paper%205.27.22.pdf">Flowcarbon GNT Litepaper</a></li></ul><h2 id="follow"><strong>Follow</strong></h2><ul><li><a href="https://twitter.com/weareflowcarbon">Flowcarbon Twitter</a></li><li><a href="https://discord.gg/8ZuKRfyf5G">Flowcarbon Discord</a></li></ul>

item.content:encoded: <h2 id="tldr"><strong>TL;DR</strong></h2><p>Toucan is a web3 regenerative finance (ReFi) protocol, focused on bringing carbon credits (primarily from the Verra registry) on-chain and making them readily accessible for emerging blockchain-powered carbon markets.</p><p>Toucan launched alongside fellow ReFi protocol KlimaDAO, in October, 2021, providing the initial pool of carbon credits branded as Base Carbon Tonne (BCT), which Klima utilized as backing for their token. Since launch, over ___ carbon tonnes have been bridged on-chain by Toucan, ___ % as BCT and ___% as their Nature-Based Carbon Tonne (NCT).</p><p>Similar to other bridges and ReFi projects working on building on-chain demand for carbon credits, Toucan's activity was immediately and severely limited once Verra announced the suspension of all bridging of carbon credits via their registry in May, 2022. As of August, 2022, Verra has launched a two-month consultation phase, seeking input from the public and key stakeholders to explore and address their concerns around the rapidly-developing on-chain markets.</p><h2 id="the-challenge"><strong>The Challenge</strong></h2><p></p><h2 id="toucans-solution"><strong>Toucan's Solution</strong></h2><p>Creating BCT and NCT pools allows for fungibility of these new tokens, while the underlying carbon credits on their own have varying vintages, methodologies and geographic provenance that make them difficult to source, trade or offset in bulk. </p><h2 id="state-of-the-on-chain-vcm"><strong>State of the On-Chain VCM</strong></h2><p></p><h2 id="toucans-partners-and"><strong>Toucan's Partners and </strong></h2><p></p><h2 id="resources"><strong>Resources</strong></h2>

item.title: ReFi Deep Dive: EthicHub
item.dc:creator: Phaedrus
item.content:encoded: <h2 id="tldr">TL;DR</h2><p>Based in Madrid, Spain, <a href="https://www.ethichub.com/">EthicHub</a> is a social impact investing platform, leveraging blockchain technology and crowdfunding mechanics to provide small-scale farmers with the financing required to bring their products to market, and for their enterprises and communities to thrive.</p><p>The project operates globally, with over 300 current projects successfully funded to date via microloans managed by blockchain-powered smart contracts.</p><h2 id="the-challenge">The Challenge</h2><p>Around the world, farmers with smaller operations struggle to access financing needed to reach their potential. This can put barriers in the way to getting products to relevant regional and international markets, as well as to maintaining and growing their offerings over time. Further, small-scale farmers in some markets like North America </p><p>Income inequality, poverty, food security and hunger are all serious consequences of this lack of of access to financial capital. </p><h2 id="ethic-hubs-approach">Ethic Hub's Approach</h2><p><em>Focus on Coffee </em>- Ethic hub is focused on farmers producing coffee, primarily in Mexico and Brazil (NEED TO DIG DEEPER)...</p><p><em>P2P Crowdlending</em> - EthicHub allows individuals to make direct loans to coffee under-banked producers who are facing challenges accessing capital. Specific producers, with defined project needs are listed in a <a href="https://app.ethichub.com/projects">public database</a>. Project backers receive pre-determined interest on their loans, managed by smart contracts.</p><p><em>Leveraging Blockchain</em> - While a cryptocurrency wallet isn't necessary to engage with the EthicHub platform, by enabling cryptocurrency payments for micro-loans expands the pool of capital that producers have access to. Fast, traceable and safe transactions enabled by blockchain bring increased inclusion and impact to the platform. EthicHub is partnered with Rootstock (RSK), a Bitcoin-operated P2P smart contract platform. </p><p><em>Ethic Hub and SDGs</em></p><p>The approach employed by Ethic Hub allows the project to address a total of 9 of the <a href="https://sdgs.un.org/goals">United Nation's 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)</a>. </p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/08/Screen-Shot-2022-08-25-at-5.14.43-PM.png" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="1004" height="1030" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2022/08/Screen-Shot-2022-08-25-at-5.14.43-PM.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2022/08/Screen-Shot-2022-08-25-at-5.14.43-PM.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/08/Screen-Shot-2022-08-25-at-5.14.43-PM.png 1004w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"><figcaption><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">SDGs addressed by Ethic Hub</span></figcaption></figure><figure class="kg-card kg-embed-card"><iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/0XTBYMfZyrM?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen="" title="Do you know all 17 SDGs?"></iframe></figure><p><em>Big Lenders Program </em> - In addition to its core microloan crowdfunding platowrm, Ethic Hub also offers a 'Big Lender' program that was launched in response to demand from their crowdfunding community. Participation in this program gives larger investors more flexibility in when they may invest.</p><p><em>Ethic Hub Local Nodes</em> - In Ethic Hub's model, local nodes are individuals who represent Ethic Hub and discover local small-scale producers who would likely benefit from participating in the fundraising platform. Having a local individual on the ground in these regions personalizes what could otherwise be seen as strictly a technological solution, and ensures that the work of the farmers and local community meets environmental standards, improving both quality and output.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/08/Screen-Shot-2022-08-27-at-9.48.37-PM.png" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="1066" height="724" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2022/08/Screen-Shot-2022-08-27-at-9.48.37-PM.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2022/08/Screen-Shot-2022-08-27-at-9.48.37-PM.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/08/Screen-Shot-2022-08-27-at-9.48.37-PM.png 1066w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"><figcaption><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Example of EthicHub Local Node Profile</span></figcaption></figure><p><em>Ethic Hub Coffee </em>- In addition to supporting farmers through microlending, you can also buy coffee direct through Ethic Hub's website, available as either beans or ground.</p><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="https://shop.ethichub.com/en/collections/cafes-de-especialidad-de-ethichub" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">Buy Ethic Hub Coffee</a></div><h2 id="tokenomics">Tokenomics</h2><p><em>Ethix Token </em>- EthicHub employs Decentralized Finance (DeFi) mechanisms through its $ETHIX token, which they refer to as a 'confidence-backed token'. With this token, holders are able to stake, bond and participate in liquidity pool farming. </p><p>Their online DeFi platform allows individuals to buy tokens.</p><h2 id="nft-art-project">NFT Art Project</h2><p>EthicHub has an innovative NFT art project they have launched <a href="https://www.ethichub.com/en/nft">here</a>, in partnership with photographer Stefano Azario. 50% of the revenue from NFT sales is redirected to coffee farmer’s cooperatives via transparent crypto transactions. These drops benefit coffee growers of Chiapas in Mexico.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/08/Screen-Shot-2022-08-27-at-10.08.39-PM.png" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="2000" height="1078" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2022/08/Screen-Shot-2022-08-27-at-10.08.39-PM.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2022/08/Screen-Shot-2022-08-27-at-10.08.39-PM.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2022/08/Screen-Shot-2022-08-27-at-10.08.39-PM.png 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/08/Screen-Shot-2022-08-27-at-10.08.39-PM.png 2248w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"><figcaption><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">EthicHub NFT Project Overview</span></figcaption></figure><h2 id="ethic-hub-and-toucan">Ethic Hub and Toucan</h2><p>Toucan has used their Nature Carbon Tonne (NCT) token to purchase EthicHub $ETHIX Bonds. (NEED MORE DETAILS ON THIS...)</p><figure class="kg-card kg-embed-card"><div><blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">7/<a href="https://twitter.com/EthicHub?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">@EthicHub</a> lets you quickly generate social impact: Improve the living standard of small farming communities by investing in their projects, buying their coffee, or providing liquidity for their loans<br><br>NCT will be used to purchase Ethic Hub bonds <a href="https://t.co/soeTYuhJEB">https://t.co/soeTYuhJEB</a></p>— Toucan (@ToucanProtocol) <a href="https://twitter.com/ToucanProtocol/status/1560628941219450881?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">August 19, 2022</a></blockquote> <script async="" src="https://platform.twitter.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script></div></figure><h2 id="key-people">Key People</h2><ul><li><a href="https://twitter.com/jori_armbruster">Jori Armbruster,</a> CEO</li><li><a href="https://www.linkedin.com/in/gabriela-chang-valdovinos-76b34410/">Gabriella Chang Valdovinos</a>, CSO</li></ul><p></p><h2 id="resources">Resources</h2><p><a href="https://twitter.com/EthicHub">Ethic Hub on Twitter</a></p><p><a href="https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCxLXFp8x93-ua34yZdHR-lA">Ethic Hub on YouTube</a></p>

item.title: Why Should You Care About Regenerative Finance?
item.dc:creator: Cate Kelly
item.content:encoded: <p>Human survival directly depends on the health of our planet. While our exponentially-growing population has built an empire of industrialism, thought, and culture, this is not without consequence. Climate change is rapidly becoming a global concern that demands our attention. The allure of constant progress and modernization have made it easy to forget that human beings have one life source: our environment. Culture and society have shaped our values to desire lifestyles that ignore the effects of climate change that we already experience regularly: Intense heat, <a href="https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-62722117">recurring flooding</a>, and <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2022/aug/29/major-sea-level-rise-caused-by-melting-of-greenland-ice-cap-is-now-inevitable-27cm-climate">rising sea levels</a> that swallow communities both large and small, among others. Our food systems are on the brink of toppling, and clean water has quickly become a precious commodity. </p><p>The growing disconnect we see from the industrial revolution to our 21st century world is between what we value and why we value it. Most of what we value as humans have social and cultural implications that we are born into. We value owning a nice house because we are taught that it will bring us happiness and security. We desire money to afford things and experiences that promise what everyone chases; happiness, popularity, freedom, exotic travel, even romance. There is nothing inherently wrong with valuing these things - some would say they are the beating heart of what it means to enjoy human existence. </p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/09/emissions-gap.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="2000" height="1509" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2022/09/emissions-gap.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2022/09/emissions-gap.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2022/09/emissions-gap.png 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/09/emissions-gap.png 2000w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"><figcaption>Courtesy of: https://blog.toucan.earth/regenerative-economies-in-web3/&nbsp;</figcaption></figure><p>However, our systems have been created ignoring the prosperity of the most valuable asset of all: our earth. Everything we hold dear relies on a healthy planet for all people. There will come a day when money can't buy oxygen, clean water, or food. The human imagination has dreamed up skyscrapers that kiss the clouds and machines that create wholly functioning robots. Yet the most vital aspect of the world's economic security has consistently been put on the backburner. </p><p>ReFi, or Regenerative Finance, is intended to be a bridge between worlds. It is a bridge that leverages the pioneering spirit that allowed us to become comfortable, technological explorers of the natural world. Instead of tearing down the global economy, it uses both old and new financial tools to reshape the it to include what we must value, and depend on, most. Many climate activists and movements call for the destruction of current systems to make room for a utopian new world that allows all people to have a voice, makes our cities green and sustainable, and returns healthcare to the sick and shelter to the misplaced. We all want this reality. However the systems we have now will not be replaced overnight. Cars will not stop driving, international shipping lanes will stay busy, and economic growth will continue to be pursued. Regenerative Finance aims to revitalize our current structures to not only include ecological health, but tie our economic success to their success. It is simply a method of revaluing what we need to value for human survival, connecting the regeneration of natural ecosystems to the generation of human wealth and prosperity. But what does that mean in practice?<br></p><figure class="kg-card kg-embed-card"><iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/2xo43tkr1TY?start=2&feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen title="ReFi Podcast S2 E6: What is ReFi?"></iframe></figure><p>This growing ReFi world, found in the corners of the internet, on podcasts, blogs, international conferences, meetups, and startups, is grown by climate and cryptocurrency enthusiasts alike. As an emerging ethos, there is room for all to share their voice. To create a new method of thinking, all must be included. From the bankers of London to the local communities of the Amazon rainforest to the high tech builders in Korea, and all in between. There is space to explore, leave your footprint, and choose the region of the growing ReFi community that most calls to you. Let's dive into the solutions being built within this new world. </p><p><strong>Community Core</strong></p><p>As with many movements and emerging cultures, a central zone exists for sharing information about the projects being created within the ReFi space: <a href="https://refidao.com">ReFi DAO</a>. To break it down, we already know what Regenerative Finance is and what it stands for- a DAO is a Decentralized Autonomous Organization, in simple terms an organization or group of people that run operations using the blockchain, which allows for transparent governance, funding, etc. </p><p><a href="https://refidao.com">ReFi DAO</a> can be considered one of the leading organizations for ReFi, listing the dozens of projects that are being built, updating about current ones, and holding discussions, community events, founders circles, funding, and more for emerging ReFi movers and shakers. As the core of the community, ReFi DAO is a fantastic resource for entering the space and learning more about where you fit and feel passionate about. </p><p><strong>ReFi Projects: A Taste Test</strong></p><p>What projects intrigue you? How could you get involved? Fortunately, deep knowledge of either climate or crypto isn't required; just a desire to be a part of a community that values the earth alongside innovation and economic philosophies born from the struggles of an unequal society. For a full list, head to <a href="https://refidao.com/?page=1">ReFi DAO</a>, but here are a few capital-backed projects that are leading the way when it comes to putting regenerative finance into practice: </p><p>1.<a href="https://www.klimadao.finance">Klima DAO- </a>Wrapping up DeFi (Decentralized finance) with ReFi is Klima DAO, a green economy structure built on the Polygon blockchain. Using technologies to reduce confusing market fragments and accelerate delivery of climate finance to sustainability projects globally, Klima utilizes carbon backed tokens ($KLIMA). These tokens add to an green treasury or improve liquidity for key environmental assets.</p><p>2.<a href="https://toucan.earth/">Toucan</a>- Toucan’s primary mission is to create public infrastructure for carbon markets running on open blockchains. This allows for carbon to become a workable and tradeable asset on the blockchain. By creating systems for regeneration, they are helping to solve key market issues including fragmentation, inefficiency, a lack of uniform data, and limited access.</p><p>3.<a href="https://www.regen.network/">Regen Network</a>- branded as ecological assets for the ReFi economy, Regen is truly leading the way when it comes to bridging between real life ecological impact and the incentives that web3 finance provides. From allowing on the ground communities to grow to tokenizing carbon credits on their registry, and allowing for decentralized governance for real life land stewards, the network of hands-on regeneration is growing. </p><p>4.<a href="https://www.openforestprotocol.org/">Open Forest Protocol</a>- offering a new paradigm for forests, Open Forest Protocol has created a system that is free and open for any forest project around the world to use in order to transparently Measure, Report, and Verify their on the ground data. This then allows for small and large forest projects alike to access carbon financing and hold the data in the hands of local communities instead of outsourcing to expensive and siloed monitoring methods. </p><p>5.<a href="https://moss.earth/">Moss</a>- from the Amazon rainforests of Brazil is MOSS, an organization focused on preserving the lungs of the planet. Using tokenization of specific carbon credits as well as NFTs, the MOSS MCO2 token represents tokenized carbon credits from projects directly working to prevent deforestation and protect the Amazon rainforest. You can also offset your carbon footprint with the data gathered from the Amazon. </p><p>6.<a href="https://www.flowcarbon.com/">Flowcarbon</a>- Flowcarbon operates at the intersection of carbon and new technology in order to protect earth’s natural carbon sinks and scale quality carbon reduction and removal projects. Their goals are to accelerate decarbonization through preserving and protecting ecosystems, some of the most immediate and cost effective carbon removal sinks, while continuing to invest in long term carbon reduction projects. They also address the world of carbon credits to bring them on the blockchain.<br><br><strong>Yes, There is Room for You</strong></p><p>These innovations and initiatives may seem overwhelming and complicated for someone not deep into the cryptocurrency or climate spaces to understand, and it does take a bit of learning. But all these solutions began as ideas from people who simply dared to dream of a new way of doing things; a new paradigm that regenerated the planet instead of destroying it, that puts people and communities before big money or rampant political corruption. Learning is a part of growing, and in ReFi, we are all learning and growing at once. There is time and room not only for you to join and be a part of the future of money and climate simultaneously, but to craft your ideas into reality. Come with your passion and your anger, your imagination and your hope for how we can turn this around. There’s a lot of work to do, but we’ll get there together. Welcome to Regenerative Finance. <br></p>

item.title: Introducing New Atlantis: Unlocking Marine Biodiversity & Blue Carbon
item.dc:creator: Gordon Gould
item.content:encoded: <p>Hello regens! <a href="https://twitter.com/g0rd0n__">Gordon</a> here, co-founder of <a href="https://gitcoin.co/grants/7126/new-atlantis-unlocking-marine-biodiversity-blue-c">New Atlantis</a>, introducing our project and the problem we're trying to solve to the ReFi community as we kick-off our new grant on <a href="https://gitcoin.co/grants/7126/new-atlantis-unlocking-marine-biodiversity-blue-c">Gitcoin GR15</a>! </p><h2 id="tldr">TL;DR</h2><p>Oceans represent a major area of opportunity to solve our ecological challenges and enable a new 'Blue Economy' that generates sustainable wealth for humanity. </p><p>New Atlantis is an ocean regeneration project that provides Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) with a viable business model by making marine biodiversity (and life-driven blue carbon) an investable asset class. We're building an open protocol leveraging ocean metagenomics, with an initial release available on <a href="https://github.com/new-atlantis-dao/Living-Oceans-Project">Github</a>.</p><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="https://gitcoin.co/grants/7126/new-atlantis-unlocking-marine-biodiversity-blue-c" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">Check out our grant on Gitcoin</a></div><hr><h2 id="our-vision-for-living-oceans-%F0%9F%A4%BF">Our vision for living oceans... 🤿</h2><p>As you might have guessed, we are very bullish on the living oceans as a vital way to regenerate the earth.</p><p>We see a future where humanity co-exists in harmony with our living seas and overcomes the twin existential crises of <strong>climate change</strong> and <strong>biodiversity loss—</strong>both of which threaten the stability of our global ecosystems and economy. In this introduction we are going to focus on the pivotal role marine biodiversity can play in this transition to a sustainable future.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/09/image-4.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1600" height="1067" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2022/09/image-4.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2022/09/image-4.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/09/image-4.png 1600w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"><figcaption><em>Photo used with permission by Cristina Mittermeier, co-founder of <a href="http://SeaLegacy.org">SeaLegacy.org</a>, UN SDG14 Ambassador, <strong>New Atlantis Founding Advisor</strong>, <a href="https://www.instagram.com/mitty/?hl=en">Instagram</a></em></figcaption></figure><h2 id="oceans-101-%F0%9F%8C%8A">Oceans 101 🌊</h2><p>The oceans are the largest feature on earth, covering 70% of the surface of the planet. Unsurprisingly, the oceans are critical to many major global processes including ecological stability, oxygen production, food production, and the carbon cycle. What is perhaps less obvious is how biodiverse marine life is a major driver of many of those processes, and how protecting biodiversity can be a major wealth unlock for humanity.</p><p>Due to their scale and vast productivity, our global biodiverse marine ecosystems</p><ul><li>Feed nearly 3 billion people</li><li>Produce 50% of the world’s oxygen</li><li>Are the basis for the global food web</li><li>Provide ecological resilience in the face of an increasingly volatile climate</li><li>Provide an estimated <strong><a href="https://ocean-climate.org/en/marine-and-coastal-ecosystem-services/">US$29.5 trillion</a></strong>/year in marine ecosystem services to humanity </li><li>Are critical to the ocean’s ability to sustainably sequester <a href="https://worldoceanreview.com/en/wor-1/ocean-chemistry/co2-reservoir/">vast amounts of “blue carbon”</a> via the marine carbon biological pump</li></ul><h3 id="marine-biodiversity-%F0%9F%90%A1">Marine biodiversity 🐡</h3><p>In other words, more biodiverse ocean life = more carbon sequestered, more food, more oxygen, greater resilience, more wealth creation, and a more beautiful world.</p><p>Unfortunately, marine biodiversity is under threat because our current economic systems lead to unsustainable practices like overfishing and pollution that focus on short term gains vs sustainable growth. If we do not find ways to arrest these processes, we could seriously damage our global ecosystems and face catastrophic changes in the planet’s ability to sustain life as we know it.</p><p>However, it is possible for humanity to effectively and sustainably partner with the oceans. By protecting marine biodiversity, we can very positively impact climate change AND provide a more abundant world for all.</p><p>So how do we both protect marine biodiversity AND help humanity thrive?</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/09/image-5.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1600" height="1064" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2022/09/image-5.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2022/09/image-5.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/09/image-5.png 1600w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><p><em>Photo used with permission by Octavio Aburto, PhD, Professor of Biological Oceanography, Scripps, <strong>Founding New Atlantis Advisor,</strong> <a href="https://www.instagram.com/octavioaburto/">Instagram</a></em></p><h2 id="marine-protected-areas-and-why-they-matter-%F0%9F%90%A0">Marine Protected Areas and why they matter 🐠</h2><p>Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) are the national parks of the oceans. MPAs are widely acknowledged as the <strong>best way to preserve and protect global marine biodiversity</strong>. In order to have globally sustainable oceans, the <a href="https://ocean.economist.com/governance/articles/the-need-to-protect-at-least-30-of-the-ocean-by-2030">UN estimates we need 30% of the oceans in fully protected MPAs by 2030</a>. Today, only 2.4% of the oceans are in fully protected MPAs.</p><p>This means we need to nearly 13x the amount of ocean in “fully protected” MPAs over the next 8 years. Unfortunately, MPAs overwhelmingly lack the resources to adequately protect life in their waters due to reliance on precarious government funding and traditional philanthropy.</p><p>So we must find ways to sustainably accelerate the deployment of full protection MPAs. </p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/09/image-6.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1285" height="961" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2022/09/image-6.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2022/09/image-6.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/09/image-6.png 1285w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"><figcaption><em>source: <a href="https://mpatlas.org/">https://mpatlas.org/</a></em></figcaption></figure><h2 id="how-we-can-protect-our-living-oceans-%F0%9F%A6%AD">How we can protect our living oceans 🦭</h2><p>New Atlantis believes the best way to scale MPAs is by providing MPAs with a viable business model that generates revenues based on MPA conservation efforts and outcomes achieved in their waters. We achieve this by creating an <strong>open marine metagenomics biodiversity analytics platform</strong> from which ecosystem health can be evaluated in order to issue blue carbon and biodiversity credits as a revenue source for MPAs.</p><p>Unpacking this further, we develop biodiversity metrics to measure and forecast the health of MPAs. MPAs can then use these biodiversity metrics to more effectively manage life in their waters and to develop blue carbon and biodiversity credits that can be sold to fund their operations. This process creates a sustainable revenue model that scales as MPAs expand their conservation efforts.</p><p>Additionally, expanding fully protected MPAs also can benefit local human populations. By protecting marine life in their waters, there is often increased—and sustainable—abundance in fisheries on the periphery of their full-protection zones which can mitigate any losses from not fishing within the protected areas.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/09/image-7.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1067" height="710" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2022/09/image-7.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2022/09/image-7.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/09/image-7.png 1067w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"><figcaption><em>Photo used with permission by Cristina Mittermeier, co-founder of <a href="http://SeaLegacy.org">SeaLegacy.org</a>, UN SDG14 Ambassador, <strong>New Atlantis Founding Advisor</strong>, <a href="https://www.instagram.com/mitty/?hl=en">Instagram</a></em></figcaption></figure><h2 id="product-roadmap-%F0%9F%97%BA">Product &amp; Roadmap 🗺</h2><p>We have already launched our cloud-based <a href="https://github.com/new-atlantis-dao/Living-Oceans-Project">Living Oceans Metagenome Assembly Pipeline</a> (available on <a href="https://github.com/new-atlantis-dao/Living-Oceans-Project">Github</a>) which analyzes ocean water DNA samples to develop “ecological fingerprints” of the planktonic species present and their relative abundance. We focus on plankton first as plankton accounts for approximately 90% of marine biomass. While plankton may seem inconsequential, they are the foundation of the global food web. Understanding and forecasting planktonic ecosystem health is mission-critical to developing ways to fully regenerate our oceans. </p><p>This initial milestone of launching our Metagenome Assembly Pipeline is just one of many phases on our roadmap, with a sneak peek below:</p><ul><li><strong>Phase 1: </strong><strong>Metagenome Assembly Pipeline</strong><strong> beta- (completed)</strong></li><li><strong>Phase 2: Expanding datasets / timeseries, adding species-level models</strong></li><li><strong>Phase 3: Integrating models into metagenome model</strong> </li><li><strong>Phase 4: Modular living oceans protocol</strong></li><li><strong>Phase 5: Marine biodiversity markets</strong></li></ul><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="https://gitcoin.co/grants/7126/new-atlantis-unlocking-marine-biodiversity-blue-c" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">See our Gitcoin grant for more details</a></div><h2 id="an-invitation-to-join-our-open-platform-%F0%9F%93%A8">An invitation to join our open platform 📨</h2><p>We know building marine biodiversity metrics and related blue carbon and bio-credit markets is a massive, complex undertaking. We know we cannot do this alone. That is why our approach is to build an <strong>open, transparent platform that rewards high quality data and ecological algorithm contributions</strong> to the overall biodiversity meta-model. See our <a href="https://gitcoin.co/grants/7126/new-atlantis-unlocking-marine-biodiversity-blue-c">Blue Paper</a> for more details.</p><p>We invite the global ocean community to come build with us, to help drive the Blue Economy, and to share in the wealth these Marine Protected Areas create. </p><p>If you're interested in learning more, check out our <a href="https://gitcoin.co/grants/7126/new-atlantis-unlocking-marine-biodiversity-blue-c">gitcoin grant</a>, follow us on <a href="https://twitter.com/NewAtlantisDAO">Twitter</a> and join our <a href="https://discord.com/invite/NewAtlantis">Discord</a>. Stay tuned for an upcoming episode on ReFi Podcast!</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/09/image-8.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1350" height="900" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2022/09/image-8.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2022/09/image-8.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/09/image-8.png 1350w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"><figcaption><em>Photo used with permission by Paul Nicklen, co-founder of <a href="http://SeaLegacy.org">SeaLegacy.org</a>, <strong>New Atlantis Founding Advisor</strong>, NatGeo Contributor, <a href="https://www.instagram.com/paulnicklen/?hl=en">Instagram</a></em></figcaption></figure>

item.title: Draft :Greenhouse Retreat : A report
item.dc:creator: Pranav Khanna
item.content:encoded: <p></p><p>Climate change represents the biggest challenge/opportunity facing humanity.</p><p>Consequently, it requires more coordination, more capital, more talent and more collaboration – between Web2 and Web3 movements – and within the exploding array of players and projects within Web3.</p><p><strong>Green House Retreat September 29 - October 1st, 2022 </strong>@BICOWG was a high signal, low noise gathering of leading operators at the intersection of blockchain, climate, and crypto in Web2 and Web3.</p><blockquote><strong>The <a href="https://bicowg.org/">BICOWG</a> is a brain trust of climate-crypto experts from protocols, organizations, and individuals supporting coordination, providing education, developing tooling, hosting forums, and providing clearinghouse services.</strong></blockquote><p>The <strong>Green House Retreat </strong>was enabled by the LOA Labs team</p><blockquote><a href="https://loalabs.io/">LOA Labs</a> is the laboratory for better world blockchains. With a focus on marketing, communications, community and network growth, LOA Labs aims to build long term relationship with impact protocols and projects. As a validator for proof-of-stake networks, LOA Labs serves as an active community member advocating for good governance and community engagement.</blockquote><h3 id="venue">Venue</h3><p>The retreat took place in a eco-friendly venue, located high up in a sacred mountain located in the municipality of Cocorná Antioquia. Colombia. Low internet connectivity was a feature in enabling quality hooman interaction - a building of Trust that accelerated conversations around "interoperability" </p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/10/DJI_0284--1-.JPG-min-min.jpg" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="2000" height="1125" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2022/10/DJI_0284--1-.JPG-min-min.jpg 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2022/10/DJI_0284--1-.JPG-min-min.jpg 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2022/10/DJI_0284--1-.JPG-min-min.jpg 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w2400/2022/10/DJI_0284--1-.JPG-min-min.jpg 2400w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><p></p><p>The invite only gathering included ecosytem stakeholders across the Web2 and Web3 domains covering L1's, Institutional investors, dApps, and NGO's</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/10/Capture-d-e-cran-2022-10-14-a--15.19.45--1--min.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="2000" height="1205" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2022/10/Capture-d-e-cran-2022-10-14-a--15.19.45--1--min.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2022/10/Capture-d-e-cran-2022-10-14-a--15.19.45--1--min.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2022/10/Capture-d-e-cran-2022-10-14-a--15.19.45--1--min.png 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/10/Capture-d-e-cran-2022-10-14-a--15.19.45--1--min.png 2178w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2022/10/Capture-d-e-cran-2022-10-21-a--14.07.35.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="2000" height="1188" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2022/10/Capture-d-e-cran-2022-10-21-a--14.07.35.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2022/10/Capture-d-e-cran-2022-10-21-a--14.07.35.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2022/10/Capture-d-e-cran-2022-10-21-a--14.07.35.png 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w2400/2022/10/Capture-d-e-cran-2022-10-21-a--14.07.35.png 2400w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><p></p><h3 id="programming">Programming </h3><p>The #ReFi movement is currently a very small part of the overall Climate addressal framework. Scaling up requires stakeholders to work towards ensuring “Interoperability” across Language, Code, and Tokens. </p><p>The two day retreat focused on specific presentations by key stakeholders around furthering “interoperability”, punctuated by Working Groups coalescing around specific initiatives.</p><p>Day 1 had presentations by</p><ul><li><strong>Dave Ford</strong> sharing his work at <strong>Ocean Plastic Leadership Network</strong> with lessons and a possible path to Interoperability with Web2 and Web3 stakeholders. Dave socialized the <strong>Blockchain for Climate Leadership Network (BxC)</strong> and invited conversations around how this could be an industry umbrella organization to enable Interoperability within Climate x Crypto and across allied domains.</li><li><strong>Philip Ackerman Leist</strong> - <strong>Foodicons</strong> - brought a <em><strong>boots on the ground</strong></em> perspective. Linking water, air, soil, carbon to climate, he galvanized the audience to think holistically around "ecosystem benefits" thereby highlighting the need for interoperability starting right from the ground up.</li><li><strong>Douglas Gayeton</strong> - <strong>The Lexicon</strong> - shared the need for interoperable language that can be standardized. Bringing his experience from helping the food industry, Douglas guided the audience towards creating a “digital fingerprint” with an <strong>outcome-based regenerative model.</strong></li><li><strong>Matthew Lawrenson</strong> - <strong>Tolam Earth</strong> - emphasized the need for a credible, efficient, transparent platform for buying and selling carbon offsets at scale - a platform that’s able to cope with, Complexity of project types and methodologies, discovery and pricing of differentiated assets, and a rapid increase in demand.</li><li><strong>Francisco Benedito</strong> - <strong>Climate Trade</strong> - spoke about climate change and carbon markets facing a problem of coordination and capital allocation. He shared the work at <strong>GreenClimateDAO</strong> and <strong>Climatecoin</strong> with the aim to create a climate finance ecosystem to fund decarbonization projects.</li><li><strong>Benoît Clément - Verra-</strong> provided insights around Verra’s <strong>openness</strong> to collaborate to make for efficient markets, drive finance to projects, and increase transparency. He highlighted the need for more positive stories of tokenization and blockchain. Questions regarding KYC surfaced several nuances around the purchase and trading of (carbon) credits.</li></ul><p><strong>Day 2</strong> of the retreat had all the participants engage with a degree of comfort, trust and desire to collaborate.</p><p>Conversations ranged across working groups, one to one’s and <strong>“out collaborating the competition”</strong></p><ul><li><strong>Gregory Landua - Regen Network -</strong> shared his vision of Regen Network as an ecosystem enabler. He cautioned against oversimplification and urged stakeholders to hold the “minimum viable complexity” as required by a holistic approach to addressing climate change. He specifically called for working with Verra as a partner rather than as a competitor.</li><li><strong>Amira Valliani - Solana -</strong> stressed the need to change the crypto narrative in Washington - to share the cases and positive stories with the policymakers. She invited the gathering to collaborate on Policy and offered to lead such work.</li><li><strong>Peter Rosberg - Ripple</strong> - shared how <strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong>giving back</strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong> is a core Ripple value that extends across a grants ecosystem and an equity investment fund focussed on Climate.</li><li><strong>Wes Geisenberger - HBAR Foundation</strong> proposed an immediately actionable item for the gathering: A common statement in response to Verra’s call for open consultation - <strong>The Medellin Statement: Response of Crypto-Climate Parties to Verra’s August 3, 2022 “</strong><a href="https://verra.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Verra-Public-Consultation-on-Crypto-Instruments-and-Tokens.pdf">Public Consultation On Third-Party Crypto Instruments And Tokens</a><strong>”</strong></li><li><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong><strong>Dave Fortson - LOA Labs -</strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong></strong> shared the work being done at LOA Labs - The laboratory for better world blockchains - to be the mycelial connection across the Web2 and Web3 climate ecosystem</li><li><strong>Nirvaan Ranganathan - Climate Collective -</strong> posited that while “interoperatability is the future” - we need to address the tension between innovation (read disruption) and the need to be “interoperable”. He shared the work at Celo and Climate Collective closing with an invitation to collaborate with the gathering.</li><li><strong>Sandra Ro - GBBC</strong> - With over 600 institutional members across the globe in 95 jurisdictions GBBC is dedicated to furthering the adoption of blockchain through engaging regulators, business leaders, and global change-makers on how to harness this ground-breaking technology to create more secure, equitable, and functional societies. Sandra highlighted the urgency for the climate crypto community to scale; to take the initiative for interoperability before the regulators and statutory authorities decide the direction of this multi trillion dollar industry.</li><li><strong>Dave Ford - BxC, OPLN</strong> - spoke on “<strong>collaborative fluency</strong>” which would drive interoperability across the corporate and political domain. Dave presented the “Ark” a metaphor and an experiential journey to bring the industry, solution providers and regulators up close to the realities of global warming in Greenland.</li><li><strong>Martin Wainstein - Open Earth Foundation -</strong> shared how they leverage emerging technologies such as AI, Blockchain and IoT to enable scalable solutions at a planetary level - <em>the operating system for Planet Earth.</em> Martin emphasized on the need for “stocktake” of work done by non stake actors in the run up to the <a href="https://climatechampions.unfccc.int/what-is-the-global-stocktake/">Global Stocktake</a> concluding at COP28 in 2023 in order to co-opt state actors to ratchet up their efforts at GHG reductions. Martin also invited the gathering to help develop an integrated climate accounting system through radical collaboration.</li></ul><p><strong>Hikes, Hot Tubs, and friendships 🔥</strong></p><p>The natural setting lent itself productively to warm conversations around nature.</p><p>Highlights included:</p><ul><li>Guided hike on a 1200 year old ancestral road, built by the indigenous people and visit to the indigenous Malokas and Eco-village</li><li>Hydrotherapy (waterfall, guava self-massage, steam room, hot &amp; cold jacuzzi)</li><li>Jeffersonian-style dinners (multi-tasking: eating, drinking and plotting the future for our planet earth)</li><li>Bonfires (where we discovered hidden talents from Green Housers during spontaneous karaoke and dancing nights, including Jefferson—our favorite Colombian rapper)</li></ul><p></p><h2 id="5-working-groups-%F0%9F%A4%9D">5. Working Groups 🤝</h2><p>Eight distinct working groups emerged from breakout sessions led by Chris Krohn of BxC. These working groups are focused around fundamental components that support ecologically beneficial multi-chain and multi-sector interoperability. Groups began within the categories of Social, Technical, Structural, and Ecological Benefits – from there, participants formed sub-groups around core needs.</p><p>The resulting groups are as follows:</p><p>Structural : Goal = Alignment of stakeholders, Web3 &amp; Web2 on Crypto x Climate interoperability</p><p></p><p></p><h2 id="6-social-proof">6. Social Proof</h2><p></p><p></p>

item.title: Meet New Atlantis DAO
item.dc:creator: Phaedrus
item.content:encoded: <p>In Episode 15 of <a href="https://anchor.fm/refipodcast">ReFi Podcast</a>'s second season, hosts John and John sit down with Courtney and Gordon, co-founders of <a href="https://newatlantis.io/">New Atlantis DAO</a> - an exciting new project at the nexus of Web3 and decentralized science (DeSci).</p><p>Listen to the full episode directly <a href="https://anchor.fm/refipodcast/episodes/Ocean-Metagenomics-with-Courtney-and-Gordon-from-New-Atlantis-DAO-e1qebi1">here</a>, or find ReFi Podcast on your favourite podcasting platform.</p><h2 id="the-challenge">The Challenge</h2><p>Climate change, ocean acidification and industrial fishing are all major threats to global marine biodiversity. Healthy marine ecosystems are vital to the overall health of our planet, as they:</p><ul><li>Produce 50% of the world’s oxygen;</li><li>Form the basis for the global food web;</li><li>Provide an estimated US$29.5 trillion/year in marine ecosystem services; and</li><li>Are critical to the ocean’s ability to sequester carbon.</li></ul><p>Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) are one of the leading ways to preserve and protect global marine biodiversity. Unfortunately, they often lack the resources and financial self-reliance to adequately protect life in their waters due to their dependence on sporadic government funding and philanthropy. </p><figure class="kg-card kg-embed-card kg-card-hascaption"><iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/U24KODxubVI?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen title="ReFi Podcast S2E15: Ocean Metagenomics with Courtney and Gordon from New Atlantis DAO"></iframe><figcaption>ReFi Podcast S2E15: New Atlantis DAO</figcaption></figure><h2 id="new-atlantis-approach">New Atlantis' Approach</h2><p>New Atlantis is an ocean regeneration project that provides Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) with a viable business model by making marine biodiversity (and life-driven blue carbon) an investable asset class. They aim to achieve this by launching a<strong> </strong>marine biodiversity analytics platform that will empower MPAs with the data they need to generate blue carbon and biodiversity credits. This process creates a sustainable revenue model that scales as MPAs expand their conservation efforts.</p><h2 id="resources">Resources</h2><p>Learn more and dive in to get involved in New Atlantis DAO:</p><p><a href="https://newatlantis.io/">New Atlantis Website</a></p><p><a href="https://gitcoin.co/grants/7126/ne">New Atlantis Blue Paper via Gitcoin</a></p><p><a href="https://discord.com/invite/newatlantis">New Atlantis Discord</a></p><p><a href="https://mobile.twitter.com/newatlantisdao">New Atlantis Twitter</a></p>

item.title: Speed & Scale with Ryan from Kleiner Perkins
item.dc:creator: Phaedrus
item.content:encoded: <p>Against the backdrop of COP27 unfolding in Egypt, your <a href="https://anchor.fm/refipodcast">ReFi Podcast</a> hosts John and Simar sit down this week for a timely conversation with Ryan Panchadsaram.</p><p>Ryan is an engineer and investor focused on solving systemic societal challenges at US venture capital firm <a href="https://www.kleinerperkins.com/">Kleiner Perkins</a>. There, he works as technical advisor to the chairman, John Doerr, investing in disruptive founders and technologies working on solutions to the climate crisis. Ryan is also the co-author of Doerr's 2018 national bestseller <em><a href="https://speedandscale.com/about/">Speed &amp; Scale</a>, </em>and previously collaborated on Doerr's bestseller <em><a href="https://www.whatmatters.com/the-book">Measure What Matters</a></em>. In March 2020, Ryan co-founded US Digital Response, a nonprofit that helps organizations respond more efficiently and effectively to emerging public needs. Previously, Ryan championed entrepreneurship, innovation, and open data as Deputy Chief Technology Officer in the Obama administration.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-embed-card kg-card-hascaption"><iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/uzq5HERxVMM?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen title="ReFi Podcast S2E16: Speed &amp; Scale with Ryan from Kleiner Perkins"></iframe><figcaption>ReFi Podcast: Season Two, Episode Sixteen</figcaption></figure><h2 id="the-challenge">The Challenge</h2><p>While the urgency of climate action has never been more clear, empowering impactful collective action remains a significant challenge. Where solutions exist, social and financial barriers to achieving meaningful scale can often get in the way.</p><p>As 27 COP meetings have demonstrated, implementing and managing climate solutions is much more challenging than simply agreeing that action is required or establishing commitments to act. </p><h2 id="ryans-thoughts-and-approach">Ryan's Thoughts and Approach</h2><p>OKR stands for Objectives and Key Results, an outcomes management tool discussed in depth in <em>Measure What Matters</em>. They address the critical facets of any goal worth achieving: the “what” and the “how.” Objectives are what you aim to accomplish. Key Results (KRs) tell us how the objectives get done.</p><p>If any goal could be considered "worth achieving", solving the climate crisis would certainly qualify. In the interview with John and Simar, Ryan explains how applying OKR's to the climate crisis is introduced in the Speed &amp; Scale book - which ultimately generated 10 separate objectives and 55 associated key results, all explorable in the <a href="https://speedandscale.com/tracker/">online tracker here</a>. </p><p>Listen to the full conversation above to learn more about Ryan, how Kleiner Perkins is helping to accelerate and scale up climate solutions, and hear his thoughts on everything from carbon markets to the future of money will shape a sustainable planet going forward.</p><h2 id="resources">Resources</h2><p><a href="https://www.panchadsaram.com/">Ryan - Website</a></p><p><a href="https://twitter.com/rypan">Ryan - Twitter</a></p><p><a href="https://www.kleinerperkins.com/ ">KleinerPerkins</a></p><p><a href=" https://speedandscale.com/tracker/">Speed &amp; Scale</a></p>

item.title: State of the ReFi Nation
item.dc:creator: Phaedrus
item.content:encoded: <p>In the latest episode of the <a href="https://anchor.fm/refipodcast">ReFi Podcast</a>, your host John Ellison is joined by Rez, co-founder of <a href="https://www.solid.world/">Solid World DAO </a>and co-host of <a href="https://music.amazon.com/podcasts/0a387dd1-88ca-46fc-9468-4638bce73082/this-week-in-refi">This Week in ReFi Podcast</a>. They take a look at the last year in the world of ReFi, the Cambrian explosion of innovation at the intersection of climate and Web3, where we are now, and where we are headed as we continue our collective ReFi journey.</p><p>Listen to the full episode directly <a href="https://anchor.fm/refipodcast/episodes/State-of-The-ReFi-Nation-with-Rez-from-Solid-World-DAO-e1rdtm8">here</a>, or tune in and follow the ReFi podcast on your favourite podcasting platform!</p><h2 id="the-challenge">The Challenge</h2><p>Climate change is undeniably the greatest and most important challenge that humanity has collectively faced. While brilliant people around the world are working to develop impactful ways to build a sustainable, resilient future on our planet, current financing models and our prevailing economic systems present significant barriers.</p><p>The carbon market is a promising mechanism, but is currently held back from realizing its transformative effects on the world. While carbon credits make climate-positive projects into viable businesses, the timelines to receive credits for their activities can be multiple years. Technologically innovative and grassroots projects alike then struggle to access the funds they need to scale and succeed in their mission. Although progress is being made, our planet can't wait for traditional finance to pivot and re-prioritize climate-positive projects. Enter Regenerative Finance...</p><h2 id="rezs-state-of-refi">Rez's State of ReFi</h2><p>So where are we at, and what progress has been made in building new financial models that re-centre and regenerate natural systems? ReFi has been on a wild ride for the past year, from the joint launch of <a href="https://klimadao.finance">KlimaDAO</a> and <a href="https://toucan.earth">Toucan Protocol</a> to the waiting game while <a href="https://verra.org">Verra Standards</a> and other off-chain incumbents explore tokenization of their carbon credits after halting bridging activity earlier this year.</p><p>Check out the full conversation with Rez below, for a deeper dive on his own story, and his take on a wide range of topics that have impacted ReFi over the last year!</p><figure class="kg-card kg-embed-card"><iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/QmIChfWM93Y?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen title="ReFi Podcast S2E18: State of the ReFi Nation with Rez from Solid World DAO"></iframe></figure><h2 id="connect-with-rez-solid-world-dao">Connect with Rez &amp; Solid World DAO </h2><p><a href="https://twitter.com/0xRez">Rez on Twitter</a></p><p><a href="https://www.solid.world">Solid World</a> </p><p><a href="https://docs.solid.world/">Solid World litepaper</a></p><p><a href="https://twitter.com/ThisWeekInReFi">This Week in ReFi </a></p>
