item.content:encoded: <p>ReFi Spring launched in May 2022 with the mission of supporting 50 in-person events to take place leading up to April 2023 to accelerate the Regenerative Finance (ReFi) movement. Learn more about the movement <a href="https://je.mirror.xyz/S-dpms92hw6aiacUHoL3f_iAnLVDvbEUOXw7wpy7JaU">here</a>.</p><p>Our small but mighty team of four fervently undertook this task and jumped into the unknown. We could not have imagined the rapid development of the movement and the sheer range of communities that have emerged since we embarked. So far, 27 events have been directly supported by ReFi Spring, along with numerous additional ReFi events occurring!</p><p>Over the past six months, ReFi Spring has contacted and supported an international group of inspiring community builders. We wrote this blog to share information about the diverse themes of events and communities that have shaped the founding months of our project.</p><p>We started out developing open-source resources focused on providing event organizers with funding, marketing materials, speaker lists, and event frameworks. All of these resources to date can be found in our <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1c1UYt6Kj20tNDOmYAiOTjSCFPqJymqthDFHsPJoNSS8/edit?usp=sharing">Event Toolkit</a>.</p><p>Our focus from the beginning has been to target support where the effects of the climate emergency are most intense: the Global South. Given the urgency of the climate crisis and its impact on communities today, we’ve been dedicated to catalyzing new ReFi communities in this region. We will continue to do so in 2023. Let’s jump into the 2022 events by themes!</p><h2 id="theme-1-engaging-new-audiences"><strong>Theme 1: Engaging new audiences</strong></h2><h3 id="refi-kenya"><a href="https://twitter.com/RefiSpring/status/1579813629633114115?s=20&amp;t=VHq7SY6CrXhnwd7sKxCFpw">ReFi Kenya</a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/defe555f-7d26-426d-a865-000efa8b8fd5/Untitled+design+-+2022-12-01T140031.046.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>Kenya is widely known as a leading country regarding strong web3 ecosystem development across the African continent. However, if we look at the scope of ReFi, a leader figure emerges in the landscape. This pioneer is <a href="https://twitter.com/shambanetwork">Shamba Network</a>, a startup led by <a href="https://twitter.com/KennedyWNganga">Kennedy Ng'ang'a</a>, working to build measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) tools accessible to small farmers. This team organized the first-ever ReFi gathering in Kenya.</p><p>The event introduced local farmers to ReFi principles, developed three ongoing projects on the ground, and included onsite tree planting.</p><h3 id="refi-uganda"><a href="https://twitter.com/RefiSpring/status/1578064304418471938?s=20&amp;t=VHq7SY6CrXhnwd7sKxCFpw">ReFi Uganda</a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/1c5706f5-4a3f-4a41-a714-30ee1332840b/Untitled+design+-+2022-12-01T140136.034.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>In Uganda’s Tororo region, a regenerative force exists at the core of the efforts of <a href="https://twitter.com/ayowecca_uganda">AYOWECCA Uganda</a>; an NGO led by <a href="https://twitter.com/j_olwenyi">Johnathan Olwenyi</a> focused on raising awareness about the climate emergency among small farmers and young generations.</p><p>More than 300 people attended this gathering, including state authorities. With the help of <a href="https://twitter.com/CeloUganda">Celo Uganda’s</a> <a href="https://twitter.com/umar_sebyala">Umar Sebyala</a> and Shamba Network’s Kennedy Ng'ang'a, this event was considered the first brick in building a bridge between local regenerative activities and the global ReFi movement.</p><h3 id="refi-peru">ReFi Peru</h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/d3f224d2-4dcf-4c07-bde5-ede547442e53/perubom.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p><a href="https://twitter.com/celoperu">Celo Peru</a> Ecosystem Leader <a href="https://twitter.com/luisotravez_eth?s=21&amp;t=GpU4as-4tkKjQwnhgNc15A">Luis Carranzas</a> organized a side event during <a href="https://twitter.com/EthereumLima">Ethereum Lima</a> to present the ReFi movement to local entrepreneurs and university students. This event focused on building trust with web3 developers and providing them with networking experiences to kick off planning for another ReFi Spring event in Peru in 2023.</p><h3 id="refi-cameroon"><a href="https://twitter.com/RefiSpring/status/1577332159559471104?s=20&amp;t=VHq7SY6CrXhnwd7sKxCFpw">ReFi Cameroon</a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/07510463-00bf-4f6c-88f2-f2b01e14c74a/Untitled+design+-+2022-12-01T140217.067.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>The first ReFi event in Cameroon brought together a female-led community to present ReFi as a way to unify social, environmental, and entrepreneurship impacts. This gathering introduced participants to the foundations of regenerative finance and explored inflation’s effects on the local community, the power of social currencies, and the adoption of mutual credit networks.</p><h3 id="refi-silicon-valley"><a href="https://www.instagram.com/p/ChFbwmkLtT_/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link">ReFi Silicon Valley </a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/5455b5d8-1983-4ec1-935c-16a8919e8a4c/siliciobom.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>This ReFi gathering took place in the heart of Silicon Valley in mid-August and focused on onboarding under-represented minorities into the web3 x climate space. A series of talks, workshops, and games brought together a local network of climate activists and crypto enthusiasts to discover the regenerative finance ecosystem.</p><h3 id="refi-suriname"><a href="https://twitter.com/RefiSpring/status/1595405668516859906?s=20&amp;t=SUGF0spsAwTrM8Ea5bhbuw">ReFi Suriname</a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/fc7368d6-d16c-4e7d-acd3-677cd1fca086/Untitled+design+-+2022-12-01T140305.727.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>The first-ever ReFi event in Suriname, “Innovators Buzz,” connected innovative minds in the web3 space to imagine a regenerative and resilient future for the country. This event served as a catalyst, sparking a new sustainable and innovative development movement in Suriname and the broader Caribbean region. This event brought together state authorities, local startups, academics, scientists, and university students to learn about regenerative finance and discuss Suriname's strategic position in this global ecosystem.</p><h3 id="rio-crypto-hub"><a href="https://linktr.ee/riocryptohub">Rio Crypto Hub</a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/78099bfd-9b96-4b57-a2d8-2d6107e899a5/Untitled+design+-+2022-12-01T140431.027.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>Rio Crypto Hub served as our leading partner for organizing ReFi events in Brazil. Together, their team organized three events introducing new communities to ReFi and showcasing local projects such as <a href="https://twitter.com/DetrashGlobal">DeTrash</a> and <a href="http://www.muda-oe.com/">Muda</a> to new audiences.</p><p>While ReFi Spring did not financially support the <a href="https://www.blockchainrio.com.br">Blockchain In Rio</a> event, our team provided content and speakers for six panels on the ReFi Summit stage. Our partnership with <a href="https://twitter.com/agroforestDAO">AgroForestDAO</a> enabled us to cover the travel expenses of Founder Diogo Jorge so he could host a workshop on how to build regenerative communities on the ground and the web.</p><h3 id="regenere-se"><a href="https://twitter.com/RefiSpring/status/1580939247418122240">Regenere-se</a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/c68dbec0-a683-41a7-84bb-dea34daf2fde/Untitled+design+-+2022-12-01T140751.086.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>With an audience composed of young members of the traditional Afro-Brazilian religion Candomblé, Muda’s event had the merit of being a gathering where people had their first contact with blockchain through the ReFi narrative, exploring Regenerative finance basics whilst learning how organizations like <a href="https://www.cambiatus.com">Cambiatus</a> are generating new forms of community through social currencies.</p><h3 id="refi-primavera-regenerativa-rio">ReFi Primavera Regenerativa (Rio)</h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/039bf498-e843-4468-9a91-5fad174681f1/Untitled+design+-+2022-12-01T140922.879.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>Moving from Rio de Janeiro to the State of Minas Gerais (the Brazilian state where two <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariana_dam_disaster">significant environmental</a> <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brumadinho_dam_disaster">crimes occurred</a>), AgroforestDAO’s Diogo organized another event, Primavera Regeneretiva, to introduce local farmers and youth to ReFi and how the movement can support local agroforestry projects.</p><h3 id="descentraliza-bh-minas-gerais"><a href="https://artigos.banklessbr.com/p/por-dentro-do-descentraliza-bh">Descentraliza BH</a> (Minas Gerais)</h3><p>On the same day of the event in Lima Duarte, another ReFi event took place in Minas Gerais, the beautiful city of Belo Horizonte, where <a href="https://twitter.com/BanklessBR">Bankless Brazil</a> organized the event DescentralizaBH with our support.</p><p>Following the lines of the Bankless narrative, the content delivered in this panel addressed the urgency of creating an on-chain market for the de-carbonization of the atmosphere and highlighted the <a href="https://climatecollective.org">Climate Collective’s</a> role in building this market.</p><h3 id="refi-costa-rica">ReFi Costa Rica</h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/fe3930b0-c19e-4b2a-8524-88a672a86316/Untitled+design+-+2022-12-01T141055.142.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>This event served as the launch of the <a href="https://medium.com/cambiatus/conociendo-de-modernos-negocios-colaborativos-con-cofiblocks-88ed3ddfa88a">CoFiBlocks Initiative</a>, a new cooperative of small coffee producers using blockchain to ensure the use of regenerative practices in coffee production in Costa Rica’s Monta Verde region. A community of local farmers and web-3 natives came together to share a day of talks and workshops exploring blockchain use cases for their local context.</p><h3 id="refi-spain"><a href="https://twitter.com/Mad_Regen">ReFi Spain</a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/49ee1e08-646c-46eb-a12a-f37400ceed7d/Untitled+design+-+2022-12-01T141240.019.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>The “Mad Regen Gathering” event organized by <a href="https://ethix.ethichub.com/">Ethic Hub</a> and <a href="https://twitter.com/lettyprados">Letty Prados</a> activated Madrid’s Regen community to come together for a weekend of planning and networking to support local regeneration projects and community development.</p><h3 id="refi-fest"><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?ab_channel=SEEDS%3ARegenerativeEconomies&amp;v=m66T0Phsxkw">Refi Fest</a></h3><p>This event held in North Carolina, United States, celebrated the third anniversary of <a href="https://joinseeds.earth">SEEDS</a>, bringing together academics, scientists, regenerators, and indigenous peoples for a full day of talks and community building illuminating the journey that is required towards regenerative cultures and economies.</p><h3 id="carbonfi"><a href="https://dandelion.earth/events/632a6f1a8a10380010acea77?cohost=refi-spring">Carbon.fi</a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/510c88e8-b74d-47f2-8819-08622f941f9a/Untitled+design+-+2022-12-01T141337.939.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>This event, held during Singapore’s <a href="https://www.mse.gov.sg/climate-action-week/">Climate Action Week</a>, brought actors, organizations, and stakeholders from the sustainability and ReFi spaces together for two days of explorative talks and interactive workshops.</p><h3 id="refi-portugal"><a href="https://twitter.com/RefiSpring/status/1542795142330847233?s=20&amp;t=SUGF0spsAwTrM8Ea5bhbuw">ReFi Portugal</a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/51ef1402-fda3-44e4-9eba-ab671c1153a5/Untitled+design+-+2022-12-01T085112.530.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>This four-day event at the <a href="https://traditionaldreamfactory.com">Traditional Dream Factory</a> focused on connecting ReFi protocols with land-based ventures and regenerative agriculture and agroforestry experts. Featured talks from <a href="https://celo.org">Celo</a>, <a href="https://www.gooddollar.org">Good Dollar</a>, <a href="https://polygon.technology">Polygon</a>, and several others served as the first experience many local farmers in attendance had with web3 and blockchain.</p><hr><h2 id="theme-2-interdisciplinary-events"><strong>Theme 2: Interdisciplinary Events</strong></h2><h3 id="refi-unconference"><a href="https://twitter.com/RefiSpring/status/1538810252719702016?s=20&amp;t=SUGF0spsAwTrM8Ea5bhbuw">ReFi Unconference</a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/eea2c91f-1adf-483e-9419-727f96305964/Untitled+design+-+2022-12-01T090027.619.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>The first ReFi Spring-supported event of 2022 was the ReFi Unconference held at the <a href="https://www.crypto-commons.org">Crypto Commons Hub</a> in Austria. Talks from <a href="https://commonsstack.org">Commonstack</a>, <a href="https://www.holochain.org">Holochain</a>, and <a href="https://regen.foundation">Regen Foundation</a> were featured amongst many others, interspersed with many discussions around defining value and impact.</p><h3 id="regens-unite"><a href="https://twitter.com/RefiSpring/status/1571781342030864386?s=20&amp;t=SUGF0spsAwTrM8Ea5bhbuw">Regens Unite</a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/bfa09f56-6598-4e45-a629-ca2abac09402/Captura+de+Tela+2022-11-30+a%CC%80s+18.30.44.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>The dedicated team behind <a href="https://www.regensunite.earth">Regens Unite</a> held an event in Berlin focused on building bridges between diverse groups, web3 Regens, web2 climate tech, non-tech, science, and climate activist audiences. This two-day gathering featured an interactive, intimate, high-participation program to facilitate open discussions around building regenerative systems.</p><h3 id="planethealth"><a href="https://twitter.com/RefiSpring/status/1584916527198965766?s=20&amp;t=SUGF0spsAwTrM8Ea5bhbuw">Planet.Health</a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/5bb5ace8-ca5c-4f95-88fd-4045d6e05be2/Untitled+design+-+2022-12-01T090920.691.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>This three-day unconference, held at the Château du Feÿ in France, brought together two seemingly disparate movements. <em>Planetary health</em>, an interdisciplinary medical field recognizing human health as interconnected and interdependent with ecology - and web3 advocates. Experts from global health, climate, governance, technology, philanthropy, law, art, ecology, and academia discussed how blockchain technology could improve planetary health. Follow this team’s ongoing journey on Twitter <a href="https://twitter.com/PlanetHealthX">here</a>.</p><h3 id="solarpunk-wow"><a href="https://twitter.com/RefiSpring/status/1583500208352030720?s=20&amp;t=SUGF0spsAwTrM8Ea5bhbuw">Solarpunk WOW</a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/f6088133-0bcb-4076-8995-a47fc9e9ab68/Untitled+design+-+2022-12-01T141828.604.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>This event, held at the <a href="https://www.crypto-commons.org">Crypto Commons Hub</a> in Austria, brought together permaculture and web3 developers to participate in a hands-on permaculture workshop. Together, attendees explored applying internet of technology (IoT) and AI-backed visualization tools during a facilitated skills exchange session, all embedded in a continuous discussion about the politics and aesthetics of the Solarpunk and broader ReFi movement.</p><h3 id="refi-singapore-x-indigenous"><a href="https://twitter.com/RefiSpring/status/1577615027993022464?s=20&amp;t=SUGF0spsAwTrM8Ea5bhbuw">ReFi Singapore x Indigenous</a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/05952d32-0212-4a8c-a1c9-81a75da078a5/chinezinmanero.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>This event brought together indigenous community representatives to explore creating an inclusive framework for responsible planet stewardship. Discussions featured questions such as how to generate a shared understanding of the measurement of hyper-local ecological and social capital and how to approach the inclusion of second-order spiritual impacts and indigenous commons into calculating carbon credits and other economic measurements.</p><h3 id="the-future-is-now"><a href="https://twitter.com/RefiSpring/status/1582378546194153472?s=20&amp;t=SUGF0spsAwTrM8Ea5bhbuw">The Future is Now</a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/b48e3c79-bfd9-4592-bbd7-abe35affe704/co%CC%81pia+de+1_8inSz0XCO5qWx8xMOiGTuA+%281%29.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>Just north of Berlin, Germany, <a href="https://twitter.com/pstehlik">Philip Stehlik</a> gathered a group of Regens from different parts of the world to build the basis for coordinating their projects. This gathering also served as a moment for group reflection and spiritual healing.</p><hr><h2 id="theme-3-bioregion-focused-events"><strong>Theme 3: Bioregion-Focused Events</strong></h2><h3 id="kolektivo-festival"><a href="https://medium.com/kolektivo-co/regenerative-finance-blooms-in-the-caribbean-b1dfef2dfa25">Kolektivo Festival</a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/06d09f57-b01e-4a73-b1c1-863b64a846e5/Untitled+design+-+2022-12-01T141449.099.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>On the island of Curaçao, next to the coast of Venezuela, <a href="https://www.kolektivo.network">Kolektivo</a> organized a ReFi event to bring together global and local ecosystem representatives. This event served as the largest ReFi-only event of the year, with 700+ attendees. Attendees gathered to participate in different workshops and build bridges between their projects.</p><h3 id="refi-barichara"><a href="https://twitter.com/SevNightingale/status/1579715211824889857">ReFi Barichara</a></h3><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/d177d9c8-00ae-4024-a5d9-a3f18a21f247/Untitled+design+-+2022-12-01T141659.044.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="675"></figure><p>Just before <a href="https://schellingpoint.gitcoin.co">Schelling Point Bogotá</a> and <a href="https://sbs.tech">Sustainable Blockchain Summit</a>, several ReFi ecosystem representatives gathered in a small city eight hours from Bogotá to learn from locals about the regeneration of the Barichara bioregion. During the four-day event, attendees visited projects aimed at different fields of regeneration: land, forest, social tissue, and water. Stay updated with this project’s development by following them on Twitter <a href="https://twitter.com/cognitivepolicy">here</a>.</p><h3 id="conclusion">Conclusion</h3><p>The first season of ReFi Spring events has brought together ~2500 attendees across 20+ countries. Our team is pleased to see a diverse range of communities and projects taking off as we collectively explore and define this growing movement, bursting at the seams with talented humans striving to explore web3 pathways to enable communities to build a regenerative economy. ReFi Spring will return in January 2023 in preparation for the next season of local events! We are very excited about the communities that have been born, the communities to come, and the conversations that will arise. Follow our ongoing developments on <a href="https://twitter.com/RefiSpring">Twitter</a>, <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/refi-spring">LinkedIn</a>, and <a href="https://www.instagram.com/refispring/">Instagram</a>.</p>
item.excerpt:encoded: Celebrating the first season of 27 ReFi Spring events bringing together ~2500 attendees across 20+ countries!

item.title: The Brazilian Ecosystem of Regenerative Finance PT I
item.dc:creator: Marcelo Silva
item.content:encoded: <p>Regenerative Finance (ReFi) is a decentralized global movement that uses blockchain technology and web3 concepts to address the climate emergency. Brazil is worldly known for its abundance of natural resources and the challenges of protecting it, hence the fact that this specific ecosystem has grown so fast here.</p><h3 id="the-community"><strong>The Community</strong></h3><p>The Brazilian ReFi ecosystem stands out worldwide with its growth rate and the diversity of its components.</p><p>From large companies like MOSS creating solutions to preserve the Amazon rainforest, to initiatives like AgroforestDAO that aim to accelerate the adoption of Agroforestry practices by small producers, passing through the Rio Crypto Hub that links education about DeFi with social impact.</p><p>The reason is simple: we are home to enormous biodiversity, which is under recurrent threats from both internal and external sources. We are also home to intense innovation activity, particularly in the FinTech sector.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/513f7d12-19f7-4c48-bc1c-45278adbda1a/Captura+de+Tela+2022-12-19+a%CC%80s+19.56.14.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1764" height="396"><figcaption><em>Brazil is the home of the Amazon River, the largest in the world. Also, it was the home of the Rio Doce (which goes through 230 cities covering a population of more than 3,6mi people) that was reduced to toxic mud by the environmental crime of the mining company Vale do Rio Doce.</em></figcaption></figure><p>In the second part of this article, we will present the Brazilian ReFi initiatives. Here we will talk about the moments when this ecosystem came together, and the position of ReFi Spring in this process.</p><p>The biggest meeting was certainly on the impact stage of the <a href="https://www.blockchainrio.com.br/en-gb">Blockchain In Rio</a> event in the first days of September, the stage (called ReFi Summit) had fifteen panels on social and environmental impact.</p><p>In the first part of the day, topics such as the presence of women in Web3, Black Money, Bitcoin Mining, the Carbon Market, the future of education, and waste management were discussed.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/cae7ce4c-2854-4d08-acc2-0c6c67b182c0/Captura+de+Tela+2022-12-19+a%CC%80s+19.56.42.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1550" height="895"><figcaption><em>The event Blockchain in Rio had an entire stage dedicated to Social Impact and ReFi, the ReFi Summit organized by Impacta.Finance.</em></figcaption></figure><p>The relaxed tone of the discussions both among the speakers and with the audience was not a coincidence, but a result of the fact that there were not only specialists in their fields but also individuals who already cooperate in several projects related to both ReFi and Social Impact in general.</p><p>This proximity meant that, instead of isolated discussions, there was a continuous dialogue distributed in different sections where the participants were interspersed between the stage and the audience.</p><p>In the afternoon, discussions shifted to financial instruments, forests, Games, and Impact-driven DAOs. The final panel was a workshop on how to build regenerative communities, where I shared the stage with Diogo J. from AgroForestDAO.</p><p>The most striking aspect of the discussions in this second part was the enormous diversity of experiences and narratives. The panels were held with the participation of activists, entrepreneurs, investors, and intellectuals, who had complete freedom to expose their positions.</p><p>It's worth mentioning that considering the context of a polarized country with little to no space for sharing ideas, the ReFi Summit was an oasis of civility, innovation, and cooperation. In Portuguese, Spanish, and “Portunhol”.</p><p>However, the day before the event Blockchain In Rio gifted us with this immersion into the ecosystem, a big part of the speakers and the audience who were on the ReFi Summit stage came together in one of the <a href="https://linktr.ee/riocryptohub">Rio Crypto Hub</a>.</p><p>With the support of ReFi Spring, the event featured a series of lectures on ReFi and Chainlink oracles.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/52f0a40a-b8a6-4c48-8818-b11a9087efef/Captura+de+Tela+2022-12-19+a%CC%80s+19.57.00.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1636" height="565"></figure><p>It is interesting to note that Rio Crypto Hub had one edition on the day before the start of Blockchain in Rio and another one right after it.</p><p>Right after the last day of Blockchain In Rio, representatives from ReFi Spring, Play4Change, Impact Plus, Chainlink, and SandBox left for the beautiful city of Seropédica to exchange an idea about Blockchain, Oracles and ReFi with students from the Federal Rural University of Rio de Janeiro in another edition of the Rio Crypto Hub.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/d0fddb0d-9a42-4165-b45d-620bcd247a86/Captura+de+Tela+2022-12-19+a%CC%80s+19.57.19.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1527" height="541"></figure><p>The reality of the Brazilian ecosystem is one of uninterrupted work for survival. And the fact that all these events took place in such a short time is a good demonstration of this effort.</p><p>The sequence of the events and gatherings in Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais can be considered as the first steps of a road that led to the consolidation of a common narrative in the Brazilian ReFi ecosystem. Let's dive into it.</p><h3 id="the-meaning"><strong>The Meaning</strong></h3><p>This Brazilian narrative consolidated in the events mentioned above refers to two basic elements: Syncretism and Ginga (as innovation).</p><p><strong>Syncretism</strong>, the combining of diverse beliefs and schools of thought, is a hallmark of our country, and this ecosystem reflects that in a way that the rest of the innovation industry could only dream of. This unique diversity comes from both external and internal factors, including the relevance of political agendas related to inequality or <a href="https://www.unicef.org/globalinsight/what-climate-justice-and-what-can-we-do-achieve-it">climate justice.</a></p><p>The native projects of the Brazilian ReFi ecosystem arise with this demand for diversity, which is also an advantage as it offers access to a wide range of perspectives on topics like how to properly approach a specific social group in order to have cooperation.</p><p>One of the most explicit manifestations of this syncretism could be observed at the Primavera Regenerativa event. In this specific event, the participants organized themselves into three conversation circles where experts, newbies, skeptics, and curious people took turns contributing to the most diverse range of topics related to the intercession between regeneration, blockchain, and sacred memory.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/f693baca-b8b5-4888-8512-af5e863d5de0/Captura+de+Tela+2022-12-19+a%CC%80s+19.57.35.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1128" height="435"></figure><p><strong>Innovation</strong>, or ginga, relates to the fact that Brazilian Web3 entrepreneurs (we call them ‘Builders’) are used to reacting to obstacles in the most creative and unexpected ways.</p><p>This type of innovation is easily perceived in the way our Builders overcome institutional insecurity (like the lack of legal framework) and lack of resources to offer the world some of the most interesting solutions in ReFi.</p><p>Whatever the reason, the fact is that unlike our colleagues in the global north, here we are used to delivering results with very little support. The space for mistakes is small.</p><p>These two characteristics, together with a desire to open doors and build bridges, make <em>builders</em> anxious yet hopeful about how Blockchain can be used to address social and environmental challenges in Brazil.</p><h3 id="the-connection"><strong>The Connection</strong></h3><p>ReFi Spring, in this context, serves the humble purpose of accelerating the emergence of new micro-ecosystems by enabling events to reach new audiences inside and outside the Web3 ecosystem.</p><p>The support from ReFi Spring takes place through marketing, framework, networking, an organizer toolkit for ReFi events, content, and funds to bootstrap the events.</p><p>Except for the Blockchain In Rio event, all the other events mentioned in this article had direct support from ReFi Spring. The presence of ReFi Spring in Blockchain In Rio refers to the content delivered in six different stages, this was possible due to the diligent work of the Divas from <a href="https://www.impacta.finance/pt">Impacta.Finance</a>: Rafaela Romano and Paula Palermo.</p><p>If the three editions of the Rio Crypto Hub are good examples of how a micro-ecosystem is built around the topic of ReFi, the Regenere-se event organized by Muda (also in Rio de Janeiro) was the perfect case for presenting the topic of ReFi to a new audience.</p><p>There, an audience composed of members of religions of African origin exchanged experiences and were introduced to Regenerative Finance, ReFi Spring, and the purpose of the Climate Collective.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/cbc45b4d-78d9-47a2-a703-81e167d4cd46/Captura+de+Tela+2022-12-19+a%CC%80s+19.57.49.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1202" height="401"></figure><p>The presence of members from Afro-Brazilian religions and the encounter with the topic of Web3 is a new thing for the ecosystem, a happy novelty organized by the Muda team together with Luísa from<a href="http://www.krya.studio/"> Studio Krya</a> and <a href="https://www.cambiatus.com/">Cambiatus</a>.</p><p>Rio de Janeiro is a metropolis, and even though it is a geographically small city, these aforementioned events took place in profoundly different realities. The Rio Crypto Hub usually happens in urban areas with a very techie audience, and the Regenere-se happened within a sacred place for the afro-Brazilian religion Candomblé.</p><p>If Web3's biggest challenge is to achieve mass adoption, one of the priorities in the ReFi ecosystem is the onboarding of those who work directly with the land. The first step towards this challenge was the Primavera Regenerativa event organized by Diogo Jorge from AgroForestDAO in Lima Duarte (interior of Minas Gerais).</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/e9c1532d-8a8c-4a1f-bb4a-bbe5a20b4cbb/Captura+de+Tela+2022-12-19+a%CC%80s+19.58.00.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1293" height="433"></figure><p>The event focused on small farmers and school-age youth in the Lima Duarte region (Minas Gerais), and took place on November 19th. It was a moment of integration and discussion about the possibilities of the ReFi ecosystem for the region.</p><p>On the 19th of November, another pioneering event, built in a partnership between <a href="https://artigos.banklessbr.com/">BanklessBR</a>, Chainlink, <a href="https://www.nftfy.org/">NFTFY,</a> <a href="https://zapper.fi/pt">Zapper</a>, and ReFi Spring, was Descentraliza-BH.</p><p>This was the first Web3 event in the city of Belo Horizonte to address ReFi. Direct mining effects have damaged Minas Gerais and the city of Belo Horizonte for decades, and the topic of ReFi is of particular importance for the region. Minas Gerais was also the Brazilian state where two (<a href="https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2019/01/25/vale-dam-breaks-in-minas-gerais-3-years-after-mariana-disaster-at-least-200-missing/">1</a>, <a href="https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2018/12/06/samarco-dam-disaster-in-brazil-surpasses-1100-day-mark-miners-remain-unassisted/">2</a>) of the biggest environmental crimes in history took place, making the demand for regenerative solutions extremely urgent.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/588fae02-2fa0-4822-8e39-8993ecae194e/Captura+de+Tela+2022-12-19+a%CC%80s+19.58.19.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1447" height="701"></figure><p>DescentralizaBH was also important in presenting the topic of Regenerative Finance to the municipal authorities of the neighboring city (Nova Lima), in the person of Italo L. Salvador, manager of the Rego dos Carrapatos Ecological Park in Nova Lima.</p><p>Last but not least, Brazil was the place of a pioneering experience: A hackathon to tokenize all real estate properties of the Brazilian State. It was organized through a partnership between the Celo Foundation and the Brazilian public company SERPRO (Federal Service of Data Management).</p><p>The team's challenge was coming up with the best ideas to bring more than U$400bi worth of assets on-chain. This was a singular event in the history of the ReFi ecosystem as a whole, and we can be grateful for the efforts of the Celo team in Brazil (especially Mila Rioja and Rafael) and the employees of SERPRO.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/ebd60c76-2192-4b97-86d4-89fe86984383/Captura+de+Tela+2022-12-19+a%CC%80s+19.58.30.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1431" height="395"><figcaption><em>The Hackathon organized by Celo and the public company SERPRO happened due to the efforts of the Celo team in Brazil and Mila Rioja (Celo Lead for Latin America).</em></figcaption></figure><p>This was a singular event in the history of the ReFi ecosystem as a whole and we can be grateful for the efforts of the Celo team in Brazil (especially Mila Rioja and Rafael) and the employees of SERPRO.</p><h3 id="the-conclusion"><strong>The Conclusion</strong></h3><p>We cannot say that the journey of events above describes all the greatness of the Brazilian ReFi ecosystem, it describes a roadmap of encounters and re-encounters that made people perceive themselves as part of an ecosystem.</p><p>By perceiving themselves as an ecosystem, Brazilian projects are starting to coordinate talent, resources, and challenges at a national level to increase the vitality of Regenerative Finance in the country exponentially.</p><p>In the next part of this article, we will talk about the initiatives and projects of our ecosystem and find out what's in the mind of the founders and CEOs of these initiatives.</p><p>If Celo's proximity to Brazil and Moss’ importance to the world have already made our country stand out in the global ReFi ecosystem, the creation of an alliance between communities that recognize themselves through the events mentioned here has the potential to take Brazil to a new level of collective leadership in the global ReFi ecosystem.</p>
item.excerpt:encoded: By perceiving themselves as an ecosystem, Brazilian projects are starting to coordinate talent, resources, and challenges at a national level to exponentially increase the vitality of Regenerative Finance in the country.

item.title: The Institutional Pioneerism of Celo and The Climate Collective
item.dc:creator: Marcelo Silva
item.content:encoded: <p>Since its inception, <a href="https://twitter.com/CeloOrg"><strong>Celo</strong></a> has presented itself as a protocol constituted by the need for a blockchain infrastructure adapted to the needs of a future market.</p><p>Even if the Web3 ecosystem is marked by innovation, a relevant portion of the solutions launched aim to solve already recognized challenges or improve existing solutions.</p><p>Celo, since its initial design, is not part of that statistic. Celo was designed as a solution to a challenge that was not specific to the ecosystem but to the human experience itself: solving the problem raised by the Aristotelian denunciation of chrematistics.</p><h3 id="what-was-this-problem">What was this problem?</h3><p>Most of the solutions launched in the ecosystem follow the same premise, of being neutral in relation to the type of problem they can solve. This is a good strategy to avoid the emergence of niches within niches in an ecosystem that was already small.</p><p>The ecosystem that emerged from the technology generated, in large part, solutions that presented themselves as innovations for the original technology itself.</p><p>Applications started to come later, generally driven by incentive programs on the part of the protocols themselves.</p><h4 id="celo%E2%80%99s-pioneerism">Celo’s pioneerism</h4><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/03/image-22.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1200" height="627" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/03/image-22.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/03/image-22.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/03/image-22.png 1200w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><p>By presenting itself as a blockchain designed to house solutions related to the planet and social justice, Celo stood out with its successful pilots and its alliances and partnerships with traditional institutions in the impact field.</p><p>This institutional design is noticeable both in Celo's history and in the options for places and challenges to be faced (pilots developed to face challenges in the Global South, in places like Colombia, Kenya, and Nigeria).</p><p>If this design positively highlighted Celo inside and outside the ecosystem, the alliances created around themes such as social transformation and climate action provided Celo (and its partners) with centrality in the field of Blockchain For Good.</p><p>The first alliance, The Alliance for Prosperity, quickly brought together more than 100 initiatives dedicated to offering financial tools to redesign our relationship with money.</p><p>It was a simple initiative in its intent to bring together global interests in overcoming the challenges of inequality through DeFi, and innovative in its realization (in fact, bringing together companies, startups, funds, and various initiatives native or not from the web3, in a common goal of positive impact on the planet).</p><p>The second alliance, Climate Collective, however, did more than bring together initiatives.</p><h4 id="the-climate-collective">The Climate Collective</h4><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/31cdb8c4-27d5-403c-af6c-a8525a3fb4b2/Logo-Animation.gif?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1080" height="412"></figure><p>The <a href="https://twitter.com/clim8collective"><strong>Climate Collective</strong></a> is an initiative that was born within the ReFi ecosystem and had such a decisive contribution that we can define it as one of the main catalysts of this ecosystem. The CC definitely contributed to the consolidation of a new ecosystem that comprises what many believe to be the key to achieving mass adoption and guaranteeing the reversal of the process of destruction of human living conditions on the planet.</p><p>Consisting of twenty-four initiatives (<a href="https://twitter.com/AstralProtocol">Astral Protocol</a>, <a href="https://twitter.com/byterocket">Byterocket</a>, <a href="https://twitter.com/CeloOrg">Celo</a>, <a href="https://twitter.com/cLabs">CLabs</a>, <a href="https://twitter.com/curvelabs">Curve Labs</a>, <a href="https://twitter.com/carbonflowcap">Flow Carbon</a>, <a href="https://twitter.com/KolektivoLabs">kolektivo Labs</a>, Loam, Moss, <a href="https://twitter.com/Plastiks_io">Plastiks</a>, <a href="https://twitter.com/regen_network">Regen Network</a>,<a href="https://twitter.com/ToucanProtocol"> Toucan Protocol</a>, Wren, <a href="https://twitter.com/allegorylabs">Allegory</a>, Flori, Mento,<a href="https://twitter.com/Open__Earth"> Open Earth Foundation</a>, <a href="https://twitter.com/SimplexDNA">SimplexDNA</a>, <a href="https://twitter.com/SpiralsProtocol">Spirals Protocol</a>, <a href="https://twitter.com/senken_io">Senken</a>, ValuescCO (SocialStack) &amp; <a href="https://twitter.com/thallo_io">Thallo</a>), the initial objective of the CC was about creating a trusted marketplace of high-quality environmental digital assets that bring prosperity to people and the planet.</p><p>With global reach and relevant market cap, the Climate Collective accomplishes this mission both through the efforts of each of its members and collectively, through initiatives such as the Grants system.</p><p>The first wave of grants covered fourteen initiatives (<a href="https://plastiks.io">Plastiks</a>, <a href="https://untangled.finance">Untangle Finance</a>, ReFi Spring, <a href="https://medium.com/@Athena_Protocol">Athena Protocol</a>, <a href="https://www.atem.io">Atem</a>, <a href="https://podcast.refidao.com">ReFi Podcast</a>, <a href="https://www.kernel.community/en/">Kernel</a> (the Regeneration Guild), <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/posts/simplexdna_web3-refi-restoration-activity-6963448528320786432-a3Jd/?originalSubdomain=fr&amp;trk=public_profile_like_view">SimplexDNA</a>, <a href="https://www.thallo.io">Thallo</a>,<a href="https://senken.io"> Senken</a>, <a href="https://www.sequestr.io">Sequestr</a>, <a href="https://mrvcollective.org">MRV Collective</a>,<a href="https://www.socialstack.co/about-socialstack"> Socialstack</a>, and <a href="https://closer.earth">Closer</a>) which after less than one year after receiving the funds, bring together a network of partnerships that encompasses most of the global ReFi ecosystem, and specific ReFi locations.</p><p>The carefully curated first wave covered both the more immediate challenges of raising awareness and educating on Blockchain and regeneration such as Kernel and ReFi Spring, as well as solutions built focusing on a long-term regenerative finance global structure such as Socialstack and Athena Protocol.</p><p>The Climate Collective has also proven an increased impact on the overall ReFi ecosystem on its own development as an organization. Important upgrades range from independent fund management to high-level governance (multisig and beyond) and grants selection process. <br><br>It remains to be seen, the operational and practical effects of such changes, but it has adopted the governance and fund management best practices, something expected of all after the hurtful experiences of crypto 2022 bad examples.</p><p>The next challenge as a community and ecosystem is expanding it beyond the adoption of a niche to a standard practice of crypto, as we initially observe beyond the newly established Social Impact Collective with similar experimentations of Polygon, Ethereum, and Solana foundations.</p><p>The adoption of the best governance practices, together with an agreement about planetary healing and the support for new ReFi initiatives makes Climate Collective the place to go if you want to understand the growth of the ReFi movement in 2022.</p><p><strong>But, what are the expectations of Climate Collective for 2023?</strong></p><p>In the year ahead, the Climate Collective is focused on advancing the use of web3 technology to unlock climate action at scale. They’re doing this in three ways: <strong>First</strong>, they’ll accelerate the adoption and deployment of digital environmental assets (DEAs). <strong>Second</strong>, they will help build trust and credibility for the web3 x climate sector. <strong>And finally</strong>, invest in frameworks and interoperable tech infrastructure that support market-making activities.</p><p>So, now that you understand Climate Collective's mission and its accomplishments you are ready to contribute to this mission. If you have an outstanding idea that you think is able to fit the mission of CC, make sure to contact them using the links below:</p><p><a href="https://twitter.com/clim8collective">https://twitter.com/clim8collective</a><br><a href="https://climatecollective.org/￼￼Finally,">https://climatecollective.org/</a><br></p>
item.excerpt:encoded: The Climate Collective was the first agreement between web3-native initiatives to build, together, the bases for a new digital economy in order to heal the planet.

item.title: The Case for a ReFi Ecosystem between Brazil and Cameroon
item.dc:creator: Marcelo Silva
item.content:encoded: <h3 id="roots-diaspora-and-entrepreneurship"><strong>Roots, Diaspora, and entrepreneurship</strong></h3><p>The global ReFi ecosystem has grown at an incredible speed over the past year. At the same time that the ecosystem gained strength, the narrative that the ideal space for the ReFi, in addition to building incentives for the regeneration of the planet, our local communities also grew.</p><p>Especially the traditional ones that have maintained a harmonious relationship with nature for centuries.</p><p>However, more than being a tool available to these local communities, ReFi can allow the creation of a global network of coordination and cooperation between them.</p><p>If the agents who profit from the planet's destruction organize globally to defend their interests, it is important that the agents who preserve and regenerate our planet do as well.</p><p>In this context, we turn our attention to the initiatives that are already being built with this goal, and one of them is the beginning of coordination between Cameroon and Brazil.</p><p>The countries share a tragic history of looting by Portugal, which in addition to looting the natural riches of the countries, also kidnapped people in one and forced them to work in slavery in the other.</p><p>This tragic proximity makes Brazil and Cameroon share close positions in global indexes such as violence, corruption and a mostly primary economy.</p><p>However, both countries reacted to this tragedy through industrialization and cooperation with each other. One of the most striking facts of this cooperation was the <a href="https://www.diplomaciabusiness.com/balanca-comercial-entre-brasil-e-camaroes-ja-cresceu-quase-20-em-2022/">20% </a>growth<a href="https://www.diplomaciabusiness.com/balanca-comercial-entre-brasil-e-camaroes-ja-cresceu-quase-20-em-2022/"> of the trade balance between the two countries in 2022</a>.</p><p>The recent <a href="http://portal.mec.gov.br/component/content/article/221-noticias/2107596713/2443-sp-1488659651?Itemid=164">scientific cooperation agreement</a> between the countries is also part of this. However, this whole introduction only makes sense when we consider the emergence of the ReFi ecosystem in both countries.</p><p>From this analysis, we will be able to point out what are the bases for the growth of this cooperation to be accelerated to the point that representatives of the ReFi ecosystems of both countries can benefit from an international partnership.</p><p>Our mission here is simple: to find a space of coordination where Brazilian and Cameroonian ReFi Startups can mutually benefit while pursuing their own mission.</p><h4 id="the-potential">The Potential</h4><p>The African continent has the potential to be a significant player in the ReFi ecosystem due to its large and youthful population, rapidly growing economies, and increasing access to technology.</p><p>With a growing tech scene and a government committed to promoting financial innovation, Cameroon is well-positioned to become a hub for ReFi activity in West Africa.</p><p>Cameroon's entrepreneurial ecosystem, particularly its startups focused on climate solutions, will play a crucial role in driving the growth of the ReFi ecosystem in the country.</p><p>Just to name some examples: <a href="https://cassvita.com/">Cassavita</a>, Multi-Tech Sustainable Solutions (who honored the country during the COP27), and others like <a href="https://www.name-recycling.com/">Name Recycling</a>, <a href="http://www.asafe.org/">ASAFE</a>, and <a href="http://thenoncefoundation.org">The NONCE Association</a>, are leveraging technology to create new financial products and services that address challenges faced by communities across the continent.</p><p>At the same time, they are also working to promote financial literacy and increase access to finance for the underbanked and unbanked population.</p><p>In order for this ecosystem to keep its rhythm of growth without losing sight of its mission, it's important to acknowledge the relevance of the indigenous people stewarding forested land.</p><p>On this specific matter, while in Brazil Rede de Sementes do Xingu is coordinating local seed collectors, administrators, and buyers in the state of Mato Grosso, being responsible for the recovery of more than 6,000 hectares.</p><p>In Cameroon, NONCE Association is trying to do the same thing with the creation of a circular economy using a blockchain-backed UBI token.</p><p>This alignment is only one of the several that highlight the fact that it’s time to build a bridge between Brazil and Cameroon, a bridge that will allow radical partnerships and mutual growth where ReFi will be just the catalyst of broader cooperation.</p><p>In Brazil, while the topic of ESG has a strong presence in the Startup and Business environment in general, the limitations of the ESG brand started to spark in the news as fields such as the traditional carbon market started to raise questions about transparency and legitimacy.</p><p>The lack of web2 alternatives to ESG had made a lot of startups move to web3 in search of a better environment to do business, such as the example of the startup <a href="https://nossaterrafirme.com/">Nossa Terra Firme</a>.</p><p>This movement is interesting because it signals a path of migration of startups focused on the Environment to Web3, however, it also points to a probable reduction in the availability of services provided by these startups to their former Web2 customers.</p><p>The relevance of this sign comes from the fact <a href="https://exame.com/esg/investimentos-em-esg-devem-chegar-a-us-53-trilhoes-ate-2025-diz-estudo/">that 74% of business managers and owners rather have information agencies (56%) and suppliers (50%) taking over the initiatives for their companies</a>.</p><p>So, as more companies start to take the climate emergency seriously in Brazil, we’ll have a continental-size country, with a high demand for services and suppliers (related to environmentally friendly solutions) and with a historical link to Africa.</p><p>Cameroon is known as Little Africa, due to the high cultural diversity present in the country, which puts it in a very special place regarding Brazil.</p><p>Then, what's needed in order for climate and impact-driven startups from Cameroon and Brazil to start the coordination?</p><p>We believe that from all the resources, the one with the highest cost right now is the information, that's why we are launching a synchronized event between Cameroon and Brazil, so founders and people with interest can share what would make their mission easier.</p><p>This is just one of the spaces where Brazil and Cameroon can thrive together, just the beginning.</p><p>If you want to be a part of that construction you can start by staying tuned to the work of The Nounce Foundation!</p>
item.excerpt:encoded: The global ReFi ecosystem has grown at an incredible speed over the past year. At the same time, incentives for local regeneration of the planet, also grew.

item.title: The ReFi Ecosystem in Suriname 🇸🇷
item.dc:creator: Marcelo Silva
item.content:encoded: <p><strong><em>Orginally published on Feb 23rd at ReFi Spring Blog from a<strong>uthors:</strong></em></strong><em><br><a href="https://twitter.com/GoudzandT">Tim Goudzand</a> - S</em>urinamese f<em>ounder of Infinitri.io<br><a href="https://twitter.com/MarceloReFi">Marcelo Silva</a> - Community Builder @ ReFi Spring &amp; ReFi DAO<br><a href="https://twitter.com/KaicAnna">Anna Kaic</a> - Marketing lead @ ReFi Spring &amp; ReFi DAO</em></p><p>As the global ReFi ecosystem expands, it takes on new forms, both in terms of the global markets and, more recently, attention to the need to build local references to accelerate the emergence of new ReFi ecosystems.</p><p>These local references have different forms and are integrated into the global movement of ReFi each in their own way, thus, there is still no formula or even general bases that are shared by all these local collectives of agents that are organized around ReFi.</p><p>One of the most relevant values that ReFi Spring delivers to the ecosystem is the opportunity to visualize these communities and join them from a collection of Telegram groups and local events in almost thirty countries.</p><p>However, the next step, the constitution of the local ecosystem, is the result of the work of the community itself in the form of its catalysts (which may be people or organizations).</p><p>These local ecosystems do not arise automatically or impersonally, on the contrary, it arises from people's intention to organize themselves to accelerate the production of solutions using web3 to local challenges.</p><p>In this context, the ecosystems of the Global South have a special weight as they emerge as bridges between agents and organizations from the global north, and local challenges and opportunities in, often, disenfranchised neighbourhoods.</p><p>These bridges are responsible for allowing a safe, non-imperialist, and mutualist approach.</p><p>In this context, South America emerges as a special case due to the abundance of its natural reserves and the recurrent threats to such diversity of riches. This article, however, aims to highlight the conditions for the emergence of a local ReFi ecosystem in a specific South American country which is unique in many different ways.</p><h3 id="the-uniqueness-of-suriname">The Uniqueness of Suriname</h3><p>Suriname is a small but unique country with a rich history, culture, and natural beauty that sets it apart from the rest of the world. There are several factors that make Suriname unique, including its diverse population, its geography, and its biodiversity.</p><p>Suriname, the only Dutch-speaking country in South America, is home to people from a wide range of ethnic, cultural, and linguistic backgrounds. A country home to descendants from all over the world, including indigenous tribes, Africans, Chinese, Javanese, Hindus, Lebanese and Creoles.</p><p>This diverse population has created a unique cultural mosaic in the country, with a rich mix of traditions, languages, and customs. A great example of this is a mosque right next to the synagogue in the heart of our capital city Paramaribo.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/928fde9a-6e99-47e2-b68b-c1fd4a8a5497/Waterkant_Paramaribo_New.jpeg?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1080" height="668"></figure><p>Suriname's geography is equally as unique. The country, part of the Guayana-Suriname basin, is located on the northeastern coast of South America, surrounded by Guyana, French Guiana, Brazil, and the Atlantic Ocean. It is one of the few countries in the world that is located in both the Americas and the Caribbean.</p><p>This unique location provides the country with a rich diversity of ecosystems, including the Amazon rainforest, the coastal mangrove forests, and the Atlantic Ocean. Suriname is one of the most biologically diverse countries in the world, with a rich array of flora and fauna that are found nowhere else on the planet.</p><p>This biodiversity is of utmost importance for the country and the world, as it provides a valuable source of livelihood for the local population, helps maintain the balance of the Earth’s ecosystem, supports scientific research, and attracts tourists from around the world.</p><h3 id="infinitri%E2%80%99s-mission-of-creating-a-local-refi-ecosystem">Infinitri’s mission of creating a local ReFi ecosystem</h3><p>Between the different ESG or green initiatives in Suriname, <a href="https://twitter.com/INFINITRI_IO">Infinitri</a> highlights itself by the use of Web3 to address the challenge of creating incentives to the protection of the forests that covers 92% of the country.</p><p>Blockchain emerged as an alternative to traditional ways due to a set of conditions such as slow rate of national development, fast declining economy and limited access to international financial markets.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><img src="https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1ab2e724bdb47d13cf746/9cc7b879-ce71-4dad-9bd8-b637e2f82bdd/Screenshot+2023-02-23+at+14-29-57+ReFi+Spring+2022+Retrospective+%E2%80%94+ReFi+Spring.png?format=1500w" class="kg-image" alt="Infinitri organizing the first ReFi event in Suriname in 2023" loading="lazy" width="1173" height="661"><figcaption><div class="image-caption"><p style="text-align:center;white-space:pre-wrap;" class=""><em>Infinitri organized the first ReFi event in Suriname in 2022</em></p></div></figcaption></figure><p>Since the first contact with the ReFi ecosystem, Infinitri has sharpened the vision of the relevance of Suriname to the global ReFi ecosystem and has started to prepare the ground for a local ReFi ecosystem in Suriname.</p><p>The first step was the organization of a ReFi event in Paramaribo, the capital of Suriname, where entrepreneurs, scientists, federal authorities, and the local community gathered to learn about ReFi and create links between their projects.</p><p><strong>Now it's time for the next step, the settling of a formal ReFi community in Suriname, aligned around the principles of regeneration, collaboration, and common prosperity.</strong></p><p>This alliance will have the responsibility of nurturing the land for a new generation of startups that will bridge the gap between Web3 and Climate Action in Suriname.</p><p>If you want to know more about it, make sure to connect with the amazing team of <a href="http://infinitri.io/">Infinitri.io</a>.</p><p>This article is a call for the ReFi ecosystem to come to know Suriname and its important place in the world! 🌍 💚</p>

item.title: Announcing the ReFi DAO Local Node Prize! 🎉👏
item.dc:creator: John Dass
Anna Kaic
item.content:encoded: <figure class="kg-card kg-embed-card"><iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/Cag-dJHI9VE?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen title="Announcing the ReFi DAO Local Node Incubator with Commons Stack!"></iframe></figure><p>Today is a special day... on 23.03.23, we have launched ReFi DAO Local Node Prize with our friends at Commons Stack! </p><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="https://mirror.xyz/0x7340F1a1e4e38F43d2FCC85cdb2b764de36B40c0/FABiu5AhpAR6LBLZxlGSfjOrHsHYj2J8VT4QJWPxbpk" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">Read announcement on Mirror</a></div><h2 id="tldr-%F0%9F%93%96">TL;DR 📖</h2><p>As apart of our vision to realize a regenerative economy rooted in local startup communities, we have decided to incubate ReFi Lisboa as the first Local Node in the Global North. </p><p>We are looking for <strong>one city in the <a href="https://worldpopulationreview.com/country-rankings/global-south-countries">Global South</a></strong> to join ReFi Lisboa in the Alpha Cohort of our Local Node Incubator in partnership with <a href="https://twitter.com/commonsstack">Commons Stack</a>.</p><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="https://tally.so/r/3qLB47" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">Apply now</a></div><h2 id="collect-nft-on-mirror-%F0%9F%8E%A8">Collect NFT on Mirror 🎨</h2><p>We are currently crowdfunding for a match funding pool to support Local Nodes. We would be incredibly grateful if you <a href="https://mirror.xyz/0x7340F1a1e4e38F43d2FCC85cdb2b764de36B40c0/FABiu5AhpAR6LBLZxlGSfjOrHsHYj2J8VT4QJWPxbpk">could collect the post on Mirror</a> as a historic NFT and support the emergence of Local Nodes as key onramps for talent and capital into the regenerative economy!</p>
