re-envision is clear. But to what conceptual frameworks and models should we look towards? How should we evolve a new roadmap and whitepaper for ReFi DAO?</p><h2 id="part-4the-rise-of-coordi-nations-%F0%9F%99%8F">Part 4 - The Rise of Coordi-nations... 🙏</h2><p>For the final stage of our workshop we started to explore alternative models for network-state-like organizations, turning our attention to the concept of 'Coordi-nations' - a term recently introduced by <a href="https://cyber.harvard.edu/people/pdefilippi">Primavera de Filippi</a> of <a href="https://blockchaingov.eu/">BlockchainGov</a> and <a href="https://twitter.com/TBSocialist">Josh</a> from the <a href="https://theblockchainsocialist.com/">Blockchain Socialist</a> in their podcast series titled '<a href="https://theblockchainsocialist.com/category/podcast/overthrowing-the-network-state/">Overthrowing the Network State</a>'.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><a href="https://theblockchainsocialist.com/category/podcast/overthrowing-the-network-state/"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/image-18.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1280" height="720" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/07/image-18.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/07/image-18.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/image-18.png 1280w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></a><figcaption><a href="https://theblockchainsocialist.com/category/podcast/overthrowing-the-network-state/">Overthrowing The Network State</a> | <a href="https://theblockchainsocialist.com/">The Blockchain Socialist</a></figcaption></figure><p>Traditional nation-states, tied by geographical boundaries and legacy infrastructures, often fail to keep pace with the rapid transformations ushered in by networked communication and globalization. Their institutional inertia hampers their ability to effectively address increasingly complex global issues. It is here that Coordi-nations come into play as an innovative response to these challenges.</p><p>Coordi-nations offer <strong>a new institutional structure for global cooperation</strong> that leverages the inherent potential of digital communities and modern information technologies to tackle global coordination challenges. </p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-width-wide kg-card-hascaption"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/image-19.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1400" height="786" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/07/image-19.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/07/image-19.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/image-19.png 1400w" sizes="(min-width: 1200px) 1200px"><figcaption><strong><a href="https://jessykate.medium.com/coordi-nations-a-new-institutional-structure-for-global-cooperation-3ef38d6e2cfa">Coordi-nations: A New Institutional Structure for Global Cooperation</a> | <a href="https://cyber.harvard.edu/people/pdefilippi">Primavera de Filippi </a>and <a href="https://cyber.harvard.edu/people/jessy-kate-schingler">Jessy Kate Schingler</a></strong></figcaption></figure><p>What sets Coordi-nations apart from traditional nations, even from the concept of the Network State proposed by Balaji, is their emphasis on voluntary association, shared values, and mutualism rather than territorial limitations. Their sovereignty is carved out in the digital sphere, and grounded in participatory governance and decentralized decision-making. Individuals can be members of multiple Coordi-nations, fostering a rich landscape of co-existing identity.</p><h2 id="forum-conclusion-key-action-points-%F0%9F%8E%AC">Forum Conclusion &amp; Key Action Points 🎬</h2><p>So considering the awesome foundations of Coordi-nations and acting on the collective insights &amp; intelligence generated from this vibrant Forum session - What is next? Here is a summary of the strategically most important next steps for ReFi DAO to address and act upon:</p><ul><li><strong>Reframing the Concept</strong>: There is a clear need to move away from the term 'network state,' which has been identified as potentially problematic due to its inherent and divisive political and ideological implications. Instead, terms like 'coordi-nation,' 'network society,' or 'startup society' are suggested as more fitting. The team needs to steer discussions and actions towards these more cooperative, regenerative, and inclusive terminologies that reflect the essence of what ReFi DAO is actually aiming to build.</li><li><strong>Shifting Focus away from National Sovereignty and Diplomatic Recognition</strong>: Based on the insights and feedback from the session, there seems to be a consensus that striving for national sovereignty and diplomatic recognition might not be the most pragmatic or desirable route for ReFi DAO. The core team needs to shift its focus away from these political objectives towards building on the powerful network organization that ReFi DAO already represents.</li><li><strong>Building on Existing Strengths &amp; be Collaborative</strong>: Rather than seeking to form a sovereign state, ReFi DAO should aim to work as a partner alongside existing nations and institutions, potentially taking on a more integrated political role. Emphasizing the significance of community engagement and local-first approaches, the organization should build a sustainable and distributed value chain that centers on local communities and end-users.</li><li><strong>Facilitate Inclusive Community Dialogue and Effective Governance</strong>: ReFi DAO should continue engaging the community in robust discussions and decision making processes to ensure the actions and outcomes align with the community's needs. Moreover, the organization should further develop clear, fair, efficient and more formalized governance systems which could encompass community proposal systems, community voting, and the potential formation of a ReFi DAO Council or Committee. This evolving organizational and governance design should enable progressive decentralization and empower wider community participation and contributions.</li></ul><p>Overall, the forum was a true testament to the power of collective intelligence and shared passion in action. Although participants represented a broad array of organizations, initiatives and perspectives, from <a href="https://www.refidao.com/community/local">ReFi DAO Nodes</a> and <a href="https://infinitavc.com/">Network State advocates</a>, to <a href="https://crypto-commons.org/">Crypto Commons Association</a> and <a href="https://theblockchainsocialist.com/">The Blockchain Socialist</a>, they were united by a common thread: an unwavering commitment to exploring and shaping the future of decentralized, regenerative systems for a more sustainable and equitable world. Their collective efforts underscore the fact that when diverse minds come together, truly transformative ideas can emerge...</p><h1 id="a-regen-coordi-nation-%F0%9F%92%A1">A Regen Coordi-Nation? 💡</h1><p>How can ReFi DAO maximise it's impact? How can we catalyse and pioneer a new regenerative paradigm. Check out some of the exciting ideas in the works below 👇</p><figure class="kg-card kg-gallery-card kg-width-wide"><div class="kg-gallery-container"><div class="kg-gallery-row"><div ReFi Villages present a compelling solution to change how we live, work, and relate to one another.</div><div class="kg-bookmark-metadata"><img class="kg-bookmark-icon" src="https://mirror-media.imgix.net/publication-images/juOTsjFEhLa_EJH2-yT5B.png?h&#x3D;800&amp;w&#x3D;800" alt=""></div></div><div class="kg-bookmark-thumbnail"><img src="https://mirror-media.imgix.net/nft/UMYsan7npw5Xd2d94sSaD.jpeg?h&#x3D;null&amp;w&#x3D;null&amp;auto&#x3D;compress" alt=""></div></a></figure><p>But we can't do it alone. </p><p>In the midst of a bear market and the <a href="__GHOST_URL__/refi-roundup-2023/">valley of despair</a>: What if instead of adopting scarcity thinking, we embraced a mindset of collaboration and abundance? item.excerpt:encoded: In his controversial book 'The Network State: How To Start a New Country', Balaji Srinivasan set the stage for an engaging clash of ideology & technology. Utilising insights from the ReFi DAO Forum, let's explore this fascinating intersection and imagine a new regenerative paradigm... 🌱

item.title: Backup: To Network State or Not to Network State | ReFi DAO Forum 🗣️
item.dc:creator: Monty Merlin Bryant
item.content:encoded: <p>In the ever-evolving world of Web3 &amp; Crypto, one concept has ignited a firestorm of debate and discussion: <strong>the Network State</strong>. In mid-2022, <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balaji_Srinivasan">Balaji Srinivasan</a> - the controversial thinker, investor, and former CTO of Coinbase - introduced the idea in his book, '<a href="https://thenetworkstate.com/">The Network State: How To Start a New Country</a>'. In this audacious proposition, he sparked widespread intrigue and kindled a movement of communities and entrepreneurs seeking to build this new type of organisation...</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/What-is-a-Network-State--by-Balaji-Srinivasan---ReFi-DAO-1.jpg" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="2000" height="1125" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/07/What-is-a-Network-State--by-Balaji-Srinivasan---ReFi-DAO-1.jpg 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/07/What-is-a-Network-State--by-Balaji-Srinivasan---ReFi-DAO-1.jpg 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2023/07/What-is-a-Network-State--by-Balaji-Srinivasan---ReFi-DAO-1.jpg 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w2400/2023/07/What-is-a-Network-State--by-Balaji-Srinivasan---ReFi-DAO-1.jpg 2400w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"><figcaption><em><a href="https://thenetworkstate.com/the-network-state-in-one-sentence">The Network State in One Sentence</a></em></figcaption></figure><p>Taking this in a new direction, in February 2023 ReFi DAO announced a vision for a network state <strong>as a vehicle for planetary regeneration</strong>. The model imagined a globally dispersed, but deeply connected organization that takes form as a decentralized network of local startup communities with a mission to catalyze both inner and outer regeneration and pioneer a new paradigm. </p><p>The idea was born out of a sobering observation: existing institutions – be they nation-states, corporations, or civil society – have persistently fallen short in tackling the pervasive threats of climate change and other critical challenges of our time. The urgency for a leap in innovation across cultural, social, economic, and technological domains is crystal clear. Driven by this realization, ReFi DAO formulated a mission to bring about <strong>a global regenerative economy</strong>, fostered by a transformative global network of mission aligned local communities.</p><p>Yet, despite its allure, the concept of a network state is not without controversy. It has sparked a captivating ideological and political debate, drawing in a wide diversity of perspectives. What exactly constitutes as a network state? Why has become such a popular meme and what is it that is resonating with so many? And what are the lurking dangers, concerns, risks and critiques?</p><p>In this article, we set out to unravel these questions. Drawing upon the enlightening dialogues from the recent <a href="https://www.refidao.com/community/working-group/ReFi-DAO-Forum/r/recbjJ1Wa9mZXW9JI">ReFi DAO Forum</a>, we will dive deeper into the heart of the network state concept - both its potential and challenges. And from this exploration, we will begin to embark on a journey of discovery and co-creation as we seek to collectively sculpt a new vision for a ReFi DAO powered by and for our community. First, some background... 👇</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-width-wide"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/01.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="2000" height="1125" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/07/01.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/07/01.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2023/07/01.png 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w2400/2023/07/01.png 2400w" sizes="(min-width: 1200px) 1200px"></figure><h1 id="refi-daos-evolving-organisation">ReFi DAO's Evolving Organisation</h1><p>Since January 2021, ReFi DAO has been cultivating an ecosystem with hundreds of founders &amp; investors, an online community of thousands, and many dozens of events across the globe. 🌎 🌍 🌏 In this time, with a small core team at the helm, we have been able to build and iterate rapidly, testing new ideas in a live environment while responding to community feedback. </p><figure class="kg-card kg-gallery-card kg-width-wide"><div class="kg-gallery-container"><div class="kg-gallery-row"><div class="kg-gallery-image"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/35.png" width="2000" height="1125" loading="lazy" alt srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/07/35.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/07/35.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2023/07/35.png 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w2400/2023/07/35.png 2400w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></div><div class="kg-gallery-image"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/ReFi-DAO-Network-State-July-2023.jpg" width="1315" height="1110" loading="lazy" alt srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/07/ReFi-DAO-Network-State-July-2023.jpg 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/07/ReFi-DAO-Network-State-July-2023.jpg 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/ReFi-DAO-Network-State-July-2023.jpg 1315w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></div></div></div></figure><p>But now, the stakes are higher. With a powerful online influence and a growing network of local communities, we've reached beyond our startup roots. We are ready for transformation. We must evolve our organisational structure. We must become a community-first, community-led and community-owned organisation.</p><p>With this is mind, ReFi DAO is seeking to embark on a 12 to 24 months journey towards 'exit-to-community', with ownership and governance rooted in our community. This strategy seeks to distribute wealth and voice across a community rather than concentrating it among a select few, and aims to ensure that the organization is co-owned and co-governed by the communities that fuels it in a way that promotes inclusivity, dynamism, and collective capacity.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-width-wide"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-09-at-3.55.44-pm.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="2000" height="1120" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-09-at-3.55.44-pm.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-09-at-3.55.44-pm.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-09-at-3.55.44-pm.png 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-09-at-3.55.44-pm.png 2260w" sizes="(min-width: 1200px) 1200px"></figure><p>The newly launched <a href="https://www.refidao.com/community/working-group/ReFi-DAO-Forum/r/recbjJ1Wa9mZXW9JI">ReFi DAO Forum</a> aims to act as a vehicle for this transition. We are inviting a diverse network of ReFi DAO stakeholders, alongside leaders from across the Web3, distributed governance, organizational and monetary policy sectors to help shape the vision and trajectory of ReFi DAO. Taking form in monthly <a href="https://www.liberatingstructures.com/">liberating structured</a> workshops, we aim to create space for open discussions, sense-making, and active co-creation, while promoting diversity, inclusivity, and creativity. </p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-width-wide kg-card-hascaption"><a href="https://www.refidao.com/community/working-group/ReFi-DAO-Forum/r/recbjJ1Wa9mZXW9JI"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/49.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="2000" height="1125" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/07/49.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/07/49.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2023/07/49.png 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w2400/2023/07/49.png 2400w" sizes="(min-width: 1200px) 1200px"></a><figcaption><a href="https://www.refidao.com/community/working-group/ReFi-DAO-Forum/r/recbjJ1Wa9mZXW9JI#home-footer0"><strong>Join the ReFi DAO Forum</strong></a></figcaption></figure><p>Guided by principles from Holacracy and Sociocracy, Androgynous Organisations, Distributed Cooperatives (DisCO), Deep Democracy, and more, the Forum will also act as a mechanism for consent-based governance with core ReFi DAO stakeholders, aiming to surface the community's thoughts, ideas, concerns, and tensions regarding ReFi DAO's actions and proposals.</p><p>The <a href="https://lu.ma/refi-dao-forum">first ReFi DAO Forum Meeting</a> kicked off on the 24th May and served as a springboard for the beginning of our community-led sense-making. Among the many insights and action points, there was a wellspring of thoughts and concerns around the idea of Network States, which brought us to our next session...</p><h1 id="to-network-state-or-not-to-network-state">To Network State or not to Network State?</h1><p>Kicking off the second ReFi DAO Forum meeting, a vibrant ensemble of changemakers, innovators, and thinkers from around the globe assembled, each bringing a unique perspective rooted in their diverse cultural backgrounds, professional experiences, and areas of expertise. From Victor Kariuki's work on decentralized science in Kenya, to Mars' redefining of value from London; Timothy Goudzand' ReFi Leadership in Suriname, to Giulio's post-capitalist activism across Austria and Spain; Karla Córdoba-Brenes' transformative work on social currencies in Costa Rica, to Matthieu Hayoz's groundbreaking nature-centric app development in Switzerland. </p><figure class="kg-card kg-gallery-card kg-width-wide kg-card-hascaption"><div class="kg-gallery-container"><div class="kg-gallery-row"><div class="kg-gallery-image"><a href="https://lu.ma/refi-dao-forum-2"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/ReFi-Forum-twitter-post.jpg" width="2000" height="1125" loading="lazy" alt srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/07/ReFi-Forum-twitter-post.jpg 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/07/ReFi-Forum-twitter-post.jpg 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2023/07/ReFi-Forum-twitter-post.jpg 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w2400/2023/07/ReFi-Forum-twitter-post.jpg 2400w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></a></div><div class="kg-gallery-image"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-19-at-4.09.06-pm.png" width="2000" height="926" loading="lazy" alt srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-19-at-4.09.06-pm.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-19-at-4.09.06-pm.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-19-at-4.09.06-pm.png 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w2400/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-19-at-4.09.06-pm.png 2400w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></div></div></div><figcaption><a href="https://lu.ma/refi-dao-forum-2 ">To Network State or not to Network State?</a> | ReFi DAO Forum #2 with 50+ participants...</figcaption></figure><p>Coming together our aim was to delve into the concept of the Network State - its merits, drawbacks, and proposed alternatives - and dissect <a href="https://www.notion.so/refi-dao/ReFi-DAO-Network-State-Initial-Proposal-Hypothesis-Feb16th-2023-920abdb38fb34ca2aeeaae4d1f56c561?pvs=4">ReFi DAOs Initial Network State Proposal &amp; Hypothesis from Feb16th 2023</a>. Let's dive in to some of the key insights and reflections.. But first, what actually is a network state?</p><h2 id="the-short-history-of-network-states">The Short History of Network States...</h2><p>The innovative but controversial conception of a network state was originally coined by <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balaji_Srinivasan">Balaji Srinivasan</a> in mid-2022 within his book, '<a href="https://thenetworkstate.com/">The Network State: How To Start a New Country</a>'. Balaji is a well-known entrepreneur and investor, he is the former CTO of Coinbase, co-founder of Earn.com (acquired by Coinbase), and has served as a board member of Andreessen Horowitz, a renowned venture capital firm.</p><p>As defined by Balaji, he represents a network state as the next evolution from a nation-state. He envisions them starting with the formation of highly-aligned online community that takes root around a strong shared proposition or 'moral innovation'. Subsequently the community goes on to acquire land or 'territory' in various locations, acting more like a decentralized network than a contiguous piece of land. The idea is based on the convergence of digital communities and political entities, evolving from online platforms based on shared propositions into actual physical states. </p><figure class="kg-card href="https://gitbook.jur.io/wiki-network-state/">Jur Network State Wiki</a></strong></figcaption></figure><p>Srinivasan compares network states to cryptocurrency's rise to recognition. Cryptocurrency started with numerical significance, gaining traction through increased use and market capitalization, before obtaining societal significance with acceptance and recognition from existing financial institutions (although this has understandably taken a bit of a knock in recent times!). Similarly, a network state could gain numerical significance (population, land ownership, income) and then strive for societal recognition in the form of diplomatic acknowledgment from existing states.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/image-13.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1280" height="640" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/07/image-13.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/07/image-13.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/image-13.png 1280w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><p>The key innovation that makes network states possible, according to Srinivasan, is existing internet technologies. They allow for the building of massive online communities, the start of billion-dollar digital currencies, and development of comprehensive global governance &amp; coordination architecture, making the concept of such organizations feasible with todays existing technology.</p><p>However. Given it's radical departure from traditional concepts of statehood and nation-building, and the contentious political nature of the concepts covered, Balaji's proposition has sparked widespread discussion and debate. Network states are still just an idea. It is not something that has ever been done before, and many questions and concerns remain. How would existing nation states react to them? Would they ever actually be acknowledged or receive any legitimacy? But regardless of the theoretical feasibility, deeper questions also lurk. Do they represent a new frontier for economic and societal innovation? Or are they an elitist libertarian fantasy with dystopian potential?</p><h2 id="part-1collective-visioning">Part 1 - Collective Visioning</h2><p>Before diving into the nuances of network state, to kick-off the Forum we first looked inwards to collectively imagine the future we want to inhabit and what is blocking us from getting there... Here is synthesis of key ideas shared:</p><p><strong>How do you envision a better future? What does it look like? How might we get there? </strong></p><ul><li><strong>Regeneration and Decentralized Science (DeSci):</strong> Participants imagine a future where regeneration and science play a central role. This extends to digital well-being, land regeneration, and fostering a culture around regenerative ecosystems. Victor Kariuki highlighted the importance of nurturing education in regeneration, science, and web3 technologies. Owen Langham shared his interest in land regeneration and the challenge of including nature in balance sheets.</li><li><strong>Decentralization and Post-Capitalism</strong>: There's a call for a shift from traditional economic systems to alternatives that prioritize values, decentralization, and less monetary focus. This includes rethinking societal organization and incentives (Rica), moving towards a post-capitalist future (Giulio), exploring social currencies and collaborative businesses (Karla Córdoba-Brenes), and seeing the potential of decentralization to enact change swiftly and effectively (Martin).</li><li><strong>Community Involvement and Democracy:</strong> A more democratic society where individuals have a continuous voice, not just during elections, is desired. Daryl Edwards focused on community contributions and meaningful collective action. Giulio envisions a future of solidarity, democracy, beauty, and abundance.</li><li><strong>High-Tech but High-Life:</strong> Several participants voiced support for the solarpunk movement, which combines a positive vision of the future, environmental sustainability, and the use of technology for the common good.</li></ul><figure class="kg-card kg-gallery-card kg-width-wide kg-card-hascaption"><div class="kg-gallery-container"><div class="kg-gallery-row"><div class="kg-gallery-image"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/image-22.png" width="1024" height="1024" democratic, harmonious, conscious, decentralized, innovative, empowering, and inclusive. But what is blocking us from getting there?</p><p><strong>Where and how are current institutions, nation states and global systems failing us?</strong></p><ul><li><strong>Value Misalignment</strong>: Mars highlighted how current systems fail to account for costs externalized to the future and nature, leading to a crisis. There is a lack of value placed on essential resources like clean air, rivers and abundant nature. Monty Merlin also spoke about the need to redesign economic systems, calling for innovations in regenerative finance and the commons.</li><li><strong>Short-term Focus and Externalized Costs</strong>: Daryl Edwards pointed out that institutions fail in long-term planning and valuing future generations. There is also the issue of systemic drive for unsustainable growth, lack of global coordination, and lack of accountability - especially of international agreements.</li><li><strong>Inequality &amp; Exclusivity</strong>: Rica emphasized that current systems are not optimized for everyone and are instead being created by an elite to benefit the elite. These systems often lack local orientation and homogenize groups, voices, and dreams.</li><li><strong>Inadequate Institutions</strong>: Jeremy Akers mentioned how legacy institutions are built for the past and are ill-equipped to deal with the complexities of the modern world. He highlighted problems with centralization, institutional monoculture, and the lack of diversity, representation, and adaptability.</li></ul><p>These points provide an overview of the perceived failures of current systems. They highlight the need for systemic change, decentralization, redefining value, and improved representation and diversity in decision-making processes. The challenge lies in creating systems that can address these issues while remaining resonant and adaptable to the ever-changing complexities of the modern world...</p><h2 id="part-2network-states">Part 2 - Network States...</h2><p>Given the future that is being envisioned and some of the current blockers preventing us from getting there, we then dived into the world of network states to begin evaluating their applicability and dangers as a potential solution... Here is a synthesis of some key ideas shared:</p><p><strong>What are the attractive and exciting ideas surrounding the concept of a network state?</strong></p><ul><li><strong>Voluntary Participation and Mobility</strong>: As Alessandro Palombo and Niklas Anziger emphasized, Network States (NS) enable individuals to participate freely and leave at any moment. This flexibility promotes competition and innovation among different NS models. It also aligns with the idea of "voluntary association" that Joshua Yong mentions.</li><li><strong>Innovation Catalyst Amidst System Failures</strong>: As recognized by John Ellison, Monty, Alessandro Palombo, and Raam, Network States present an opportunity for innovation in governance and institutions, acknowledging current systems' shortcomings. The potential for redefining state organization, fostering legal and regulatory innovation, and experimenting with alternative governance forms are seen as key opportunities offered by NS.</li><li><strong>Value-Driven and Collective Empowerment</strong>: Karla Córdoba Brenes and Rica mention the attractiveness of a state or network built on shared values, rather than geographic location. This sentiment is echoed by Tereza Bízková and Shawn Alimohammadi who highlight the idea of how an aligned community around a shared cause could facilitate collective action, and empower citizens to pioneer new forms of socio-ecological activism while promoting faster deployment and enhanced coordination.</li><li><strong>Environmental Regeneration</strong>: Sandra Ponce de León and John Ellison bring forth the idea of environmental regeneration and harmonious co-existence with the Earth. They suggest NS can play a significant role in this process by crowdfunding nature regeneration projects and redesigning the money system to be more regenerative.</li></ul><p>The overall consensus seems to be that NS offer an opportunity for radical innovation in governance and social organization, fuelled by decentralization, voluntary participation, technological advancements, and community alignment around shared values and goals.</p><p><strong>What are the dangers, concerns, or risks surrounding the concept of a network state?</strong></p><ul><li><strong>Exclusion and Inequality</strong>: Joshua Yong, Tim, Shawn, and Raam articulated concerns that Network States might inadvertently exacerbate socio-economic inequalities through exclusion of certain societal groups, wealth concentration, and accessibility challenges in emerging economies. Coupled with potential cultural, linguistic, and physical barriers, as well as risks of nationalist or anti-foreign bias, these could lead to neo-colonial practices &amp; conflict unless local stakeholders are actively included.</li><li><strong>Conflict and Abuse</strong>: Tereza Bízková, Monty, and Daryl were also concerned about the potential for conflict, both within network states and with existing nation states. They worried about governance issues, extraction, and the potential for network states to replicate problems found in traditional systems. Monty, in particular, highlighted the dangers of creating competitive exit-based states that are likely to further perpetuate dynamics of rivalry and conflict.</li><li><strong>Legitimacy and Recognition:</strong> Sandra Ponce de León, Karla Córdoba Brenes, Giulio, and Martin expressed skepticism about whether network states could ever gain diplomatic recognition or legitimacy. They also questioned the focus on this goal, suggesting that it could be naive and unrealistic.</li><li><strong>Critique of the Underlying Philosophy</strong>: Several respondents including Raam, Claudio, and Monty also expressed doubts about the philosophical underpinnings of network states and the underlying ideology of Balaji. They were skeptical of the focus on exit over engagement, the potential for falling back into extractive dynamics, and the risk of network states being a meme that is propagated by masculine-centric and egotistical elites.</li></ul><p>In general, while the respondents recognized the innovative potential of network states, they also cautioned against rushing into the concept without thoroughly examining its implications and potential risks. They advocated for careful consideration of issues like inequality, exclusion, conflict, and governance, and they emphasized the importance of community, inclusivity, and engagement over the pursuit of independence and diplomatic recognition.</p><h2 id="part-3a-refi-network-state">Part 3 - A ReFi Network State?</h2><p>Now that we had explored both the potential and the concerns around the network state concept, we then embarked on an exercise to collectively scrutinise the <a href="https://www.notion.so/refi-dao/ReFi-DAO-Network-State-Initial-Proposal-Hypothesis-Feb16th-2023-920abdb38fb34ca2aeeaae4d1f56c561?pvs=4">original proposal</a> written in February 2022 to form a ReFi Network State. sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></div></div></div></figure><p>Many vibrant ideas, suggestions, and critiques were shared; and the need to re-define and re-envision the proposal was clear. But to what conceptual frameworks and models should we look towards? How should we evolve a new roadmap and whitepaper for ReFi DAO?</p><h2 id="part-4the-rise-of-coordi-nations">Part 4 - The Rise of Coordi-nations...</h2><p>For the final stage of our workshop we started to explore alternative models for network-state-like organizations, turning our attention to the concept of 'Coordi-nations' - a term recently introduced by <a href="https://cyber.harvard.edu/people/pdefilippi">Primavera de Filippi</a> of <a href="https://blockchaingov.eu/">BlockchainGov</a> and <a href="https://twitter.com/TBSocialist">Josh</a> from the <a href="https://theblockchainsocialist.com/">Blockchain Socialist</a> in their podcast series titled '<a href="https://theblockchainsocialist.com/category/podcast/overthrowing-the-network-state/">Overthrowing the Network State</a>'.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/image-18.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1280" height="720" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/07/image-18.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/07/image-18.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/image-18.png 1280w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><p>Traditional nation-states, tied by geographical boundaries and legacy infrastructures, often fail to keep pace with the rapid transformations ushered in by networked communication and globalization. Their institutional inertia hampers their ability to effectively address increasingly complex global issues. It is here that Coordi-nations come into play as an innovative response to these challenges.</p><p>Coordi-nations offer <strong>a new institutional structure for global cooperation</strong> that leverages the inherent potential of digital communities and modern information technologies to tackle global coordination challenges. </p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-width-wide kg-card-hascaption"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/image-19.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="1400" height="786" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/07/image-19.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/07/image-19.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/image-19.png 1400w" sizes="(min-width: 1200px) 1200px"><figcaption><strong><a href="https://jessykate.medium.com/coordi-nations-a-new-institutional-structure-for-global-cooperation-3ef38d6e2cfa">Coordi-nations: A New Institutional Structure for Global Cooperation</a> | <a href="https://cyber.harvard.edu/people/pdefilippi">Primavera de Filippi </a>and <a href="https://cyber.harvard.edu/people/jessy-kate-schingler">Jessy Kate Schingler</a></strong></figcaption></figure><p>What sets Coordi-nations apart from traditional nations, and even from the concept of the Network State proposed by Balaji Srinivasan, is their emphasis on voluntary association, shared values, and mutualism rather than territorial limitations. Their sovereignty is carved out in the digital sphere, and grounded in participatory governance and decentralized decision-making. Individuals can be members of multiple Coordi-nations, fostering a rich landscape of co-existing identity. 💚</p><h2 id="forum-conclusion-key-action-points">Forum Conclusion &amp; Key Action Points</h2><p>So considering the awesome foundations of Coordi-nations and acting on the collective insights &amp; intelligence generated from this vibrant Forum session, what next? Here is a summary of the strategically most important next steps for ReFi DAO to address and act upon:</p><ul><li><strong>Reframing the Concept</strong>: There is a clear need to move away from the term 'network state,' which has been identified as potentially problematic due to its inherent political and ideological implications. Instead, terms like 'coordi-nation,' 'network society,' or 'startup society' are suggested as more fitting. The team needs to steer discussions and actions towards these more cooperative, regenerative, and inclusive terminologies that reflect the essence of what ReFi DAO is actually aiming to build.</li><li><strong>Shifting Focus away from National Sovereignty and Diplomatic Recognition</strong>: Based on the insights and feedback from the session, there seems to be a consensus that striving for national sovereignty and diplomatic recognition might not be the most pragmatic or desirable route for ReFi DAO. The core team needs to shift its focus away from these political objectives towards building on the powerful network organization that ReFi DAO already represents.</li><li><strong>Building on Existing Strengths</strong>: Rather than seeking to form a separate state, ReFi DAO should aim to work as a partner alongside existing nations and corporations, potentially taking on a intergrated political role. Emphasizing the significance of community engagement and local-first approaches, the organization should build a sustainable and distributed value chain that centers on local communities and end-users.</li><li><strong>Facilitate Inclusive Community Dialogue and Effective Governance</strong>: ReFi DAO should continue engaging the community in robust discussions and decision making procceses to ensure the actions and outcomes align with the community's needs. Moreover, the organization should further develop clear, fair, efficient and more formalized governance systems which could encompass community proposal systems, community voting, and the potential formation of a ReFi DAO Council or Committee. This evolving organizational and governance design should enable progressive decentralization and empower wider community participation and contributions.</li></ul><p>So what does the future hold for ReFi DAO?</p><h1 id="a-regen-coordi-nation-%F0%9F%8C%B1">A Regen Coordi-Nation 🌱</h1><p>How can ReFi DAO maximise it's impact? How can we catalyse and pioneer a new regenerative paradigm. Check out some of the exciting ideas in the works below 👇</p><figure class="kg-card kg-gallery-card kg-width-wide"><div class="kg-gallery-container"><div class="kg-gallery-row"><div item.content:encoded: <p>As part of our mission to support local regeneration using the most advanced technology of our time, we are thrilled to announce the opening of the applications for the ReFi Local Node Beta Cohort + a 20k Gitcoin match funding pool for a Local Node featured round. Wait, what??? 🤯</p><p>In this post, we'll delve into several key points:</p><ul><li>What is the Beta Cohort and who can apply for it?</li><li>What are ReFi DAO Local Nodes?</li><li>What is the ReFi Local Node Gitcoin Featured Round?</li></ul><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="https://tally.so/r/mK5VYM" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">APPLY NOW</a></div><h2 id="local-nodes-regenerating-the-earth-%F0%9F%8C%B1">Local Nodes Regenerating the Earth 🌱</h2><p>Building on the successful launch of the Local Node Alpha Cohort focused on the Global South – which resulted in the formation of 14 impressive new Local Nodes nodes and distributed over $25,000 in funding – we're thrilled to announce that we're expanding our horizons. </p><p>Our forthcoming Local Node Beta Cohort is designed to empower local leaders, providing them with the tools, resources, and guidance necessary to successfully deploy their own ReFi DAO Node. But that's not all - our comprehensive program also includes steps on designing an innovative local node canvas, fundraising strategies, marketing techniques, and governance structures. Join us as we democratize finance and technology, one Local Node at a time. We invite you to be part of this endeavour that blends local action with global impact!</p><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="https://tally.so/r/mK5VYM" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">BECOME A LOCAL NODE</a></div><h2 id="who-can-become-a-local-node">Who can become a Local Node?</h2><p>Through the Local Nodes Beta cohort, we aim to aid the core team of perspective Local Nodes worldwide in crafting a compelling vision of regeneration, raising capital, and launching a Local Node token. This will be utilized to acquire land and other real-world assets for the benefit of local residents and the environment. </p><p>If you're intrigued by the idea of setting up a local node in your city, apply now and we'll get in touch soon. Our focus is to foster the emergence of Local Nodes in key startup cities globally, each with its own token, treasury, and vision of regeneration.</p><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="https://tally.so/r/mK5VYM" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">APPLY NOW</a></div><h2 id="what-is-the-local-node-beta-cohort">What is the Local Node Beta Cohort?</h2><p>The Beta Cohort program will guide the Cohort participants through the entire process of setting up their own Local Node, based on the design patterns of ReFi DAO.</p><p>Local Nodes will collectively gather funds, establish their business model canvas define governance and ultimatly launch a token with a specific mandate to utilize at least 50% or more of the funds raised to acquire land and other real-world assets.</p><p>Local Nodes represent a pivotal element of the community network architecture being probed by ReFi DAO. Nodes signify the basis for global governance with local representation and local sovereignty. </p><h2 id="how-does-it-work-%F0%9F%94%8D">How does it work? 🔍</h2><p>Step 1: If you are devoted to realizing regeneration in a city, <a href="https://tally.so/r/mK5VYM">apply now</a>!</p><p>Step 2: After your submission is reviewed by the ReFi DAO team and current Local Node representatives, you will be invited to draft a Gitcoin GG18 Round grant proposal with the full backing of ReFi DAO.</p><p>Step 3: You will fundraise for your Local Node in the Local Node featured round, supported by the Celo Foundation and Celo Europe with a 20k cUSD match funding pool. </p><p>Step 4: You will be invited to gather your local community through Gitcoin activations station to promote and support the Gitcoin GG18 and donations via Optimism. </p><h2 id="join-the-next-refi-dao-forum">Join the next ReFi DAO Forum!</h2><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/08/image.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="960" height="480" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/08/image.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/08/image.png 960w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><p></p>

item.content:encoded: <p>What's going on ReFi fam? John Ellison here! 👋</p><p>I am super excited to announce the ReFi Local Node Beta Cohort with a $30k cUSD match funding pool on Gitcoin GG18 thanks to the generosity of <a href="https://celo.org/">Celo</a>, <a href="https://twitter.com/CeloEurope">Celo Europe DAO</a> and <a href="https://twitter.com/KnktDAO">KNKT DAO</a>! 🌎🌍🌏</p><p>Our mission is to build a global regenerative economy rooted in local startup communities around the world. Local Nodes are the key element in this system.</p><p> Join us by starting a Local Node in your city!</p><p><strong>Extended deadline:</strong> Aug 24th<br><strong>Apply now:</strong> <a href="https://tally.so/r/mK5VYM">ReFi DAO Local Node Beta Cohort | Application Form</a><br><strong>View round on Gitcoin:</strong> <a href="https://explorer.gitcoin.co/#/round/10/0x10be322de44389ded49c0b2b73d8c3a1e3b6d871">ReFi DAO Local Node GG18</a></p><div class="kg-card kg-callout-card kg-callout-card-grey"><div class="kg-callout-emoji">👉🏻</div><div class="kg-callout-text"><a href="https://celo.org/">Celo</a> is the carbon-negative, mobile-first, EVM-compatible blockchain ecosystem leading a thriving new digital economy for all.</div></div><p>In this post, we'll cover:</p><ul><li>What is the Beta Cohort and who is it for?</li><li>What is the ReFi Local Node Gitcoin Featured Round on GG18?</li><li>How does it work?</li><li>How much time does it take?</li><li>Why would I want to do this?</li><li>What are Local Nodes?</li></ul><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="https://tally.so/r/mK5VYM" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">APPLY NOW</a></div><h2 id="what-is-the-refi-local-node-beta-cohort-%F0%9F%A4%94">What is the ReFi Local Node Beta Cohort? 🤔</h2><p>The ReFi Local Node Beta Cohort is a three-month program where a global network of local regenerative leaders gather online once a month to support each other through hosting regular events, building community and onboarding talent and capital into the regenerative economy.</p><p>We also support founders within Local Nodes through sharing insights, making introductions and <a href="https://www.refidao.com/submit-pitch">supporting deal flow</a> across our growing grant funding and investor network. We want to help founders build through the bear and prepare to take advantage of the next cycle. </p><p>If you're an experienced entrepreneur with a committed, long-term vision of regeneration in a specific city please do <a href="https://tally.so/r/mK5VYM">apply to join the program</a> and gain access to the $30k cUSD match funding pool on Gitcoin GG18! Graduates from the ReFi Local Node round on GG18 will be invited to the monthly Beta Cohort.</p><h3 id="existing-local-node-leaders-%F0%9F%8C%9F">Existing Local Node leaders 🌟</h3><p>If you're a leader of an existing local node, you need to submit a '<a href="https://tally.so/r/nG9zJo">Proof of Impact' form</a> in order to be eligible for the $30k cUSD Local Node round on Gitcoin GG18 and the subsequent Beta Cohort. Responses will be reviewed by a council comprised of local node leaders and community members.</p><p>We're looking to support Local Nodes who can demonstrate a clear ROI through hosting regular events and onboarding talent and capital into regeneration via web3. </p><h2 id="what-is-the-refi-local-node-gitcoin-featured-round-on-gg18">What is the ReFi Local Node Gitcoin Featured Round on GG18? </h2><p>This is a two-week fundraising party to help get your local node cash so you can build a team, host regular events and co-create a vision of regeneration in your city. It's run on a platform called <a href="https://gitcoin.co/">Gitcoin</a> which has supported over 3,700 projects to raise over $50M in 5 years.</p><p>You'll need an Ethereum wallet like <a href="https://metamask.io/">Metamask</a> and a basic knowledge of web3 applications.</p><p><strong>Start: </strong>August 15 2023<br><strong>End</strong>: August 29, 2023</p><p><strong>Chain</strong>: Optimism</p><p><strong>Critiera: </strong></p><ol><li>'Accepted' first-time Local Node Applicants (<a href="https://tally.so/r/mK5VYM">APPLY NOW</a>)</li><li>Returning Local Nodes with Proof of Impact (<a href="https://tally.so/r/nG9zJo">PROVE IMPACT</a>)</li></ol><h3 id="what-are-the-eligibility-criteria-%F0%9F%93%8B">What are the eligibility criteria? 📋</h3><p>Successful applications will fulfill the following criteria:</p><ol><li>Be led by two or more experienced founders</li><li>Founders must make a 3-5 year commitment to regeneration in their city</li><li>Demonstrate a clear and compelling vision for regenerating their city</li><li>Be able to identify key local leaders across public, private, and third sectors</li><li>Be able to gather support from advisors across web3, climate, and social justice</li><li>Demonstrate event organizing and community building competence</li></ol><p>Nodes are not designed to be led by a single person or project. They are designed to bring multiple stakeholders together and foster cross-sector collaboration with local regeneration as the common goal.</p><h2 id="what-are-local-nodes-%F0%9F%97%BA">What are Local Nodes? 🗺</h2><p>Local Nodes are local startup communities working towards a shared vision of regeneration. They are led by entrepreneurs but are a cross-pollination of public, private and third sector leaders.</p><p>The first function of local nodes is to host monthly events to onboard talent and capital into the regenerative economy via web3 rails. Through these events, we invite nodes to co-create a vision of regeneration in their city and work towards developing open source software and land-based regenerative projects.</p><p>Local nodes are invited to contribute a voluntary portion of their revenue as a reciprocation for all the services ReFi DAO provides: grant capital, ecosystem development, content creation and software. The intention is to create a peer-to-peer global network where ReFi DAO exists to serve Local Nodes who reflect the value they received through voluntary contributions.</p><p>Our long-term vision is to build a mobile-first '<a href="https://classpass.com/">classpass</a> for regeneration' that enables local nodes to cultivate a prosperous regenerative society in their city that leverages membership fees to provide various streams of funding to support regenerative economic development.</p><h2 id="how-does-it-work-%F0%9F%94%8D">How does it work? 🔍</h2><p><strong><strong>Step 1:</strong></strong> If you are an experienced entrepreneur committed co-creating a vision regeneration in your city, <a href="https://tally.so/r/mK5VYM">apply now</a>!*</p><p><em>*If you're not a startup founder, but you're a great community builder, you can still apply and gather a co-founding team through your events!</em></p><p><a href="https://www.notion.so/refi-dao/3ebdc74145684b8bb04cdc0a6dfa969c?v=51ae31f19c78464e86b446c5aae2825d">Look at the other applications and their progress</a></p><p><strong><strong>Step 2:</strong></strong> Your submission will be reviewed by our governance council and you will be given an applications status: 'Approved', 'Conditional Approval', or 'Denied'.</p><p><strong><strong>Step 3</strong></strong>. We will invite all 'Approved' applications to draft a Gitcoin GG18 grant based upon your application. We recommend using unique branding that resembles ReFi DAO but is clearly an independent, autonomous local organization.</p><p><strong><strong>Step 4:</strong></strong> You will have the opportunity to fundraise for your Local Node in the <strong><strong>Gitcoin </strong>GG18 grant round</strong> from August 15-29 and galvanize your local community by hosting in-person and online events to raise money.</p><p><strong>Optional</strong>: You can host online and in-person activation stations to onboard people onto Optimism and Gitcoin, with a big opportunity for retroactive public goods funding from Optimism!</p><p><strong><strong>Step 5:</strong></strong> All nodes that actively participate in the GG18 round will be invited to participate in the Beta Cohort!</p><h2 id="how-much-time-does-it-take-%E2%8F%B1">How much time does it take? ⏱</h2><p>We get it. Founders are busy. You need to know what to expect.</p><p>Here's a rough breakdown of the core activities assuming you're proficient in using AI tools like ChatGPT and Midjourney. If not, you can come and learn them with us!</p><ul><li><strong>Drafting an application:</strong> 25 mins</li><li><strong>Create social media profiles</strong>: 25 mins</li><li><strong>Draft a Gitcoin grant:</strong> 25 mins</li><li><strong>Fundraise on Gitcoin</strong>: 1 hour / day for 10 working days*</li></ul><p>*Fundraising on Gitcoin can be exhausting, but also has diminishing returns. We recommend a steady, consistent pace with a focus on the first three days of the round (Aug 15-18) and the last three days (Aug 27-29)</p><h2 id="why-would-i-want-to-do-this-%F0%9F%99%8B%F0%9F%8F%BC">Why would I want to do this? 🙋🏼</h2><p>There are a number of reasons why any founder would want to build a local node. As an experienced entrepreneur who has built many ventures all around the world, I can share from my personal experience, there are a number of core motivations:</p><ol><li>IRL friendships rock 🤘</li><li>IRL events open doors to powerful institutions 🏦</li><li>Our online community has got your back 👏</li><li>Access to funding and influential leaders 💰</li><li>Effective content distribution and discovery 𝌞</li></ol><p>Building a startup is hard. Don't go it alone! </p><p>Build a small local events and community team in your city to create a powerful local network moving towards a regenerative future!</p><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="https://tally.so/r/mK5VYM" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">BECOME A LOCAL NODE</a></div><h2 id="our-theory-of-change-%F0%9F%8C%B1">Our theory of change 🌱</h2><p>We believe that in order to solve the complex web of existential crises we face, we need new global coordination vehicles. The nation state and corporation have caused this crisis and have proven they cannot get us out of it...</p><p>That's why we're building a network of local startup communities all over the world that are meet regularly in key cities to co-create a local vision of regeneration while onboarding talent and capital into the regenerative economy via web3 rails like <a href="https://celo.org/">Celo</a>.</p><p>Last quarter we supported the formation of 14 local nodes (85% in emerging markets) with over $30k of grant funding via Gitcoin.</p><p>Our forthcoming Local Node Beta Cohort is designed to empower local leaders, providing them with the tools, resources, and guidance necessary to successfully deploy their own ReFi DAO Node. But that's not all - our comprehensive program also includes steps on designing an innovative local node canvas, fundraising strategies, marketing techniques, and governance structures. Join us as we democratize finance and technology, one Local Node at a time. We invite you to be part of this endeavour that blends local action with global impact!</p><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="https://tally.so/r/mK5VYM" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">APPLY NOW</a></div><h2 id="join-the-next-refi-dao-forum">Join the next ReFi DAO Forum!</h2><p>If you're a local node leader interested in co-creating the governance layer for the formation and support of local nodes, come join us at our upcoming <a href="https://lu.ma/home">Local Node Summit</a> and Forum! You'll get a chance to meet other node leaders, inform governance parameters and explore collaboration opportunities across the network.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><a href="https://lu.ma/refi-dao-forum3"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/08/image.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="960" height="480" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/08/image.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/08/image.png 960w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></a></figure><p></p>

item.content:encoded: <p>Hey, ReFi Nation!</p><p>We're thrilled to bring you an exciting bonus episode of our podcast - "<a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mHtsMVX4sgo&amp;t=2798s">To Network State or Not to Network State</a>" with <a href="https://twitter.com/MontyMerlin">Monty Merlin</a>. In this special episode, we delve deep into the world of regeneration, Web3 technology, and the potential of a network state. Join us as we discuss the mission and vision of ReFi DAO and the broader movement for positive change. </p><p>You can <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mHtsMVX4sgo">watch</a> or <a Collaboration</h2><p>The discussion evolves to the importance of collaboration and building bridges between various networks and communities. They explore the value of pluralism in designing solutions and how diverse communities can contribute to a common goal. Monty unveils exciting plans for cross-network collaboration and shared initiatives that will empower individuals to make a real impact, regardless of their level of familiarity with the Web3 space.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-embed-card"><iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/zwdXxA1T96Q?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen title="A network of coordiNATIONs — an evolution of Balaji&#39;s Network State concept"></iframe></figure><figure class="kg-card kg-embed-card"><iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/SguHnbLnlGA?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen title="Local Regeneration Enabled by Web3 #regeneration #refi #crypto #climateaction"></iframe></figure><h2 id="part-4-building-for-the-future">Part 4: Building for the Future</h2><p>As the conversation comes to a close, Monty and John share their visions for the future. They discuss the necessity of building strong foundations, both in terms of technology and community, especially during bear markets. They stress the significance of storytelling in driving attention and engagement within the Web3 movement. With an optimistic outlook, they invite listeners to join the movement, participate in events, and contribute to the shared vision of regeneration and positive change!</p><figure class="kg-card kg-gallery-card kg-width-wide"><div class="kg-gallery-container"><div class="kg-gallery-row"><div class="kg-gallery-image"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/08/Regen-CoordiNATION---ReFi-DAO.png" width="1838" height="1032" loading="lazy" alt srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/08/Regen-CoordiNATION---ReFi-DAO.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/08/Regen-CoordiNATION---ReFi-DAO.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2023/08/Regen-CoordiNATION---ReFi-DAO.png 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/08/Regen-CoordiNATION---ReFi-DAO.png 1838w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></div><div class="kg-gallery-image"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/08/ReFi-DAO---Regenerate-the-entire-economy.png" width="1802" height="1050" loading="lazy" alt srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/08/ReFi-DAO---Regenerate-the-entire-economy.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/08/ReFi-DAO---Regenerate-the-entire-economy.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2023/08/ReFi-DAO---Regenerate-the-entire-economy.png 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/08/ReFi-DAO---Regenerate-the-entire-economy.png 1802w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></div></div></div></figure><h2 id="check-the-full-episode-below-and-join-the-conversation-%F0%9F%91%87">Check the full episode below and join the conversation! Utilising insights from the ReFi DAO Forum, let’s explore this fascinating intersection and imagine a new regenerative paradigm... 🌱</div><div class="kg-bookmark-metadata"><img class="kg-bookmark-icon" src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w256h256/2022/12/6319c4c1d0b248c635dc4002_ReFi-DAO.png" alt=""><span class="kg-bookmark-author">ReFi DAO</span><span class="kg-bookmark-publisher">Monty Merlin Bryant</span></div></div><div class="kg-bookmark-thumbnail"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/ReFi-DAO-Forum---To-Network-State-or-Not-to-Network-State-2-2.jpg" alt=""></div></a></figure><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="https://youtu.be/mHtsMVX4sgo " class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">Read</a></div><p>We would love to hear what you think! Be part of the conversation, share your thoughts, and engage with us as we navigate the path to a regenerative future. Tune in to "To Network State or Not to Network State" and discover the exciting possibilities that lie ahead in the world of Web3 and positive change! Thank you 🙏</p><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="https://ctt.ac/U6c22" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">Share on Twitter</a></div><figure class="kg-card kg-gallery-card kg-width-wide"><div class="kg-gallery-container"><div class="kg-gallery-row"><div class="kg-gallery-image"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-19-at-2.23.45-pm.png" width="2000" height="1121" loading="lazy" alt srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-19-at-2.23.45-pm.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-19-at-2.23.45-pm.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-19-at-2.23.45-pm.png 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-19-at-2.23.45-pm.png 2198w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></div><div class="kg-gallery-image"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-19-at-2.24.06-pm.png" width="2000" height="1132" loading="lazy" alt srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-19-at-2.24.06-pm.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-19-at-2.24.06-pm.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-19-at-2.24.06-pm.png 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/07/Screenshot-2023-07-19-at-2.24.06-pm.png 2198w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></div></div></div></figure>

item.title: Unveiling Season 3: A Journey Into Regenerative Finance and Impact Web3 | ReFi Podcast
item.dc:creator: Lee Rael
item.content:encoded: <p></p><p>Hey, ReFi Nation!</p><p>We're gearing up for the highly anticipated launch of Season 3 of the ReFi Podcast! As the world continues to grapple with complex challenges, we're diving deeper into the realms of regenerative finance, technology, and positive impact. With support from ClimateCollectv and CeloOrg, this season promises to be a transformative exploration of how decentralized technology and mission-driven communities intersect to shape a regenerative future.</p><p>What to Expect:</p><p>In Season 3, we're delving into the heart of regenerative economics, showcasing the symbiotic relationship between technology and sustainability. Join us for a series of enlightening conversations, interviews, and insights that highlight the immense potential of impact-driven Web3 initiatives. Here's a sneak peek of what you can anticipate:</p><p>1. Regenerative Finance Unveiled:</p><p>Prepare to uncover the possibilities of regenerative economics, where innovation meets social impact. From decentralized financial protocols to emerging VC funds, we'll be exploring how financial systems can be harnessed to drive positive change on a global scale.</p><p>2. Thought Leaders and Visionaries:</p><p>Our podcast will feature thought leaders, regenerative pioneers, and technology visionaries who are at the forefront of reshaping industries. Get ready to gain insights from those who are weaving the fabric of a more sustainable and equitable future.</p><p>3. Community Spotlight:</p><p>Local communities are piloting regenerative economics, and we're shining a spotlight on their efforts. Discover how these grassroots movements are making an impact and driving change at the ground level.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/08/Screenshot-2023-08-29-at-11.54.36.png" class="kg-image" alt loading="lazy" width="795" height="609" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2023/08/Screenshot-2023-08-29-at-11.54.36.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2023/08/Screenshot-2023-08-29-at-11.54.36.png 795w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><p>4. Impact Web3 Fusion:</p><p>The fusion of technology and positive impact is a central theme in Season 3. Explore the ways in which decentralized networks are catalyzing social change and empowering communities worldwide.</p><p>5. Monty Merlin's Welcome:</p><p>To kick off the season, we're thrilled to bring you an engaging conversation with Monty Merlin. This episode will set the tone for a journey of exploration and transformation, as we delve into the possibilities of regenerative finance, new governance models and Web3.</p><p>How to Join:</p><p>Mark your calendars for September 5th, the official launch date of Season 3. Tune in to our podcast for riveting discussions that will reshape your perspective on the intersection of technology, finance, and impact. Whether you're a seasoned industry expert or a curious listener, there's something for everyone in this season.</p><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="bit.ly/3ElBV00" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">Join Our Community</a></div><p>Stay Engaged:</p><p>To make sure you don't miss a single episode, subscribe to the ReFi Podcast on your favorite podcast platform. Be sure to follow us on social media (twitter for updates, behind-the-scenes insights, and opportunities to engage with the regenerative finance community.</p><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="bit.ly/3QYP7zN" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">Watch now on YouTube</a></div><figure class="kg-card kg-embed-card"><iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/Uv0ZfQ7vOp4?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen title="Refi Podcast S3 TRAILER"></iframe></figure><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="bit.ly/45s4Vzr" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">Listen on Spotify</a></div><p>Conclusion:</p><p>As we prepare to embark on this transformative journey, we invite you to join us in exploring the infinite possibilities of regenerative finance and impact Web3. This season promises to be a powerful blend of inspiration, education, and action – driving us all towards a more sustainable and interconnected world. Get ready to dive into the heart of regenerative finance, one episode at a time.</p>
