item.title: Combating Plastic Waste In Nigeria with Web3 🚯
item.dc:creator: Adaeze Okafor
item.content:encoded: <p><em>Nigeria faces a severe plastic waste crisis, contributing to environmental degradation and health risks. The challenges are exacerbated by inadequate infrastructure, illegal dumping, and rising urbanization. In this article </em><a href="https://x.com/Aida_Regen" rel="noreferrer"><em>Adaeze </em></a><em>explores the transformative power of Web3 and regenerative finance (ReFi) in solving these issues.</em></p><div class="kg-card kg-callout-card kg-callout-card-blue"><div class="kg-callout-emoji">🖐️</div><div class="kg-callout-text">Support the authors of this post from <a href="https://explorer.gitcoin.co/?ref=blog.refidao.com#/round/42220/14/10" rel="noreferrer">ReFi Lagos</a> in the current Gitcoin <a href="https://explorer.gitcoin.co/?ref=blog.refidao.com#/round/42220/14"><u>Regen Cordi-Nation Genesis Round</u></a>. Thank you!</div></div><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-5-1-1.png" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="960" height="469" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/08/image-5-1-1.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-5-1-1.png 960w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"><figcaption><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Source: </span><a href="https://punchng.com/waste-management-and-flood-control-in-lagos/" rel="noreferrer"><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Punchng.com</span></a></figcaption></figure><h2 id="a-global-challenge">A Global Challenge</h2><p>The impact of&nbsp;<a href="https://www.green-sail.com/blog/how-does-poor-waste-management-affect-the-climate-change-crisis" rel="noopener ugc nofollow">climate change</a>&nbsp;on our environment is profound and far-reaching, affecting every aspect of our lives. Rising global temperatures and increasingly erratic weather patterns are leading to more frequent and severe natural disasters, affecting food security, water resources, and public health. Plastic pollution exacerbates the effects of climate change by contributing to flooding, harming wildlife, and posing significant health risks to communities. Due to&nbsp;growing urbanization and increasing usage of plastics, managing these synthetic materials has become a global challenge. The breakdown of these larger plastic items into microplastics further complicates the issue, as these tiny particles can be ingested by marine and terrestrial animals, eventually finding their way into human food and water supplies.&nbsp;<a href="https://ourworldindata.org/plastic-pollution#introduction" rel="noopener ugc nofollow">Globally, over 450 million tons of plastic waste are generated each year.</a></p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-8.png" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="1400" height="989" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/08/image-8.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2024/08/image-8.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-8.png 1400w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><p><a href="https://www.globalplasticaction.org/nigeria" rel="noreferrer">Nigeria</a> is no exception. With<a href="https://nesgroup.org/download_resource_documents/NRFP%20Policy%20Brief-%20Dr%20Theresa%20&amp;%20Peter%20Agada%20Ali_1701187431.pdf"><strong><u> over 200 million people </u></strong></a>and a growing urbanization, the country faces significant challenges in managing plastic waste. Nigeria ranks ninth among countries with the highest contributions to plastic pollution, producing over 2.5 million tons of plastic waste annually. Unfortunately, more than 88% of plastic waste created in Nigeria is not recycled. The most prevalent single-use plastics we encounter daily are food and beverage packaging.&nbsp;</p><p><a href="https://ourworldindata.org/plastic-pollution#introduction" rel="noopener ugc nofollow"></a></p><h2 id="environmental-and-health-impacts-of-plastic-waste">Environmental and Health Impacts of Plastic Waste</h2><p>Landfills are often overlooked, representing more than mere heaps of rubbish; they are major sources of harmful gases that exacerbate climate change. Daily, tons of household waste are deposited into landfills. Within these sites, a variety of discarded food, plastics, and other debris undergo a decomposition process that releases gases. According to a World Bank report, solid waste management accounted for approximately<a href="https://datatopics.worldbank.org/what-a-waste/trends_in_solid_waste_management.html" rel="noopener ugc nofollow"><u>&nbsp;</u>five percent of global emissions<u>&nbsp;</u></a>with methane emission being a key contributor, While the majority of oceanic plastic waste originates from land-based activities, an estimated&nbsp;<a href="https://www.rts.com/blog/plastic-pollution-in-the-ocean-facts-and-statistics/" rel="noopener ugc nofollow">75 to 199 million tons<u>&nbsp;</u></a> are already present in marine environments. Studies suggest that tourist activities are the primary source of microplastics on most beaches in Lagos, Nigeria.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-10-1.png" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="640" height="383" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/08/image-10-1.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-10-1.png 640w"><figcaption><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Source: </span><a href="https://punchng.com/waste-management-and-flood-control-in-lagos/" rel="noreferrer"><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Punchng.com</span></a></figcaption></figure><h2 id="problem-worth-solving-indiscriminate-waste-disposal"><strong>Problem Worth Solving: Indiscriminate Waste Disposal</strong></h2><p><a href="https://medium.com/@ThistlePraxis/igniting-waste-management-culture-in-nigeria-738d279c3fc8" rel="noopener">Improper waste disposal</a>&nbsp;is a significant issue in Nigerian cities, impacting public health, the environment, and urban aesthetics. Despite efforts to manage waste, several challenges hinder effective waste handling. One of the primary challenges is the inadequate waste management infrastructure. Many cities in Nigeria lack sufficient facilities for proper waste collection, recycling, and disposal, leading to waste being discarded illegally in open spaces, waterways, and streets. Coupled with this is the issue of insufficient funding. Waste management systems are frequently underfunded, restricting the state's capacity to effectively fight illegal dumping and preserve cleanliness. A significant factor that also contributes to illegal dumping is the lack of public awareness about its environmental and health impacts. Education and awareness campaigns are not widespread or effective enough to change public behavior. As a result, many individuals end up burning their waste thereby releasing harmful pollutants into the air, contributing to air pollution and posing serious health risks to residents, especially children and the elderly.</p><p>Addressing these challenges involves investing in modern waste management facilities, promoting public-private partnerships, and exploring decentralised climate solutions.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><a href="https://x.com/Afrilearn1/status/1802731892191412259"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-11-1-1.png" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="700" height="617" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/08/image-11-1-1.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-11-1-1.png 700w"></a><figcaption><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Source:</span><a href="https://x.com/Afrilearn1/status/1802731892191412259" rel="noreferrer"><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;"> AfriLearn1 X spaces</span></a></figcaption></figure><h2 id="the-rise-of-circular-and-regenerative-economy"><strong>The Rise of Circular and Regenerative Economy</strong></h2><p>For decades, our global economy followed a linear trajectory, extracting raw materials, producing goods, and disposing of them once their usefulness has expired. This linear approach, while fostering economic growth, led to mountains of waste and the depletion of finite resources. A circular economy envisions a regenerative cycle where resources are used, reused, and regenerated. It promotes designing products for longevity, repairing and refurbishing, recycling materials, and ultimately reducing waste.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-12.png" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="500" height="290"><figcaption><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Source: </span><a href="https://www.repsol.com/en/sustainability/sustainability-pillars/environment/circular-economy/index.cshtml" rel="noreferrer"><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Repsol</span></a></figcaption></figure><p>Innovations have emerged as pivotal solutions to address the growing challenge of plastic waste. &nbsp;<a href="https://www.plastiks.io/"><u>Plastiks</u></a>, a Web3 initiative, offers a reward system that ensures plastic waste is properly recovered and recycled. Plastiks also certifies that plastic waste is collected and recycled according to stringent standards. Using blockchain technology, all transactions and verifications are recorded on-chain, ensuring full transparency and trust. Funds from plastic credit sales are used to improve recovery infrastructure, provide fair wages, and support community projects.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-18.png" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="1200" height="677" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/08/image-18.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2024/08/image-18.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-18.png 1200w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><h1 id="unlocking-climate-finance-with-web3-and-refi">Unlocking Climate Finance With Web3 and ReFi</h1><p>In recent years, the world has witnessed an alarming increase in climate-related disasters, underscoring the urgent need for effective climate action. However, despite the growing recognition of the climate crisis, traditional climate finance mechanisms have struggled to keep pace with the scale of the problem. According to a&nbsp;<a href="https://blogs.afdb.org/a-race-against-time/post/climate-change-interventions-in-africa-applying-a-gender-lens-18464?ref=blog.refidao.com" rel="noopener ugc nofollow">report</a>&nbsp;by the&nbsp;<a href="http://www.afdb.com/?ref=blog.refidao.com" rel="noopener ugc nofollow">African Development Bank</a>, the total cost of adapting to climate change in the continent is estimated to be between US$20 billion and US$30 billion per year. However, the actual amount of finance currently being provided for climate change adaptation and mitigation initiatives in the region is far below this estimate.</p><p><a href="https://blog.toucan.earth/what-is-refi-regenerative-finance/" rel="noopener ugc nofollow">Regenerative finance (ReFi)</a>&nbsp;— a decentralized finance built on&nbsp;<a href="https://www.ey.com/en_gl/insights/climate-change-sustainability-services/regenerative-principles-sustainable-future" rel="noopener ugc nofollow">regenerative principles</a>- plays a pivotal role in scaling climate finance by supporting projects and businesses that prioritize resource efficiency, waste reduction, and societal regeneration. Web3 grant platforms such as&nbsp;<a href="https://www.gitcoin.co/" rel="noopener ugc nofollow">Gitcoin</a>&nbsp;and&nbsp;<a href="https://giveth.io/" rel="noopener ugc nofollow">Giveth</a>&nbsp;allocate funds to climate solutions and sustainable businesses working to reduce waste. These financial innovations promote <a href="https://scholar.harvard.edu/files/hitzig/files/buterin_hitzig_weyl_draft.pdf"><u>public goods funding</u></a> and&nbsp; <a href="https://greenpill.network/pdf/onchain-capital-allocation.pdf"><u>on-chain capital allocation</u></a> mechanisms such as <a href="https://www.wtfisqf.com/"><u>quadratic funding (QF)</u></a>. On-chain capital allocation offers transparency, efficiency, and democratization, challenging traditional finance and scalability issues. Gitcoin grant has facilitated the distribution of <a href="https://www.gitcoin.co/blog/gg20-reflections-insights-and-future-plans"><u>more than $60 million</u></a> to public goods in the Ethereum ecosystem</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card kg-card-hascaption"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-13.png" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="1100" height="777" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/08/image-13.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2024/08/image-13.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-13.png 1100w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"><figcaption><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Source:&nbsp;</span><a href="https://www.planet3r.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener ugc nofollow"><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Planet 3R</span></a><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">&nbsp;— each of these bags were made from&nbsp;</span><a href="https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2021/3/18/from-trash-to-treasure-how-nigerians-recycle-waste-into-wealth" target="_blank" rel="noopener ugc nofollow"><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">250 used water sachets (plastics)</span></a></figcaption></figure><h2 id="exploring-opportunities-and-use-cases-in-nigeria"><strong>Exploring Opportunities and Use Cases in Nigeria</strong></h2><p>Plastic waste recycling is&nbsp;<a href="https://www.howwemadeitinafrica.com/an-opportunity-worth-millions-exporting-lagos-plastic-waste/143447/" rel="noopener ugc nofollow">10 billion dollar market in Nigeria</a>. According to a&nbsp;<a href="https://www.ellenmacarthurfoundation.org/the-new-plastics-economy-rethinking-the-future-of-plastics" rel="noopener ugc nofollow">report,<u>&nbsp;</u></a>studies show that only 14% of plastics are collected and recycled. Unfortunately, over&nbsp;<a href="https://gca.org/how-one-nigerian-enterprise-is-tackling-the-global-plastic-plague-one-shoe-at-a-time/" rel="noopener ugc nofollow">90%<u>&nbsp;</u></a>of the plastic waste generated in Nigeria is not recycled. Instead, much of it ends up in water bodies — rivers, lakes, drains, lagoons and the ocean. Here are some innovative startup tackling plastics pollution in Nigeria:</p><ul><li><a href="https://twitter.com/Planet3r" rel="noopener ugc nofollow">Planet 3R</a>&nbsp;is a social enterprise in Oyo, converting textile and plastic wastes into eco-friendly products using the 3R ( Reduce, Reuse, Recycle)</li><li><a href="https://www.wecyclers.com/about" rel="noopener ugc nofollow">Wecyclers</a>&nbsp;is a social enterprise in Lagos incentivizing low-income communities to recycle their waste. In return, participants earn points that can be exchanged for essential goods and services.</li><li><a href="https://thewastemuseum.com/"><u>Waste Museum</u></a>, the first of its kind in Africa, is dedicated to transforming waste into wealth. The Waste Museum recycles discarded materials and converts them into marketable products.</li></ul><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-14.png" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="1173" height="333" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/08/image-14.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2024/08/image-14.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-14.png 1173w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><p>Another amazing project is <a href="https://x.com/wassetltd"><u>Wasset</u></a>, a Web3 platform rewarding&nbsp; plastic waste collection through its unique blockchain protocol and reward token ($WST). This reward system facilitates efficient waste collection and management.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-15.png" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="1400" height="467" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/08/image-15.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2024/08/image-15.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-15.png 1400w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><blockquote><em>“I hope that other young people will be able to save the environment with their hands too. The more wastepreneurs we have, the cleaner our environment becomes.”&nbsp;</em><a href="https://x.com/AdejokeLasisi" rel="noopener ugc nofollow">Adejoke Lasisi</a></blockquote><h2 id="%F0%9F%92%A1-conclusiongoing-forward"><strong>💡 Conclusion - Going Forward</strong></h2><p>Tackling plastic pollution in Nigeria demands a comprehensive strategy that blends innovation, education, and efficient waste management. The current challenges, ranging from inadequate infrastructure to widespread illegal dumping, require urgent attention and systemic changes. Decentralized solutions like <a href="https://www.plastiks.io/"><u>Plastiks</u></a> and <a href="https://x.com/wassetltd"><u>Wasset</u></a> offer promising avenues for turning waste into valuable resources, ensuring transparency and trust with blockchain technology. Integrating regenerative finance principles to secure necessary funding, can enhance efforts and pave the way toward a more sustainable and cleaner environment, one city at a time.&nbsp;</p><h2 id="%F0%9F%91%80-whats-trending">👀 <strong>What's trending</strong>&nbsp;</h2><p><strong>🥳🎉 </strong><a href="https://grants.gitcoin.co/"><u>Gitcoin Grant 21</u></a> is live!&nbsp; <strong>Fund What Matters </strong>by contributing to projects that best reflect your vision for a regenerative future. </p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-17-1-1.png" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="500" height="285"></figure><p>👉 <a href="https://explorer.gitcoin.co/?ref=blog.refidao.com#/round/42220/14"><u>Regen Cordi-Nation Genesis Round</u></a></p><p>👉 <a href="https://explorer.gitcoin.co/?ref=blog.refidao.com#/round/42161/388"><u>Climate Coordination Network Round</u></a></p><p>👉 <a href="https://explorer.gitcoin.co/?ref=blog.refidao.com#/round/42161/388"><u>Celo Real World Builders Round</u></a></p><p>👉 <a href="https://explorer.gitcoin.co/#/round/42161/387"><u>Decentralized Science (DeSci) Round</u></a></p><p>Be part of the SOLUTION, not the POLLUTION💚♻️🍀</p><p><a href="https://t.me/+zGhwit24SUNkZWJh" rel="noopener ugc nofollow">Join us @ ReFi Lagos</a>&nbsp;Let’s make a difference, together!</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-16.png" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="1080" height="360" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/08/image-16.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2024/08/image-16.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/08/image-16.png 1080w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure>
item.excerpt:encoded: The pressing issue of plastic waste in Nigeria presents significant environmental and health impacts. Web3 and regenerative finance are turning these challenges into an opportunity for sustainable growth.

item.title: ReFi Nexus Is Here!🌐 Bioregional Finance With Samantha Power│ S4Ep1 🎧
item.dc:creator: Tereza Bizkova
Maya Dentzel
item.content:encoded: <p>Season 4 of the <strong>ReFi Podcast</strong> has arrived, focusing on <strong>The Regeneration Nexus</strong>—a theme centered on how we can integrate systems thinking, real-world impact, and emerging technologies to address global challenges like climate change and social inequality.</p><p>🎙️ <strong>In the first episode</strong>, hosts <a href="https://x.com/mayazdentzel" rel="noreferrer"><strong>Maya Dentzel</strong></a> and <a href="https://x.com/TerezaBizkova" rel="noreferrer"><strong>Tereza Bízková</strong></a> chat with <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/in/samanthapower/" rel="noreferrer"><strong>Samantha Power</strong></a>, a regenerative economist and co-founder of the <a href="https://www.biofi.earth" rel="noreferrer"><strong>BioFi Project</strong></a>. Samantha breaks down the transformative potential of Bioregional Financing Facilities (BFFs) and how they are reshaping financial models to empower local communities in their regeneration efforts. 🙌</p><div class="kg-card kg-callout-card kg-callout-card-purple"><div class="kg-callout-emoji">🌿</div><div class="kg-callout-text"><i><em class="italic" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">"Life wants to live. That is the nature of the planet we were born into. And we can create space for that life to come back."</em></i></div></div><figure class="kg-card kg-embed-card"><iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/Nd2LAykkFl4?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen="" title="Bioregional Finance with Samantha Power | S4E1: Regeneration Nexus"></iframe></figure><p><strong>Key insights from Episode 1 include...🌱</strong></p><ul><li><strong>Bioregional Financing Facilities (BFFs)</strong>: Samantha introduces the concept of BFFs as a framework for directing financial support to local communities. These facilities help fund projects focused on ecological restoration, sustainable economic development, and cultural preservation.</li><li><strong>Decentralized finance for local impact</strong>: The episode explores how decentralized technologies, like blockchain, allow communities to take control of financial resources, making decisions that directly benefit their local environments and economies.</li><li><strong>Case studies on bioregionalism</strong>: Samantha discusses successful projects where BFFs have been used to fund regeneration efforts, such as rewilding programs and community-led ecological restoration, showing how financial and ecological systems can align to create meaningful impact.</li><li><strong>Innovative tools for regeneration</strong>: Samantha highlights the use of eco-credits, nature-based currencies, and other technologies that are helping scale regenerative projects by making their impacts measurable and traceable, thus attracting more support and investment.</li></ul><h3 id="%F0%9F%8E%A7-tune-in-to-episode-1">🎧 Tune in to Episode 1</h3><ul><ul><li><a href="https://open.spotify.com/episode/13rQln9AjdjFfGDhTU5y5h?si=e7ed9e52123c4367" rel="noreferrer">Spotify</a></li><li><a href="https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/bioreginal-finance-with-samantha-power-s4e1/id1609683147?i=1000669705411" rel="noreferrer">Apple</a></li><li><a href="https://youtu.be/Nd2LAykkFl4?si=9wV69er-VQtb41aa" rel="noreferrer">YouTube</a></li></ul></ul><p>Throughout Season 4, we will continue engaging with leaders at the forefront of the regenerative movement to uncover how local actions, innovative financial models, and cutting-edge technologies are driving real change.</p><p>To keep the conversation going, we’re hosting a <strong>live discussion on Episode 1 this Friday, Sept 20, at 11 AM ET</strong>! 🎙️ Come share your thoughts and explore the bioregional approach further. 🌿</p><p>👉 Join the discussion on Twitter Spaces: <a href="https://twitter.com/i/spaces/1OwGWNbQEvqKQ" rel="noopener">https://twitter.com/i/spaces/1OwGWNbQEvqKQ</a></p><p><strong>Thank you to everyone who has joined this journey.</strong> Please share your thoughts and feedback, and if you've found value in our efforts, consider supporting us with <a href="https://podfollow.com/refi-podcast/episode/666c565da13f0cd174b1e355aa826f570df9dbb9/view" rel="noreferrer">a five-star review on your favorite podcast platform</a>. </p><p>Every bit of encouragement helps us expand our reach and deepen the impact of ReFi Podcast. You can also <a href="https://buymeacoffee.com/refipodcast" rel="noreferrer">buy us a coffee</a> or support our work directly <a href="https://giveth.io/project/refi-podcast-season-4-the-regeneration-nexus" rel="noreferrer">on Giveth</a>. <br><br>We are honored to be on this journey alongside you. 💜</p>

item.title: Building a Regenerative Economy with John Fullerton │ S4Ep2 🌿🎧
item.dc:creator: Tereza Bizkova
Maya Dentzel
item.content:encoded: <h3 id="what-if-finance-could-create-conditions-for-life-to-thrive">What if finance could create conditions for life to thrive? </h3><p>In Episode 2 of Season 4, the <strong>Regeneration Nexus, </strong>of the ReFi Podcast, hosts <a href="https://x.com/mayazdentzel" rel="noreferrer"><strong>Maya Dentzel</strong></a> and <a href="https://x.com/TerezaBizkova" rel="noreferrer"><strong>Tereza Bízková</strong></a> sit down with <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/in/john-fullerton-a5abbb4" rel="noreferrer"><strong>John Fullerton</strong></a>, founder of the <a href="https://capitalinstitute.org/" rel="noreferrer"><strong>Capital Institute</strong></a> and one of the<strong> leading thinkers in regenerative economics.</strong></p><p>After transitioning from a successful <strong>career on Wall Street</strong>, John dedicated his work to <strong>challenging the status quo of economics</strong>. His vision focuses on building an economic framework that supports the long-term health of people, communities, and the planet. In this episode, he explains why traditional financial models are failing and how regenerative finance offers a path forward.</p><p>John’s deep understanding of systems thinking and the global economy translates into practical solutions that both businesses and investors can adopt. He shares how regenerative finance can move us away from extractive practices and <strong>toward models that prioritize life and prosperity</strong>—together.</p><div class="kg-card kg-callout-card kg-callout-card-purple"><div class="kg-callout-emoji">🌿</div><div class="kg-callout-text"><i><em class="italic" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">"We’re running our society in conflict with the patterns and principles that explain how life works."</em></i> – John Fullerton</div></div><figure class="kg-card kg-embed-card"><iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/Cdk2xG4rZ2A?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen="" title="The Foundations of Regenerative Economics with John Fullerton | S4E2: Regeneration Nexus"></iframe></figure><p><strong>Key insights from Episode 2 include...🌱</strong></p><ul><li><strong>The Shift to Regenerative Finance:</strong> Regenerative finance offers a solution to the failures of extractive models by creating systems that not only repair past damage but also actively promote the flourishing of ecosystems and communities. This shift is essential for achieving long-term sustainability.</li><li><strong>The Role of Finance in Regeneration:</strong> Finance isn’t just a tool; it’s a critical lever for driving systemic change. By investing in nature-based solutions, financial systems can build resilience in local economies, making them more adaptable to global challenges like climate change and resource scarcity.</li><li><strong>Recycling Financial Capital into Regenerative Capital</strong>: John emphasizes that surplus financial capital needs to be “recycled, recomposted, regenerated” into other forms of capital, such as natural, social, and cultural capital. </li><li><strong>Embedding Regeneration in Business:</strong> Businesses, regardless of size, must rethink their internal culture and operational models to align with regenerative principles. This includes creating business models that integrate environmental and social goals, ensuring that financial success doesn’t come at the cost of the planet.</li><li><strong>Decentralized Technology as a Force for Regeneration:</strong> Blockchain and decentralized finance aren’t just tech trends—they are vital for scaling regenerative efforts. These tools can decentralize power and resources, giving communities control over their own regeneration processes and ensuring transparency in impact measurement.</li></ul><h3 id="%F0%9F%8E%A7-tune-in-to-episode-2">🎧 Tune in to Episode 2</h3><ul><ul><li><a href="https://open.spotify.com/episode/441b4YhzpuSSctD0xwaKMA?si=fea7c9468655424d" rel="noreferrer">Spotify</a></li><li><a href="https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/the-foundations-of-regenerative-economics-with/id1609683147?i=1000670422620" rel="noreferrer">Apple</a></li><li><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cdk2xG4rZ2A" rel="noreferrer">YouTube</a></li></ul></ul><p>And don’t forget! We’re hosting a<strong> live discussion on Episode 2 this Friday, Sept 27, at 11 AM ET! 🎙️</strong> Share your thoughts and dive deeper into the world of regenerative economics with us on Twitter Spaces. 🌿</p><p>👉 Join the discussion on Twitter Spaces: <br><a href="https://twitter.com/i/spaces/1MnxnDzkEaoGO">https://twitter.com/i/spaces/1MnxnDzkEaoGO</a></p><p><strong>Thank you to everyone who has joined this journey.</strong> Please share your thoughts and feedback, and if you've found value in our efforts, consider supporting us with <a href="https://podfollow.com/refi-podcast/view" rel="noreferrer">a five-star review on your favorite podcast platform</a>. </p><p>Every bit of encouragement helps us expand our reach and deepen the impact of ReFi Podcast. You can also <a href="https://buymeacoffee.com/refipodcast" rel="noreferrer">buy us a coffee</a> or support our work directly <a href="https://giveth.io/project/refi-podcast-season-4-the-regeneration-nexus" rel="noreferrer">on Giveth</a>. <br><br>We are honored to be on this journey alongside you. 💜</p>

item.title: Democracy, Technology, and Plurality with Glen Weyl │ S4Ep3 💻🎧
item.dc:creator: Tereza Bizkova
Maya Dentzel
item.content:encoded: <h3 id="what-if-technology-could-enhance-the-very-fabric-of-our-democratic-systems">What if technology could enhance the very fabric of our democratic systems?</h3><p>In Episode 3 of Season 4, <em>The Regeneration Nexus</em>, of the ReFi Podcast, hosts <a href="https://x.com/mayazdentzel" rel="noreferrer"><strong>Maya Dentzel</strong></a> and <a href="https://x.com/TerezaBizkova" rel="noreferrer"><strong>Tereza Bízková</strong></a> welcome <a href="https://twitter.com/glenweyl?lang=cs" rel="noreferrer"><strong>Glen Weyl</strong></a>, a political economist, researcher at <a href="https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/group/plural-technology-collaboratory/" rel="noreferrer">Plural Technology Collaboratory</a> at Microsoft Research, and founder of <a href="https://www.radicalxchange.org/" rel="noreferrer">RadicalxChange</a>, and <a href="https://www.plurality.institute/about" rel="noreferrer">Plurality Institute</a>. In this conversation, Glen shares his insights on how concepts like <strong>plurality can reshape democracy and finance</strong>, building systems that prioritize interconnection and community.</p><p>After a successful career in economics, Glen turned his focus toward exploring new ways of thinking about governance, technology, and democracy. In this episode, he discusses how <strong>technology can enable more nuanced democratic systems</strong> and offers examples from <strong>Taiwan's digital democracy</strong> to explain how governments can adapt to the challenges of the 21st century.</p><p>Through his work on <em>plurality</em>, Glen advocates for breaking down rigid structures and enabling<strong> more dynamic connections within our social and political systems</strong>. From blockchain's role in supporting decentralized coordination to addressing polarization in the U.S., Glen explains how embracing complexity and diversity can lead to more resilient systems.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-embed-card"><iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/aRYJbBH6jlo?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen="" title="Democracy, Technology, and Plurality with Glen Weyl | S4E3: Regeneration Nexus"></iframe></figure><div class="kg-card kg-callout-card kg-callout-card-purple"><div class="kg-callout-emoji">🏛️</div><div class="kg-callout-text"><i><em class="italic" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">"We need to take the places where there’s energy—like the anger on social media—and </em></i><i><b><strong class="italic" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">convert that energy into work</strong></b></i><i><em class="italic" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">, instead of letting it dissipate as heat. That’s the challenge, turning emotional reactions into productive outcomes."</em></i></div></div><p>Key insights from Episode 3 include... 💡</p><ul><li><strong>The Importance of Plurality</strong>: Glen explains how pluralistic systems better reflect the complexities of human relationships and community needs, in contrast to rigid political and economic frameworks.</li><li><strong>Taiwan’s Digital Democracy</strong>: Glen highlights Taiwan as a leading example of combining technology with democracy, showcasing the POLIS system, which has helped reduce polarization through innovative citizen engagement tools.</li><li><strong>Conflict as a Catalyst for Progress</strong>: Rather than avoiding conflict, Glen suggests that embracing multiple forms of conflict can help break down polarization and lead to more collaborative societies.</li><li><strong>Blockchain and Regenerative Communities</strong>: While blockchain can be a tool for decentralized coordination, Glen stresses that not all blockchain models are beneficial—advocating for privacy-oriented, community-based ledgers over speculative public blockchains.</li></ul><p>🎧 <strong>Tune in to Episode 3</strong></p><ul><li><a href="https://open.spotify.com/episode/4IIBL68IiKNAo9JHDB5PpP?si=eb5d874a5098451b" rel="noreferrer">Spotify</a></li><li><a href="https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/democracy-technology-and-plurality-with-glen-weyl/id1609683147?i=1000671308736" rel="noreferrer">Apple</a></li><li><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aRYJbBH6jlo" rel="noreferrer">YouTube</a></li></ul><p>And don’t forget! We’re hosting a<strong> live discussion on Episode 3 this Friday, Oct 4, at 11 AM ET! 🎙️</strong> Share your thoughts and dive deeper into the world of regenerative economics with us on Twitter Spaces. 🌿</p><p>👉 Join the discussion on Twitter Spaces: <a href="https://twitter.com/i/spaces/1vOGwrprqZVKB">https://twitter.com/i/spaces/1vOGwrprqZVKB</a></p><p><strong>Thank you to everyone who has joined this journey.</strong> Please share your thoughts and feedback, and if you've found value in our efforts, consider supporting us with <a href="https://podfollow.com/refi-podcast/view" rel="noreferrer">a five-star review on your favorite podcast platform</a>. </p><p>Every bit of encouragement helps us expand our reach and deepen the impact of ReFi Podcast. You can also <a href="https://buymeacoffee.com/refipodcast" rel="noreferrer">buy us a coffee</a> or support our work directly <a href="https://giveth.io/project/refi-podcast-season-4-the-regeneration-nexus" rel="noreferrer">on Giveth</a>. <br><br>We are honored to be on this journey alongside you. 💜</p>

item.title: Ecoweaving with Tony Lai │ S4Ep4 🍃🎧
item.dc:creator: Tereza Bizkova
Maya Dentzel
item.content:encoded: <h3 id="what-if-the-future-of-humanity-depended-on-how-we-reconnect-with-the-earth%E2%80%94and-each-other">What if the future of humanity depended on how we reconnect with the Earth—and each other?</h3><p>In Episode 4 of Season 4, <em>The Regeneration Nexus</em>, of the ReFi Podcast, hosts <a href="https://x.com/mayazdentzel" rel="noreferrer"><strong>Maya Dentzel</strong></a> and <a href="https://x.com/TerezaBizkova" rel="noreferrer"><strong>Tereza Bízková</strong></a> welcome <a href="https://x.com/lai" rel="noreferrer"><strong>Tony Lai</strong></a>, co-steward of <a href="https://www.mothertreelabs.com/" rel="noreferrer">Mother Tree Labs</a> and fellow at Stanford’s <a href="https://law.stanford.edu/codex-the-stanford-center-for-legal-informatics/" rel="noreferrer">CodeX</a>. With his background in law, technology, and ecological transition, Tony shares a vision for how we can build <strong>systems that honor both human relationships and the natural world</strong>. </p><p>Tony dives into how <strong>law can evolve from a set of rigid rules to a tool for ecological and social healing</strong>. He urges us to rethink governance—not as a way to manage resources but as a way to foster <strong>deeper connections between people, communities, and ecosystems</strong>. His message is clear: we need systems that prioritize interconnection, care, and regeneration.</p><p>Tony illustrates how <strong>regenerative practices, powered by both technology and human connection, can reshape our economies</strong> and the way we live. By using decentralized tools like blockchain, communities can take control, managing their resources based on shared values and sustainability goals. It’s a shift that empowers local, grassroots action over top-down control.</p><p>Through his expertise in computational law and commons governance, Tony shares how these emerging tools can<strong> decentralize power, make law an agent of regeneration, and help communities thrive</strong>. </p><figure class="kg-card kg-embed-card"><iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/x101tNRm9xg?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen="" title="Ecoweaving with Tony Lai | S4E4: Regeneration Nexus"></iframe></figure><div class="kg-card kg-callout-card kg-callout-card-purple"><div class="kg-callout-emoji">🌎</div><div class="kg-callout-text"><i><em class="italic" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Law has been intertwined with religion, politics, and economics, shaping how we cooperate and how we punish. But now, law must evolve to serve not just human interests, but the </em></i><i><b><strong class="italic" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Earth’s regeneration and the balance of life</strong></b></i><i><em class="italic" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">.</em></i></div></div><p>Key insights from Episode 4 include... 💡</p><ul><li><strong>Law as a Tool for Ecological Healing:</strong> Tony envisions a legal system where the Earth is recognized as a living entity with rights, reshaping how we protect natural resources. Law, he argues, can be used to restore balance between people and the planet, shifting from exploitation to stewardship.</li><li><strong>Regeneration Starts with Us:</strong> Tony shares personal practices like forest singing and tree hugging, demonstrating how simple acts of mindfulness can ground us and fuel broader ecological and social healing. He reminds us that regeneration begins at the individual level and ripples outward.</li><li><strong>Community-Driven Governance:</strong> Tony advocates for governance systems that prioritize relationships over rigid roles, showing how communities can self-organize to manage their resources in a way that reflects shared values. This shift towards decentralized, community-led governance opens up new possibilities for resilience and collaboration.</li><li><strong>Rethinking Economic Systems:</strong> Tony explains how regenerative finance, through local currencies and decentralized tools, offers a new way to connect economies to both people and nature. This rethinking of finance shifts from extraction to replenishment, where value is created through sustaining ecosystems and communities.</li></ul><p>🎧 <strong>Tune in to Episode 4</strong></p><ul><li><a href="https://open.spotify.com/episode/4ZX2SyOaAPiRaYwl4ofDiB?si=84a2de28d8a24f64" rel="noreferrer">Spotify</a></li><li><a href="https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/ecoweaving-with-tony-lai-s4e4-regeneration-nexus/id1609683147?i=1000672088948" rel="noreferrer">Apple</a></li><li><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x101tNRm9xg" rel="noreferrer">YouTube</a></li></ul><p>And don’t forget! We’re hosting a<strong> live discussion on Episode 3 this Friday, Oct 11, at 11 AM ET! 🎙️</strong> Share your thoughts and dive deeper into the world of regenerative economics with us on Twitter Spaces. 🌿</p><p>👉 Join the discussion on Twitter Spaces: <a href="https://twitter.com/i/spaces/1vOxwrelZbDJB">https://twitter.com/i/spaces/1vOxwrelZbDJB</a></p><p><strong>Thank you to everyone who has joined this journey.</strong> Please share your thoughts and feedback, and if you've found value in our efforts, consider supporting us with <a href="https://podfollow.com/refi-podcast/view" rel="noreferrer">a five-star review on your favorite podcast platform</a>. </p><p>Every bit of encouragement helps us expand our reach and deepen the impact of ReFi Podcast. You can also <a href="https://buymeacoffee.com/refipodcast" rel="noreferrer">buy us a coffee</a> or support our work directly <a href="https://giveth.io/project/refi-podcast-season-4-the-regeneration-nexus" rel="noreferrer">on Giveth</a>. <br><br>We are honored to be on this journey alongside you. 💜</p>

item.title: Regen Coordination & GG22 - Collaborative Pathways to Regeneration ✨
item.dc:creator: Monty Merlin Bryant
item.content:encoded: <h2 id="overview">Overview</h2><hr><p><strong>Regen Coordination</strong> is an evolving alliance of Web3 organizations united in collaboration to drive ecological, social, and economic regeneration. Through innovative programs and collective action, we help empower a global network of people and communities to <em>realize a better future</em>.</p><p>In partnership with <a href="https://www.celopg.eco/" rel="noreferrer">Celo Public Goods</a>, <a href="https://grants.gitcoin.co/" rel="noreferrer">Gitcoin</a>, <a href="https://linktr.ee/refidao" rel="noreferrer">ReFi DAO</a>, <a href="https://greenpill.network/" rel="noreferrer">GreenPill Network</a>, <a href="https://www.letsgrow.network/" rel="noreferrer">Let’s Grow DAO</a>, <a href="https://www.biofi.earth/" rel="noreferrer">The BioFi Project</a>, <a href="https://opencivics.co/" rel="noreferrer">Open Civics</a>, and other key collaborators, Regen Coordination has helped to raise over $200,000 for local regenerative communities, bioregional organizing teams, and regen citizens over the past six months. This includes two key funding rounds, live today for Gitcoin Grants Round 22 (GG22) on Celo: <a href="https://www.regencoordination.xyz/GG21-Regen-Coordination-Genesis-11a2e7251f2f80c98b8ceee0b571b9ff?pvs=4" rel="noreferrer">Regen Citizens Genesis</a> and <a href="https://nifty-humidity-dcf.notion.site/GG22-BioFi-Pathfinders-Round-11866e07503c80e89439c0c4fdba6df7" rel="noreferrer">BioFi Pathfinders</a>. </p><p>This is just the beginning. Our vision is to support the global transition to a regenerative economy. Keep reading for more details on some of the key theories of change underpinning the Regen Coordination and an overview of current programs &amp; partnerships.</p><h2 id="theory-of-change"><strong>Theory of Change</strong></h2><hr><h3 id="coordi-nations-a-new-paradigm-for-global-cooperation">Coordi-nations: A New Paradigm for Global Cooperation</h3><p>At the heart of Regen Coordination lies the concept of <strong>Coordi-nations</strong> or '<strong>Network Nations</strong>', an innovative approach to global cooperation. Unlike traditional network states, Coordi-nations focus on interwoven networks of communities that operate on mutualism, collaboration, and distributed decision-making. These communities come together through shared values and participatory governance to pool resources for greater impact.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-bookmark-card"><a class="kg-bookmark-container" href="https://jessykate.medium.com/coordi-nations-a-new-institutional-structure-for-global-cooperation-3ef38d6e2cfa"><div class="kg-bookmark-content"><div class="kg-bookmark-title">Coordi-nations: A New Institutional Structure for Global Cooperation</div><div class="kg-bookmark-description">Coordi-nations are a new form of network sovereignty designed around voluntary association, participatory governance and mutualism.</div><div class="kg-bookmark-metadata"><img class="kg-bookmark-icon" src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/icon/10fd5c419ac61637245384e7099e131627900034828f4f386bdaa47a74eae156" alt=""><span class="kg-bookmark-author">Medium</span><span class="kg-bookmark-publisher">Jessy Kate Schingler</span></div></div><div class="kg-bookmark-thumbnail"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/thumbnail/1-zeA3yz6uCudv6WR3_NgLgw.png" alt="" onerror="this.style.display = 'none'"></div></a></figure><h3 id="web3-regenerative-finance-transforming-economic-systems">Web3 &amp; Regenerative Finance : Transforming Economic Systems</h3><p>ReFi's<strong> </strong>core principles involve the reimagining of economic systems away from extractive and exploitative outcomes, towards models that support the holistic wellbeing of people and planet. Utilizing advanced technologies like blockchain, digital measurement, reporting, &amp; verification (dMRV), and AI, ReFi aims to channel resources to projects that aim for systemic change and positive impact. Regen Coordination is grounded in a shared belief that Web3 and ReFi are a key part of realizing a next-generation economy. </p><figure class="kg-card kg-bookmark-card"><a class="kg-bookmark-container" href="https://www.regenerative.fi/insights/what-is-refi-regenerative-finance"><div class="kg-bookmark-content"><div class="kg-bookmark-title">What is ReFi (Regenerative Finance)? | Blog</div><div class="kg-bookmark-description">Discover how ReFi revolutionizes finance, transforming it from extractive to restorative, and aligning economic systems with the Earth’s well-being. Dive into the world where finance fosters regeneration, not depletion.</div><div class="kg-bookmark-metadata"><img class="kg-bookmark-icon" src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/icon/652d421c1214a2eebd967f2f_Favicon.png" alt=""><span class="kg-bookmark-author">Regenerative blue colored logo</span><span class="kg-bookmark-publisher">ReFi DAO</span></div></div><div class="kg-bookmark-thumbnail"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/thumbnail/65bbd334a50c62fdb0efbfa2_What-20is-20ReFi_.png" alt="" onerror="this.style.display = 'none'"></div></a></figure><h3 id="cosmo-localism-connecting-global-knowledge-to-local-action">Cosmo-localism: Connecting Global Knowledge to Local Action</h3><p><strong>Cosmo-localism</strong> bridges global knowledge with local action by empowering communities to access global tools and resources while adapting them to their local contexts. This concept eliminates hierarchical global-to-local dynamics, promoting decentralized, participatory models that allow communities to tailor solutions to their specific cultural and environmental needs.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-bookmark-card"><a class="kg-bookmark-container" href="https://www.thealternative.org.uk/dailyalternative/2019/5/13/what-is-cosmo-localism-and-why-we-think-its-a-game-changer"><div class="kg-bookmark-content"><div class="kg-bookmark-title">What is “cosmo-localism”? Why do we think it’s a game changer? And help fill out a dictionary for it — THE ALTERNATIVE</div><div class="kg-bookmark-description">Yes, what is cosmo-localism? Is it just a more sophisticated way of talking about complex and integrated community work? Is it another, more fashionable way of talking about the “glocal” ? Or is it a sign of the cosmopolitan elite trying to take over local initiatives? Suffice it to say, some o</div><div class="kg-bookmark-metadata"><img class="kg-bookmark-icon" src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/icon/favicon.ico" alt=""><span class="kg-bookmark-author">THE ALTERNATIVE</span><span class="kg-bookmark-publisher">pat kane</span></div></div><div class="kg-bookmark-thumbnail"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/thumbnail/The-Alternative-logo-banner--1-.png" alt="" onerror="this.style.display = 'none'"></div></a></figure><h2 id="current-programs-partnerships"><strong>Current Programs &amp; Partnerships</strong></h2><hr><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/Regen-Coordi-Nation-GG21-Genesis-Round.jpg" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="1721" height="418" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/10/Regen-Coordi-Nation-GG21-Genesis-Round.jpg 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2024/10/Regen-Coordi-Nation-GG21-Genesis-Round.jpg 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2024/10/Regen-Coordi-Nation-GG21-Genesis-Round.jpg 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/Regen-Coordi-Nation-GG21-Genesis-Round.jpg 1721w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><h3 id="%F0%9F%8C%B1-gg21-regen-coordination-genesis">🌱 GG21 &amp; Regen Coordination Genesis</h3><p>The <a href="https://explorer.gitcoin.co/#/round/42220/14" rel="noreferrer">GG21 Regen Coordination Genesis Round</a> served as the official launch of Regen Coordination, aiming to support a global movement of regenerative Web3 communities and catalyze collaboration. With a $50,000 matching pool, the round invited applications from ReFi DAO Local Nodes, GreenPill Local Chapters, and Celo Regional DAOs. With further funding committed towards a retroactive program in Q1 2025, GG21 was just the beginning.</p><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="https://www.regencoordination.xyz/GG21-Regen-Coordination-Genesis-11a2e7251f2f80c98b8ceee0b571b9ff?pvs=4" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">Learn more</a></div><hr><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/GG22-Regen-Citizen-Round-Banner.jpg" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="2000" height="486" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/10/GG22-Regen-Citizen-Round-Banner.jpg 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2024/10/GG22-Regen-Citizen-Round-Banner.jpg 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2024/10/GG22-Regen-Citizen-Round-Banner.jpg 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w2400/2024/10/GG22-Regen-Citizen-Round-Banner.jpg 2400w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><h3 id="%F0%9F%91%A5-gg22-regen-citizens-genesis-round">👥 GG22 Regen Citizens Genesis Round</h3><p>The <a href="https://explorer.gitcoin.co/#/round/42220/16" rel="noreferrer">GG22 Regen Citizens Genesis Round</a> is a joint initiative between GreenPill Network, ReFi DAO, Let’s Grow DAO, and Celo Public Goods. Focusing primarily on these organisation as a starting point, the aim of this program is to empower and recognize builders making meaningful contributions to the regenerative movement on Ethereum. To participate during GG22, applicants must be nominated or invited by a Core or Guest Organization - see <a href="https://www.regencoordination.xyz/GG22-Regen-Citizens-Genesis-11a2e7251f2f80b0b958c8ef1f89bb7a?pvs=4" rel="noreferrer">Nomination Process</a>. The round is live now, with the application period running until October 22, 2024, and donations open from October 23 to November 6, 2024.</p><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="https://www.regencoordination.xyz/GG22-Regen-Citizens-Genesis-11a2e7251f2f80b0b958c8ef1f89bb7a?pvs=4" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">Learn more</a></div><hr><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/photo_2024-10-15-5.14.39-pm-copy.jpeg" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="1280" height="362" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/10/photo_2024-10-15-5.14.39-pm-copy.jpeg 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2024/10/photo_2024-10-15-5.14.39-pm-copy.jpeg 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/photo_2024-10-15-5.14.39-pm-copy.jpeg 1280w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><h3 id="%F0%9F%8D%83-gg22-biofi-pathfinders-round">🍃 GG22 BioFi Pathfinders Round</h3><p>The <strong>BioFi Pathfinders Round</strong>, also live now, is a partnership between The BioFi Project, Open Civics, The Design School for Regenerating Earth, and Regen Coordination. This round is designed to support advanced Bioregional Organizing Teams that are actively developing Bioregional Finance (BioFi) strategies. The goal is to build decentralized, place-based financial governance systems that drive regenerative economies. Teams that demonstrate a deep connection to place, coherent bioregional identities, and strong financial practices have been invited to apply by October 22, 2024. The donation period runs from October 23 to November 6, 2024.</p><div class="kg-card kg-button-card kg-align-center"><a href="https://nifty-humidity-dcf.notion.site/GG22-BioFi-Pathfinders-Round-11866e07503c80e89439c0c4fdba6df7" class="kg-btn kg-btn-accent">Learn more</a></div><hr><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/ReFi-EBF-Cover-2-copy.png" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="2000" height="396" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/10/ReFi-EBF-Cover-2-copy.png 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2024/10/ReFi-EBF-Cover-2-copy.png 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2024/10/ReFi-EBF-Cover-2-copy.png 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w2400/2024/10/ReFi-EBF-Cover-2-copy.png 2400w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><h3 id="%F0%9F%97%BA%EF%B8%8F-ebf-cohort-0-coming-soon">🗺️ EBF Cohort 0 (Coming Soon)</h3><p>Starting with six words –&nbsp;<strong>Air, Water, Soil, Biodiversity, Equity, </strong>and<strong> Carbon</strong>&nbsp;– the <a href="https://ebfcommons.org/" rel="noreferrer">Ecological Benefits Framework (EBF)</a> is an adaptive way to explain impact with a comprehensive yet intuitive visual language. Now, in collaboration with <a href="https://spark.eco/" rel="noreferrer">Spark Eco</a>, ReFi DAO and Regen Coordination are supporting the development of <a href="https://impactscribe.xyz/" rel="noreferrer">Impact Scribe</a>. Built on Web3 rails, Impact Scribe is a tool to help anyone showcase their project’s work using EBF and help unlock new sources of funding. More details on this exciting new tool and a potential upcoming EBF cohort will be shared soon!</p><figure class="kg-card kg-bookmark-card"><a class="kg-bookmark-container" href="https://ebfcommons.org/"><div class="kg-bookmark-content"><div class="kg-bookmark-title">Can You Change the Future?</div><div class="kg-bookmark-description">A Framework for Diverse Investors to Create Positive Impacts in Six Key Areas: Air, Water, Soil, Biodiversity, Equity, and Carbon</div><div class="kg-bookmark-metadata"><img class="kg-bookmark-icon" src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/icon/EBF-Logo_v1-177-300x300.png" alt=""><span class="kg-bookmark-author">Ecological Benefits Framework</span></div></div><div class="kg-bookmark-thumbnail"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/thumbnail/EBF-Logo_v1-179.png" alt="" onerror="this.style.display = 'none'"></div></a></figure><figure class="kg-card kg-bookmark-card"><a class="kg-bookmark-container" href="__GHOST_URL__/ecological-benefits-activator/"><div class="kg-bookmark-content"><div class="kg-bookmark-title">A Common Framework for ReFi | EBF Activator x ReFi DAO 🌱</div><div class="kg-bookmark-description">What actually is ReFi? What is Regeneration? How should we measure &amp; compare projects?</div><div class="kg-bookmark-metadata"><img class="kg-bookmark-icon" src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/icon/6319c4c1d0b248c635dc4002_ReFi-DAO-1.png" alt=""><span class="kg-bookmark-author">ReFi DAO</span><span class="kg-bookmark-publisher">Monty Merlin Bryant</span></div></div><div class="kg-bookmark-thumbnail"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/thumbnail/ReFi-DAO-x-The-Lexicon---Ecological-Benefits-Framework-Activator--EBF-.jpg" alt="" onerror="this.style.display = 'none'"></div></a></figure><figure class="kg-card kg-bookmark-card"><a class="kg-bookmark-container" href="__GHOST_URL__/refi-ebf-whats-next/"><div class="kg-bookmark-content"><div class="kg-bookmark-title">ReFi &amp; Ecological Benefits Framework - Whats Next?</div><div class="kg-bookmark-description">Explore the transformative journey of the Ecological Benefits Framework (EBF), the launch of ReFi EBF, and what’s coming next…</div><div class="kg-bookmark-metadata"><img class="kg-bookmark-icon" src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/icon/6319c4c1d0b248c635dc4002_ReFi-DAO.png" alt=""><span class="kg-bookmark-author">ReFi DAO</span><span class="kg-bookmark-publisher">Monty Merlin Bryant</span></div></div><div class="kg-bookmark-thumbnail"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/thumbnail/ReFi-EBF-Article-Cover-2.png" alt="" onerror="this.style.display = 'none'"></div></a></figure><hr><h2 id="a-new-era-for-regen-coordination"><strong>A New Era for Regen Coordination</strong></h2><p>Regen Coordination is more than just a series of funding rounds. By leveraging decentralized technologies and fostering collaboration between innovative organizations and local efforts, Regen Coordination is supporting a future where cooperation and mutualism replace extraction and exploitation. Our vision is clear: to scale regenerative solutions, empower communities, and catalyze a global transition to an economy rooted in regeneration and resilience. In this pursuit, we are committed to forging new pathways for collaboration, innovation, and real-world impact. Our current programs are just the beginning.</p><p>Join us as we continue to build this movement. Explore our programs, engage with our communities, and become part of the future we are creating together. Visit <a href="https://www.regencoordination.xyz/" rel="noreferrer">RegenCoordination.xyz</a> to learn more and join the <a href="https://t.me/+dfOMYhMROdU5YzY0" rel="noreferrer">Telegram group</a> for further discussion and announcements.</p><p>Thank you to our partners and collaborators—Luuk Weber, Obi Onwuzurike, Sejal Rekhan, Scott Morris, Samantha Power, Tyler Scharf, Benjamin Life, Jon Ruth, and all the organizations from ReFi DAO, GreenPill Network, Celo Public Goods, Gitcoin, and many others who have been instrumental in this journey so far. ✨</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/magicstudio-art-copy-10.jpg" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="1024" height="1024" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/10/magicstudio-art-copy-10.jpg 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2024/10/magicstudio-art-copy-10.jpg 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/magicstudio-art-copy-10.jpg 1024w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure>
item.excerpt:encoded: How can we scale regenerative solutions, empower communities, and catalyze a global transition to an economy where cooperation and mutualism replace extraction and exploitation?

item.title: Reflections on the First ReFi Podcast S4 Miniseries: Laying the Groundwork for Systems Change 💭🎙️
item.dc:creator: Maya Dentzel
Tereza Bizkova
item.content:encoded: <p>As we conclude the first miniseries of Season 4 of The Regeneration Nexus, "<em>The Vision: Why do we need to reimagine traditional economic and belief systems?</em>", our goal was to clearly define the core principles of regeneration and understand why rethinking these systems is crucial.</p><p>While each guest—<a href="https://www.linkedin.com/in/john-fullerton-a5abbb4" rel="noreferrer"><strong>John Fullerton</strong></a><strong>, </strong><a href="https://www.linkedin.com/in/samanthapower" rel="noreferrer"><strong>Samantha Power</strong></a><strong>, </strong><a href="https://twitter.com/lai" rel="noreferrer"><strong>Tony Lai</strong></a>, and<strong> </strong><a href="https://x.com/glenweyl" rel="noreferrer"><strong>Glen Weyl</strong></a>—approached systems change from a different lens, common threads emerged throughout their insights. </p><p>From regenerative economics and bioregionalism to ecoweaving and pluralism, each guest brought unique ideas on how we can address the polycrisis, while highlighting shared values like interconnectedness, diversity, and the need to honor life and local wisdom. Let's take a closer look. </p><h2 id="%F0%9F%94%8E-a-new-vision-for-a-regenerative-future">🔎<strong> A New Vision for a Regenerative Future</strong></h2><p><strong>Samantha Power</strong> kicked off the series by highlighting <strong>bioregionalism</strong>, emphasizing the importance of local, place-based governance systems that allow ecosystems to thrive.<strong> John Fullerton</strong> expanded on this by exploring the transformative principles of <strong>regenerative economics</strong>, demonstrating how aligning financial systems with nature’s patterns can foster sustainable growth and well-being. <strong>Tony Lai</strong> introduced the concept of <strong>ecoweaving</strong>, blending law, technology, and community to create structures that honor the Earth. Finally, <strong>Glen Weyl</strong> brought us into the world of <strong>pluralism</strong>, emphasizing the need for diversity and interconnected systems to foster resilience and adaptability.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/GaA0jVwa8AA_NLI.jpeg" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="1080" height="1080" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/10/GaA0jVwa8AA_NLI.jpeg 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2024/10/GaA0jVwa8AA_NLI.jpeg 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/GaA0jVwa8AA_NLI.jpeg 1080w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><h2 id="%F0%9F%92%A1-key-themes"><strong>💡 Key Themes</strong></h2><p>Throughout these conversations, several key themes emerged, laying the groundwork for a regenerative future:</p><p>🌱<strong> Respect for Life</strong></p><p>A unifying theme across the series is a profound respect for life and its inherent ability to regenerate. The concept of “life wanting to live” calls for systems that prioritize nature’s rhythms and provide space for ecosystems to heal and communities to flourish. </p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/samantha.jpeg" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="1920" height="1080" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/10/samantha.jpeg 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2024/10/samantha.jpeg 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2024/10/samantha.jpeg 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/samantha.jpeg 1920w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><p><strong>🌀 Interconnectedness</strong></p><p>Another critical insight was the interconnectedness of ecological, social, and economic systems. Ignoring these deep links has driven us toward crisis, and true regeneration requires a holistic approach. </p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/john.jpeg" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="1920" height="1080" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/10/john.jpeg 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2024/10/john.jpeg 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2024/10/john.jpeg 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/john.jpeg 1920w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><p><strong>🍃 Decentralization &amp; Indigenous Wisdom</strong></p><p>Empowering communities rooted in the land, especially those with indigenous knowledge, is vital for ecological healing and systemic change. Decentralization and local stewardship play a key role in fostering these regenerative systems, allowing communities to take ownership and align their practices with the rhythms of nature.</p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/tony.jpeg" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="1920" height="1080" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/10/tony.jpeg 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2024/10/tony.jpeg 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2024/10/tony.jpeg 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/tony.jpeg 1920w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><p><strong> </strong>🌈<strong> Diversity &amp; Complexity</strong></p><p>Finally, diversity and complexity emerged as key ingredients in building resilient systems. Embracing community energy and transforming it into positive action can help us navigate uncertainty and change. </p><figure class="kg-card kg-image-card"><img src="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/photo_2024-10-16-16.44.05.jpeg" class="kg-image" alt="" loading="lazy" width="1920" height="1080" srcset="__GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w600/2024/10/photo_2024-10-16-16.44.05.jpeg 600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1000/2024/10/photo_2024-10-16-16.44.05.jpeg 1000w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/size/w1600/2024/10/photo_2024-10-16-16.44.05.jpeg 1600w, __GHOST_URL__/content/images/2024/10/photo_2024-10-16-16.44.05.jpeg 1920w" sizes="(min-width: 720px) 720px"></figure><h2 id="%F0%9F%8C%B1-our-takeaway-a-life-centered-future"><strong>🌱 Our Takeaway: A Life-Centered Future</strong></h2><p>The key takeaway from these episodes is simple: <strong>We need to move beyond profit-centered systems and place life at the heart of everything we do</strong>. Regenerating economies and communities starts with honoring the rhythms of nature and tapping into the wisdom of local and indigenous knowledge. </p><p>As we continue this journey, it’s clear that these principles—respect for life, interconnectedness, decentralization, and diversity—are essential to shaping a more regenerative, life-affirming future. </p><p><strong>What’s Next?</strong></p><p>As we look ahead, we invite you to join us in exploring real-world innovations and regenerative projects that are already reshaping our world. Stay tuned for the next miniseries, where we dive into the practical applications of these systems and hear from leaders on the ground driving transformative change.</p><p><strong>🎧 Listen to Season 4 now on your favorite platform:</strong></p><ul><li><a href="https://open.spotify.com/show/5RTHF6JVgQL1cgaVfvi7cv" rel="noreferrer">Spotify</a></li><li><a href="https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/refi-podcast/id1609683147" rel="noreferrer">Apple Podcasts</a></li><li><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I63gGjNv2Ag&amp;list=PLArKB4hKFyGHwsAl-AntG1qc2cswK08Bw" rel="noreferrer">YouTube</a></li></ul><p>Help us grow the <a href="https://x.com/ReFiPodcast" rel="noreferrer"><strong>ReFi Podcast</strong></a> and reach even more listeners! You can directly support our work by <a href="https://giveth.io/project/refi-podcast-season-4-the-regeneration-nexus" rel="noreferrer">contributing on Giveth</a> or simply <a href="https://buymeacoffee.com/refipodcast" rel="noreferrer">buy us a coffee</a> to fuel the journey. Your support, no matter how small, makes a big impact. 🙌</p><p>Thank you for being part of this journey toward a regenerative future! 💜</p>

item.dc:creator: Tereza Bizkova
Maya Dentzel
item.content:encoded: <h3 id="what-if-we-had-a-better-way-to-value-forests-and-the-communities-that-protect-them"><strong>What if we had a better way to value forests and the communities that protect them?</strong></h3><p>In Episode 5 of Season 4, <em>The Regeneration Nexus</em>, of the ReFi Podcast, hosts <a href="https://x.com/mayazdentzel" rel="noreferrer"><strong>Maya Dentzel</strong></a> and <a href="https://x.com/TerezaBizkova" rel="noreferrer"><strong>Tereza Bízková</strong></a> welcome <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/in/pete-corke-82063a3/" rel="noreferrer">Pete Corke</a>, regenerative innovator and co-founder of <a href="https://www.kwaxala.com/" rel="noreferrer">Kwaxala</a>. Pete’s work in British Columbia focuses on moving away from harmful economic models and empowering indigenous communities to protect and regenerate their forests.</p><p>Pete shares his approach to shifting from extraction to stewardship, emphasizing the importance of respecting <strong>indigenous knowledge and land rights</strong>. He shows us how <strong>local communities can take control of their resources and create sustainable futures.</strong></p><p>By combining real-world impact with innovative finance, Pete offers practical solutions for protecting ecosystems and <strong>valuing them for their economic worth and their role in supporting life</strong>.</p><div class="kg-card kg-callout-card kg-callout-card-purple"><div class="kg-callout-emoji">🌳</div><div class="kg-callout-text"><i><em class="italic" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">The current economic model incentivizes destruction—</em></i><i><b><strong class="italic" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">forests are seen as financial liabilities unless they’re being cut down</strong></b></i><i><em class="italic" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">. We’re changing that narrative by creating regenerative finance models that allow forests to generate revenue through protection, not extraction.</em></i></div></div><p>Key insights from Episode 5 include... 💡</p><ul><li><strong>Rights to Regenerate:</strong> Pete explains how British Columbia's indigenous-led cooperatives are turning the tables on traditional logging by securing rights to regenerate, not extract. This creates a long-term, sustainable way to manage forests.</li><li><strong>Indigenous Leadership at the Core:</strong> Pete highlights the vital role that indigenous knowledge plays in protecting forests. These communities have been caring for the land for generations, and empowering them is key to effective conservation.</li><li><strong>Transforming Economic Models:</strong> Pete shows how regenerative finance can provide an economic alternative that benefits both people and the planet. Instead of focusing on extraction, these models value ecosystems as living assets that need to be protected and nurtured.</li><li><strong>Moving Beyond Carbon Offsets:</strong> Carbon credits are just one part of the equation. Pete talks about the broader ecological benefits of forests, like improving biodiversity and water quality, and how we can capture and measure these impacts.</li></ul><p>🎧 <strong>Tune in to Episode 5</strong></p><ul><li><a href="https://open.spotify.com/episode/6f2on7Yvk5Ywe2iHqFzOT2?si=8k-IO2PBTbi2uWGiaTu2tQ" rel="noreferrer">Spotify</a></li><li><a href="https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/refi-podcast/id1609683147?i=1000673863714" rel="noreferrer">Apple</a></li><li><a href="https://youtu.be/GpkKQcKhMW0?si=BRgbsRPmhgswL-Sc" rel="noreferrer">YouTube</a></li></ul><p>And don’t forget! We’re hosting a<strong> live discussion on Episode 5 this Friday, Oct 25, at 11 AM ET! 🎙️</strong> Share your thoughts and dive deeper into the world of regenerative finance with us. 🌿</p><p>👉 Join the discussion on Twitter Spaces: <a href="https://twitter.com/i/spaces/1mrxmMeDmRgxy">https://twitter.com/i/spaces/1mrxmMeDmRgxy</a></p><p><strong>Thank you to everyone who has joined this journey.</strong> Please share your thoughts and feedback, and if you've found value in our efforts, consider supporting us with <a href="https://podfollow.com/refi-podcast/view" rel="noreferrer">a five-star review on your favorite podcast platform</a>. </p><p>Every bit of encouragement helps us expand our reach and deepen the impact of ReFi Podcast. You can also <a href="https://buymeacoffee.com/refipodcast" rel="noreferrer">buy us a coffee</a> or support our work directly <a href="https://giveth.io/project/refi-podcast-season-4-the-regeneration-nexus" rel="noreferrer">on Giveth</a>. <br><br>We are honored to be on this journey alongside you. 💜</p>
